jahmyr gibbs.verdict: Elite volume plus elite efficiency; only the contract hold-in and a 67% snap share cap the floor.
jahmyr gibbs.report: Back-to-back 363/367-point seasons with 21+ PPG and rising receiving usage (94 targets, 16.2% share, 1.04 rec EPA/g) puts him in the high-volume/high-efficiency quadrant — 5.0 YPC, 3.5 yards before contact behind a strong line. Ceiling is the overall RB1 if the 67% snap share climbs; floor risk is the tracked hold-in and a committee body (Pacheco) stealing early-down work. Week 17 @CHI is a plus.

bijan robinson.verdict: 78% snaps, 19.8% target share, 366 touches — the safest volume-plus-efficiency profile in the position.
bijan robinson.report: 371 points on 287 carries and 103 targets, with a 0.31 WOPR and 1.56 rec EPA/g, is a true bell-cow in the high-volume/good-efficiency quadrant; 2.3 yards after contact and 22 broken tackles say the production is earned, not scheme. Ceiling is a 400-point overall RB1 given the pass-game role keeps growing. Floor is protected by touch count even if rush EPA (-0.72) says the offense stalls. Brian Robinson only takes goal-line snaps.

christian mccaffrey.verdict: League-best 23.4% target share and 0.40 WOPR, but age 30 and a lost 2024 make the floor thinner than the price.
christian mccaffrey.report: 417 points on 129 targets and 311 carries is elite volume; the 0.40 WOPR and 2.30 rec EPA/g are receiver-grade. But 3.9 YPC, 2.3 yards before contact and -1.24 rush EPA/g are the warning flags of the high-volume/mediocre-run-efficiency quadrant, and 2024 was 48 points across a wrecked year. Ceiling is another overall RB1; floor is a mid-season breakdown. Playoff slate (@LAC, @KC, PHI) is the toughest of the top tier.

jonathan taylor.verdict: Only top-5 back with positive rush EPA; 323 carries and 83% snaps carry him despite an 11% target share.
jonathan taylor.report: He jumped from 245 to 362 points on real efficiency, not luck: +1.10 rush EPA/g, 4.9 YPC, 27 broken tackles, 99 first downs on an 83% snap share — high volume with genuinely good efficiency. Ceiling is a repeat top-3 finish if touchdowns hold. Floor is the receiving profile: 55 targets, 0.16 WOPR, -0.8 aDOT means a negative game script torpedoes a week. Giddens is a change-of-pace only, so the workload is safe.

de'von achane.verdict: Big-play efficiency plus an 18.8% target share; the receiving floor makes him a PPR anchor.
de'von achane.report: Two straight 300-point seasons with 85+ targets, 0.29 WOPR and 75% snaps — high volume, high efficiency, headlined by 5.7 YPC and a position-best 3.0 yards after contact per rush with 22 broken tackles. Ceiling is a 350-point top-3 season if the goal-line work stays his. Floor is his frame and a -0.64 rec EPA/g that hints the check-downs are low-value; Wright and Gordon exist but neither has taken touches.

james cook iii.verdict: 309 carries at 5.2 YPC in the best scoring offense, but 40 targets makes him touchdown-reliant in PPR.
james cook iii.report: No advanced sheet here, so I lean on the raw split: carries jumped 207 to 309 and PPG rose to 17.8 at 5.2 YPC — high volume with strong per-carry efficiency. Ceiling is 330 if the Buffalo goal-line scripts stay his. Floor is the 40-target receiving role, which caps PPR weeks and makes him hostage to TD variance; his points-per-touch actually fell from 1.12 to 0.88 as volume rose. Playoff slate is neutral.

jeremiyah love.verdict: Listed RB1 ahead of Allgeier and Conner as a rookie; all projection, no NFL usage data yet.
jeremiyah love.report: Zero pro data, so the case is the depth chart: he sits #1 with Allgeier, an aging Conner and Benson behind him, which implies a real early-down role from Week 1. Ceiling is a 280-300-point three-down rookie if he takes the passing work too. Floor is a genuine timeshare on a bad offense — the crowd chatter is mostly contentless hype, and the one substantive take (Arizona trailing all year) is a fair scoring-environment worry. Round 2 is paying full price for an unproven profile.

ashton jeanty.verdict: Elite workload, dreadful blocking: 1.6 yards before contact and -3.83 rush EPA/g is the volume-at-risk quadrant.
ashton jeanty.report: 339 touches and a 78% snap share on 73 targets is bell-cow usage, but 3.7 YPC, -3.83 rush EPA/g and just 1.6 yards before contact per rush say the offensive line, not the back, was the problem; 24 broken tackles and 2.1 yards after contact are the encouraging half. Ceiling is a 320-point season if the line improves at all — the receiving role is already there. Floor is another 14 PPG grind. No credible competition on the roster.

omarion hampton.verdict: Nine-game rookie sample with neutral efficiency; the touch monopoly is the whole bet at a Round 2 price.
omarion hampton.report: Only 9 games and a 63% snap share, with roughly neutral rush and rec EPA and 2.9 yards before contact — low volume, average efficiency, so the profile is unproven rather than proven bad. Ceiling is 300-plus if he holds three-down duty for 17 games; 35 targets in nine games projects to a usable PPR floor. Floor is the injury that already cost him half a season plus Vidal and Mitchell taking change-of-pace work. Wk15 SF/wk17 KC is a rough finish.

saquon barkley.verdict: Efficiency collapsed from 5.8 to 4.1 YPC with -1.51 rush EPA/g; volume alone won't hold at age 29.
saquon barkley.report: The 2024 season (355 points, 5.8 YPC) is now the outlier: 2025 was 13.7 PPG on 280 carries with -1.51 rush EPA/g and 2.5 yards before contact — high volume, poor efficiency, the quadrant where the volume gets taken away. Bigsby's arrival is exactly that threat. Ceiling is 300 if Philadelphia leans run again and the touchdowns return. Floor is a 12-PPG committee back drafted in Round 2. Only 50 targets means no PPR safety net.

derrick henry.verdict: Still 5.2 YPC with positive rush EPA, but a 55% snap share and 4.9% target share make him pure TD math.
derrick henry.report: At 32 he ran for 5.2 YPC with +0.54 rush EPA/g and 83 first downs — genuinely good efficiency — but only 55% of snaps and 21 targets all year, the low-volume/high-efficiency profile that lives entirely on goal-line scripts. Ceiling is 300 if Baltimore scores at 2024 rates. Floor is an age cliff or Justice Hill absorbing more passing downs, and PPR gives him zero cushion. Divisional playoff slate (@PIT, CLE, @CIN) is unfriendly.

chase brown.verdict: 88 targets and a 14.3% share make him a floor-first PPR back; the run efficiency is the ceiling cap.
chase brown.report: Two straight 250-plus point seasons with target volume climbing to 88 and the lowest weekly stdev (7.1) in this range — reliable, high-touch, PPR-friendly. But 4.4 YPC, -0.25 rush EPA/g and -0.61 rec EPA/g put him in the good-volume/ordinary-efficiency box, so 310 is realistic and 350 isn't. Perine and Brooks nibble at goal-line and third-down work but haven't threatened the role. Round 3 ADP is a fair discount to his rank.

kenneth walker iii.verdict: New team, new opportunity, but a 47% career-low snap share and -0.84 rush EPA/g don't support a 273 projection.
kenneth walker iii.report: 2025 was 11.3 PPG on a 47% snap share and an 8.3% target share — low volume with unremarkable efficiency (4.6 YPC, 23 broken tackles is the one bright spot). The Kansas City move is the case: no depth chart is available for the new room, so I'm inferring a lead role rather than confirming it. Ceiling is 290 if he handles three downs in a high-scoring offense. Floor is another timeshare at 11 PPG, which busts a Round 3 pick.

josh jacobs.verdict: PPG fell to 13.9 on a 59% snap share with -0.99 rush EPA/g; touchdown regression already started.
josh jacobs.report: 293 to 237 points with carries down to 234 and 4.0 YPC — the 2.1 yards before contact and -0.99 rush EPA/g say the blocking and the burst both eroded, a high-volume/poor-efficiency warning. Ceiling is 285 if Green Bay funnels goal-line work to him again. Floor is a 15-game, 13-PPG season with Lloyd and Martinez chipping in. Only 44 targets, so no PPR insulation. The Round 3 price is roughly right, not a bargain.

breece hall.verdict: Two straight declining seasons and -1.39 rush EPA/g; Braelon Allen keeps eating into a shrinking role.
breece hall.report: 12.2 PPG on a 64% snap share with the receiving role halved (76 targets to 48, 0.15 WOPR) is the wrong trend line — high-ish volume, poor rushing efficiency at 4.4 YPC and -1.39 rush EPA/g. Ceiling is 270 if the passing-game usage snaps back to 2024 levels, which is the entire bull case. Floor is a true committee with Allen and Davis at 11 PPG. Round 4 ADP finally prices the risk fairly.

javonte williams.verdict: Positive rush EPA and 25 broken tackles on a 69% snap share; the 8.6% target share caps the PPR ceiling.
javonte williams.report: Real bounce-back: 158 to 243 points, 4.8 YPC, +0.76 rush EPA/g, 2.4 yards after contact and 25 broken tackles — solid volume with above-average rushing efficiency. Ceiling is 275 if Dallas keeps feeding him 250-plus carries in a good scoring offense. Floor is the receiving collapse (51 targets, -1.42 rec EPA/g) plus Jaydon Blue taking third downs, which makes him a two-down back in a PPR league.

kyren williams.verdict: Lowest weekly variance at the position and positive EPA, but the Rams keep adding backs and targets stay scarce.
kyren williams.report: 15.5 PPG with a 5.9 stdev is the steadiest profile here, backed by 259 carries, 86 first downs and mildly positive rush and rec EPA on a 68% snap share — decent volume, adequate efficiency. Ceiling is 265; there's no receiving upside with an 8.1% target share. Floor is Corum or Hunter finally cutting into a role the team has clearly tried to replace. Chatter is generic rankings content and tells me nothing about the player.

travis etienne jr..verdict: Rebound year was real (7.7 to 14.9 PPG) but he changes teams with no depth chart confirmed; ADP too high to call sleeper.
travis etienne jr..report: He doubled his output on 260 carries at 4.3 YPC with 52 targets — decent volume, average efficiency, the rebound is credible. No advanced sheet or New Orleans depth chart is provided, so the pass-catching role ESPN's call is built on is an inference, not a confirmed fact. Ceiling is 275 if he's the clear three-down back. Floor is a split in a new scheme. No sleeper badge: at ADP 47.8 he is already priced inside the top 50.

cam skattebo.verdict: Eight-game rookie flash on 52% of snaps; the opportunity jump is real but ADP 43.6 already pays for it.
cam skattebo.report: Only 8 games at 52% snaps, yet a 12.9% target share, 0.19 WOPR and 1.02 points per touch — low volume with encouraging receiving efficiency, the classic breakout shape. But -1.51 rush EPA/g and 2.2 yards before contact behind that line temper the run projection, and Tracy and Singletary are still on the roster. Ceiling is 285 with a full 17-game bell-cow role; floor is a split plus injury recurrence. ESPN's sleeper call is sound but he's no longer cheap.

quinshon judkins.verdict: 3.6 YPC, -1.79 rush EPA/g and 51% snaps — the volume-at-risk quadrant with Sampson pushing behind him.
quinshon judkins.report: 230 carries produced only 10.0 PPG at 3.6 YPC with -1.79 rush EPA/g; the 1.4 yards before contact per rush is an offensive-line indictment and the 2.2 after contact is the one credit to him. Just 36 targets and a 51% snap share leaves no PPR cushion. Ceiling is 250 if Cleveland's line and offense improve and he holds goal-line work. Floor is a genuine committee loss to Sampson by midseason. Round 5 is the earliest I'd take him.

treveyon henderson.verdict: Rookie efficiency monster on a part-time snap share; the RB1 job is his now and the volume math is scary
treveyon henderson.report: Low volume + elite efficiency quadrant: 206 PPR points on just a 46% snap share, 5.1 ypc, 3.0 yards before contact and +0.50 rush EPA/g as a rookie. Give that back a 65%+ role and 250+ touches and he's a top-6 RB. Floor risk is real — Stevenson is still there and took 130 carries plus a 9.8% target share, so this can stay a two-man rotation. Playoff slate (@KC, @NYJ, DEN) is the one negative. ADP 67.5 is a bargain.

d'andre swift.verdict: High volume with genuinely positive rush EPA behind a strong line; boring, safe, and priced fairly
d'andre swift.report: High volume + adequate efficiency: 223 carries, 58% snaps, 73 first downs, +0.97 rush EPA/g and 3.2 yards before contact — Chicago's line is doing work, but Swift converted it to 13.4 ppg with a tame 7.1 stdev. Ceiling is capped by a -0.5 aDOT and only 48 targets; he won't win weeks through the air. Monangai's 169 carries are the floor threat if the injury tag clears. @BUF/GB/DET playoffs are unfriendly.

bucky irving.verdict: 2024's 14.4 ppg is real talent, but 2025's -3.56 rush EPA and Gainwell's 85 targets make ADP 55 the wrong price
bucky irving.report: Classic warning quadrant: still-high volume (173 carries, 62% snaps) with collapsed efficiency — 3.4 ypc, 1.8 yards before contact, -3.56 rush EPA/g, and only 10 games of tracked usage. Gainwell ate the passing down role outright (16.3% target share, 73 catches), so the receiving floor Irving had in 2024 is gone. Ceiling is a return to 14+ ppg if he's healthy and reclaims third downs; floor is a 55/45 timeshare. The field is already fading him.

rico dowdle.verdict: Back-to-back 200-point seasons at a 107 ADP; committee caps the ceiling but the price is wrong
rico dowdle.report: High volume, league-average efficiency: 236 carries, 17 games, 11.0% target share, 65 first downs, 4.6 ypc with near-zero rush and receiving EPA. That profile has produced 198 and 216 PPR points in consecutive years — the floor is the asset. Warren is a legitimate 1B (211 carries himself), so neither back gets a workhorse share, and Dowdle's ceiling needs a Warren injury. BAL/CAR/@TEN playoff run is favorable.

jaylen warren.verdict: Best per-touch efficiency in this committee — 23 broken tackles, 2.4 YAC/rush — at a 101 ADP
jaylen warren.report: Mid volume + strong efficiency: 12.8 ppg on 211 carries and 40 catches, 23 broken tackles, 2.4 yards after contact per rush and +0.67 receiving EPA/g with a -2.5 aDOT checkdown role. The depth chart lists him behind Dowdle, but the 2025 snap split (51%) says co-starter, not backup. Floor is ~11 touches in a true split; ceiling is RB1 numbers if Dowdle misses time. Friendly wk15-17 draw (BAL, CAR, @TEN).

kenny gainwell.verdict: 16.3% target share and 73 catches is WR-grade receiving volume for an RB going in round 11
kenny gainwell.report: Low rush volume + huge receiving volume: 85 targets, 16.3% target share, 0.23 WOPR, 1.18 points per touch and 221 PPR points — that is a startable PPR floor even as the nominal RB2. ESPN's call (13.3 touches, 17.8 ppg from Week 8 on) matches the tracked usage rather than contradicting it. Irving's 2025 efficiency collapse means the touch split may not revert. Sleeper: the passing-down job is already his — start taking him in round 9, a full two rounds before ADP 121.

bhayshul tuten.verdict: Clear runway as Jacksonville's RB1, but you're paying round-7 price for volume he's never held
bhayshul tuten.report: Low volume, mixed efficiency: 21% snaps, 83 carries, 3.0% target share, 3.7 ypc and -0.68 rush EPA/g, though 2.0 yards after contact and 0.95 points per touch hint at real burst behind poor blocking (1.7 YBC). The room ahead of him — Rodriguez, Allen, Abdullah — is the weakest in this group, so a 60%+ snap share is plausible and that's the 220+ point ceiling. Floor is a committee where he never fixes the per-carry inefficiency. ADP 76.6 prices the good case.

jadarian price.verdict: Rookie already listed atop Seattle's chart with a 6.0 ypc college profile; the range of outcomes is enormous
jadarian price.report: No NFL data, so the inference is depth chart plus profile: he is listed RB1 ahead of Charbonnet, and ESPN's call cites 6.0 yards per carry with 13 touchdowns. That's a low-volume, high-efficiency projection until proven otherwise. Ceiling is 240+ if Seattle gives him 15 touches a game with goal-line work; floor is a 45% snap timeshare with Charbonnet, who has been the short-yardage answer before. ADP 75.8 already reflects the hype, so he's not a bargain — just a bet.

tony pollard.verdict: Volume-driven RB2 with the lowest efficiency in the tier; the touches themselves are the risk
tony pollard.report: High volume + poor efficiency: 242 carries and a 62% snap share produced 10.9 ppg, but -1.28 rush EPA/g and -0.70 receiving EPA/g say Tennessee is losing value on those touches. The 5.5 weekly stdev and 17-game streak make him one of the safest weekly floors here. Ceiling is limited — 4.53 points per target and a 0.3 aDOT means no passing-game spike. Spears and rookie Singleton are the obvious carve-outs if the offense wants more juice.

rj harvey.verdict: 58 targets and +1.12 receiving EPA/g on a 42% snap share; the pass-game role alone pays at ADP 123
rj harvey.report: Low rush volume + split efficiency: 3.7 ypc with -1.35 rush EPA/g is bad, but 47 catches, a 10.2% target share and +1.12 receiving EPA/g gave him 207 PPR points and 1.07 points per touch as a rookie. Dobbins is the early-down starter but has missed extended time repeatedly and offers no receiving work (14 targets). Sleeper: he's one Dobbins absence from 18 touches — take him round 10 rather than waiting out ADP 123.

david montgomery.verdict: New team, 37% snaps, 5.4% target share — a touchdown-dependent grinder priced like a starter
david montgomery.report: Low volume + flat efficiency: 158 carries on a 37% snap share, 29 targets, 0.4 aDOT and -0.03 rush EPA/g with just 3 broken tackles. The 9.8 ppg was largely scoring-driven, and moving to Houston puts him next to Woody Marks, who is the better pass-catcher. Ceiling is a 15-touch, goal-line role worth low-end RB2 numbers; floor is a genuine split with almost no receiving equity. JAX/@PHI/@GB playoff slate offers no help. ADP 73.5 is the clear overpay in this group.

rhamondre stevenson.verdict: Excellent per-touch numbers behind a better back; the best pure handcuff on the board
rhamondre stevenson.report: Mid volume + good contact efficiency: 1.10 points per touch, 2.8 yards after contact per rush, 16 broken tackles, 9.8% target share and a 0.18 WOPR — the best receiving profile among these backups. But -1.31 rush EPA/g and Henderson's ascent cap the role, and the 10.0 weekly stdev shows how spiky the usage was. Ceiling is 190+ if Henderson misses time; floor is a 10-touch change-of-pace. Tough wk15-17 (@KC, @NYJ, DEN).

kyle monangai.verdict: 4.6 ypc and 3.0 YBC on 169 rookie carries; one Swift absence from an every-down role
kyle monangai.report: Low volume + solid rushing efficiency: 41% snaps, 169 carries, 4.6 ypc, 3.0 yards before contact and +0.22 rush EPA/g, but only a 5.7% target share and -0.43 receiving EPA/g cap the PPR ceiling. ESPN flags an expanding role, and 147 points as the RB2 is a real baseline. The questionable tag is a live concern to monitor. Sleeper: he's the direct backup to a 223-carry starter on a good line — round 11 is the spot, ahead of ADP 124.

jacory croskey-merritt.verdict: Listed RB1 in Washington after 175 rookie carries and 13 broken tackles, and he's free at pick 140
jacory croskey-merritt.report: Mid rush volume + no receiving work: 175 carries, 39% snaps, 13 broken tackles, 2.1 yards after contact, but a 3.0% target share and 0.04 WOPR make him touchdown-dependent in PPR (8.3 ppg, -0.38 rush EPA/g). He tops the depth chart with White and McNichols behind him, so a bump toward 15 carries plus goal-line work is the 190-point path. Sleeper: the starting job is nominally his at an RB4 price — start taking him in round 11.

j.k. dobbins.verdict: 5.0 ypc and positive rush EPA, but 14 targets and a long injury file make him a two-down TD bet
j.k. dobbins.report: Mid volume + fine rush efficiency: 153 carries, 5.0 ypc, +0.42 rush EPA/g, 2.6 yards before contact and 2.4 after — the running was good. The problem is PPR shape: 14 targets, a 4.6% target share and only 10 games of tracked snaps, with 6.8 ppg the result. Harvey owns the passing downs and would inherit everything. Ceiling is ~190 with touchdown regression in his favor; floor is another missed month.

chuba hubbard.verdict: 14.2 ppg in 2024 became 7.4 with 3.8 ypc and one broken tackle — the efficiency crash is the story
chuba hubbard.report: High-ish volume + bad efficiency, the fade quadrant: 3.8 ypc, -1.04 rush EPA/g, 2.0 yards before contact and a single broken tackle across 15 games. The 2024 season looks like the outlier now. Brooks is healthy and behind him, Etienne and Dillon exist, and Carolina drafted for competition — the volume is exactly what gets reallocated. Ceiling requires Brooks to fail again; floor is a bench back by midseason. CIN/@PIT/SEA playoffs are unhelpful.

jonathon brooks.verdict: Cleared knee, camp buzz, and the starter ahead of him just posted 3.8 ypc — a cheap lottery ticket
jonathon brooks.report: No usage data at all, so this is a depth-chart and health bet: ESPN reports he's cleared and can overtake Hubbard, whose 2025 efficiency (3.8 ypc, -1.04 rush EPA/g, 1 broken tackle) invites replacement. Crowd chatter about camp is vague hype, not a reported role change, so I'm not treating it as fact. Ceiling is a 200-point takeover; floor is a third knee setback and 40 touches. Sleeper at ADP 130 — round 11-12, and pair him with nothing.

blake corum.verdict: 5.1 ypc and 3.5 YBC on 29% of snaps; the highest-leverage handcuff in football given Kyren's workload
blake corum.report: Low volume + strong rushing efficiency: 145 carries, 5.1 ypc, 3.5 yards before contact, +0.94 rush EPA/g and 12 broken tackles — the breakout quadrant, blocked entirely by Kyren Williams. The 2.3% target share and 0.03 WOPR mean he'd be a touchdown-dependent RB2 even with the job, so don't overpay. Sleeper: he inherits a bell-cow role in an offense that funnels goal-line work to the back — round 12, and he's a top-15 RB the week Kyren sits.

rachaad white.verdict: Pass-pro praise doesn't buy targets; 8.3% share, -2.3 aDOT and a rookie ahead of him on the chart
rachaad white.report: Low volume + poor efficiency: 8.4 ppg, 4.8 yards per target, -2.3 aDOT, -0.11 receiving EPA/g and 1.5 yards after contact per rush, down from 11.7 ppg in 2024. Sanderson's third-down-back thesis is real football value but Croskey-Merritt is listed RB1 and McNichols has passing-down history, so I'm skipping the sleeper badge — the target volume isn't there to make his ceiling matter. Floor is 8 touches a week; ceiling needs a JCM injury.

aaron jones sr..verdict: 242 points to 119 in one year, 4.2 ypc, and no clear role listed — the age cliff looks live
aaron jones sr..report: No advanced usage available, so I'm inferring from raw output: 7.0 ppg on 132 carries and 28 catches, down from 14.2 ppg and 255 carries in 2024, with points per touch falling to 0.74. That's the fade quadrant — declining volume and declining efficiency together. The depth chart returns no match, which itself signals an unsettled role. Ceiling is a 12-touch veteran split if Minnesota's room stays thin; floor is waiver fodder by October. Let someone else pay pick 119.

zach charbonnet.verdict: Two straight 180-point seasons at 48% snaps; PUP is the only thing keeping him this cheap.
zach charbonnet.report: Mid-volume, league-average efficiency quadrant: 184 carries at 4.0 ypc, 2.1 YBC and 14 broken tackles, with neutral rush EPA — he doesn't create, but he holds the job. He's cleared 180 PPR points in back-to-back years without ever being the No.1, and the Seattle depth ahead of him is unproven. The PUP tag is the verifiable fact that caps the floor and must be tracked into August. Ceiling is a genuine lead role; floor is a Week 4 return to a timeshare.

tyrone tracy jr..verdict: 161 and 182 PPR points the last two years at RB155 cost — real dual-threat volume, priced like a backup.
tyrone tracy jr..report: High-volume, mediocre-efficiency profile: 176 carries plus 48 targets, 54% snaps, 10.8% target share and 53 first downs, but -0.65 rush EPA/g and only 1.7 yards after contact. The receiving usage is what makes him PPR-safe; the poor rushing efficiency is why the carries could be split. No listed competition here, so I'm inferring an open committee rather than a locked job. Take him in the 13th round or earlier as a flex.

woody marks.verdict: Real snap share and 196 carries, but the worst rush EPA in this group and Montgomery now ahead of him.
woody marks.report: Classic high-volume/poor-efficiency warning: 52% snaps and 196 carries turned into 3.6 ypc, -1.82 rush EPA/g and just 1.8 yards before contact — volume that a veteran signing can take away, and Montgomery is exactly that. The 6.8% target share and 2.1 aDOT limit the PPR safety net. Ceiling is Montgomery missing time and Marks returning to 15 touches; floor is a 8-touch change-of-pace. The 'Woody Marks SZN' clip is stale 2025 chatter. @PHI/@GB playoffs are unhelpful.

jordan mason.verdict: Best pure runner in this tier — 4.8 ypc, 2.4 YAC, 13 broken tackles — sitting behind a 31-year-old.
jordan mason.report: Low-volume, strong-efficiency quadrant: 159 carries at 4.8 ypc with 2.3 YBC and 2.4 yards after contact and 13 broken tackles, after 5.2 ypc the year before. The catch is zero pass game — 3.5% target share, -3.3 aDOT — so he's a rushing-only asset whose PPR value is entirely tied to Aaron Jones's availability. Ceiling is 200+ if Jones misses six games; floor is 7 ppg grinding. Worth a 13th-round shot; crowd chatter never actually names him.

tyjae spears.verdict: 12.3% target share and 45 catches make him the most PPR-proof back on this list at RB166 cost.
tyjae spears.report: Low rushing volume, receiving-driven: 50 targets in 13 games, 12.3% target share, 46% snaps and 0.95 points per touch — the reception floor is what matters in PPR. Rushing efficiency is poor (3.9 ypc, -0.30 EPA/g), so Pollard keeps the early downs and the ceiling needs a Pollard absence. ESPN's 149 projection is the highest in this group against an ADP of 168 — that gap is the buy signal. Games-missed risk is real; he's played 13 of 17 in usage terms.

isiah pacheco.verdict: Detroit's early-down complement to Gibbs is a valuable job; his own efficiency is the problem.
isiah pacheco.report: Low-volume, poor-efficiency quadrant: 118 carries at 3.9 ypc with -1.05 rush EPA/g and a single broken tackle, plus 1.6 yards after contact. The bull case is entirely situational — Montgomery's vacated Detroit role in a high-scoring offense with goal-line work. FantasyPros flagged him as a sleeper, but I'm withholding the badge: the per-touch data says he's replacement level and Vaki lurks. Ceiling is a 12-touch TD-dependent flex; floor is irrelevant.

justice hill.verdict: Pure passing-down back, 1.67 pts/touch, 10% target share behind a 32-year-old workhorse — cheap PPR equity.
justice hill.report: Extreme low-volume/high-efficiency profile: only 18 carries but 27 targets in 10 games, 10% target share, 37% snaps and 3.9 yards after contact per rush. He scored 127 in 2024 in the same role, so ESPN's 114 projection against a 170 ADP is defensible. Ceiling is Henry breaking down and Hill absorbing third downs plus 8 carries a game; floor is 3-4 ppg dead weight. Start considering him around round 14 in PPR only.

dylan sampson.verdict: 8.7% target share and +0.46 receiving EPA on 26% snaps — a PPR pass-down specialist behind Judkins.
dylan sampson.report: Low-volume, split-efficiency: 40 targets and 33 catches with positive receiving EPA, but a disastrous 2.7 ypc, 1.2 yards before contact and -1.12 rush EPA — he cannot run between the tackles yet. That makes him reception-dependent, which is exactly what PPR pays for at a 170 ADP. Ceiling is Judkins missing time and Sampson catching 55 balls; floor is 25% snaps and 5 ppg. Worth a final-round flier.

alvin kamara.verdict: Age-31 collapse across the board — -2.62 rush EPA, 3.6 ypc — and now behind Etienne.
alvin kamara.report: Volume fell and efficiency fell with it: 5.9 ppg on 64% snaps, 3.6 ypc, -2.62 rush EPA/g and -1.06 receiving EPA after a 265-point 2024. That's the fade quadrant. The 11.7% target share is the one thing left worth owning, and RotoWire is right that 20-30 snaps a week has PPR pulse. Etienne's arrival caps the carries entirely. Ceiling is a 45-catch flex if Etienne misses time; floor is a mid-season roster cut.

tyler allgeier.verdict: Durable 143-carry grinder, but 3.6 ypc behind a first-round rookie caps everything.
tyler allgeier.report: Moderate-volume, weak-efficiency: 143 carries at 3.6 ypc with -0.68 rush EPA/g and 2.0 yards before contact, 30% snaps, and essentially no pass game (3.2% target share). He's played 17 games two years running, which is the appeal. New team, and he's sandwiched between rookie Love and Conner, so the touch count could go either way. Ceiling is a Love injury and 15 carries a week; floor is short-yardage only.

tank bigsby.verdict: Elite contact metrics — 3.0 YBC, 2.7 YAC, 5.7 ypc — trapped behind the league's most durable workhorse.
tank bigsby.report: Textbook low-volume/high-efficiency: 63 carries at 5.7 ypc with +0.48 rush EPA and 10 broken tackles on 13% snaps. He ran for 129 points in 2024 when given 168 carries, so the talent-to-opportunity gap is real. But Barkley is a true workhorse and Bigsby offers nothing receiving (1.2% target share), so the standalone floor is near zero. This is a pure Barkley handcuff purchase, not a flex.

chris rodriguez jr..verdict: Positive rush EPA on 112 carries in an unsettled Jacksonville backfield — cheap early-down lottery ticket.
chris rodriguez jr..report: Low-volume, decent-efficiency runner: 112 carries at 4.5 ypc with +0.52 rush EPA/g and 33 first downs, and he's one of the few backs here with positive rushing EPA. The problem is a 1.3% target share — four targets all year — which caps PPR upside hard. No depth chart data available, so I'm inferring an open committee in Jacksonville with Etienne gone. Ceiling is a 12-carry early-down role; floor is inactive.

jordan james.verdict: 2% career snap share, but he's the name behind a McCaffrey who has never stayed healthy two years running.
jordan james.report: No usable usage data — 3 games, 2% snaps — so this is entirely a bet on the depth chart, not on demonstrated efficiency. The San Francisco RB2 job is one of the most valuable lottery tickets in fantasy given CMC's history, but Guerendo and McCormick are still on the roster and James carries his own Questionable tag. Ceiling is 150+ if he wins the backup job and CMC misses six weeks; floor is zero.

braelon allen.verdict: Lost 2025 to injury after a functional 2024; pure Breece Hall insurance with no standalone role.
braelon allen.report: Four games, 23% snaps, -2.17 rush EPA and zero broken tackles in a tiny 2025 sample — that's the fade quadrant on the data we have, though the sample is small enough that 2024 (92 carries, 27 targets) is the better guide. Hall's presence means no weekly role, and Isaiah Davis is a live competitor for the backup snaps. Ceiling requires a Hall absence; floor is a bench stash you cut in Week 3.

brian robinson jr..verdict: Snap share fell off a cliff to 17% and points fell from 160 to 63 — the arrow is straight down.
brian robinson jr..report: Low-volume with only mediocre efficiency to show: 92 carries at 4.3 ypc on a 17% snap share, and 2.6 yards before contact is the one flattering number. The 2024 line (187 carries, 160 points) is now two systems stale. FantasyPros calls him a volume-dependent early-down sleeper, but nothing in the usage suggests the volume is coming back with Bijan entrenched. Ceiling is short-yardage TD vulture; floor is waiver fodder.

keaton mitchell.verdict: 5.8 ypc and 3.6 yards before contact says explosive; 17% snaps and Hampton ahead says irrelevant.
keaton mitchell.report: Low-volume, high-efficiency burner: 59 carries at 5.8 ypc, +0.20 rush EPA and 3.6 YBC, but only 18 first downs and a 4.2% target share on 17% snaps. That efficiency is partly scheme and partly small-sample explosiveness. New team, and Hampton is a bell-cow with Vidal also in the mix, so the path to touches is narrow. Ceiling is a big-play flex if Hampton misses time; floor is a special-teams body.

jonah coleman.verdict: Rookie RB3 in Denver, but Payton's backs catch passes and Dobbins has never finished a season.
jonah coleman.report: No NFL data at all, so this is a projection call: Joel Smyth and FantasyPros both cite three-down potential in a system that funnels receptions to backs, and the opening is Dobbins's injury history plus Harvey's unproven hold on the job. ESPN's 41-point projection and 188 overall rank price him as a nobody. Ceiling is a mid-season pass-down role worth flex points; floor is inactive. Last-round-only dart, round 15+.

mike washington jr..verdict: Rookie with no data and no depth-chart clarity in a backfield with an established lead back.
mike washington jr..report: Nothing to interpret — no 2025 or 2024 usage, no snap share, no listed depth chart, so I'm inferring from ESPN's 65-point projection that they see him as a backup rather than a committee piece. He is a pure name-recognition dart in a Las Vegas backfield that already has a workhorse. Ceiling requires an injury ahead of him plus a role win over the rest of the room; floor is a healthy scratch. Bye week 13 also hurts the playoff run-in.

ray davis.verdict: Fourth on the Buffalo depth chart with a 14% snap share — the projection of 38 points is honest.
ray davis.report: Low-volume with only ordinary efficiency: 58 carries, 13 targets, 14% snaps, 2.8% target share and just 22 first downs across a full season, and the 2024 line (116 points) came from a role he no longer has. Cook is a workhorse and both Ty Johnson and Gore sit ahead of Davis now, so there is no realistic path without two injuries. Ceiling is a couple of usable weeks; floor is never starting a fantasy lineup.

james conner.verdict: ESPN projects him for zero — age 31, RB3, Questionable, and three games of usage last year.
james conner.report: The 2024 season (254 points, 236 carries) is the ghost being drafted here; the 2025 reality was three games, 1.2 yards before contact and -0.93 rush EPA before he disappeared. He is now behind rookie Love and Allgeier and carries a Questionable tag. RotoWire's trade-candidate angle is the only path to relevance, and it depends on an event that may not happen. Fade at this price; there are healthier darts with the same cost.

kaelon black.verdict: Rookie RB3 in SF; only a CMC injury unlocks him, and Jordan James is ahead in that line.
kaelon black.report: No NFL usage to grade, so I'm inferring from depth chart alone: he's third behind McCaffrey and Jordan James. That's the low-volume/unknown-efficiency quadrant — a pure dart throw. Ceiling is real only if CMC misses time AND James disappoints, since Shanahan backfields print points. Floor is inactive most weeks. Playoff slate (@LAC, @KC, PHI) is among the harshest here.

kaytron allen.verdict: Fourth on a four-deep Washington chart; no data, no clear path, lowest projection in the group.
kaytron allen.report: No collegiate-to-NFL usage to interpret, and the depth chart is the whole story: Croskey-Merritt, Rachaad White and McNichols all sit ahead. That's low volume with no efficiency evidence to argue from — the fade quadrant until camp says otherwise. Ceiling requires two injuries plus a coaching preference we have no signal for. ESPN's 16-point projection is the honest read; leave him on waivers.

nicholas singleton.verdict: Best rookie path in this tier: Pollard is a lease, not a deed, and Spears has never held a job.
nicholas singleton.report: No pro data, so this is an opportunity bet: Pollard is a volume-over-efficiency veteran and Spears has never stayed healthy or held early-down work, which makes Singleton the likeliest man standing by midseason. Unknown efficiency, but the draft capital and the two-man competition ahead is thinner than most rookies here face. Floor is a rotational 6-8 touch role; ceiling is a lead back on a run-first Titans team.

demond claiborne.verdict: Third in Minnesota now, but Aaron Jones is on borrowed time and Mason is a two-down thumper.
demond claiborne.report: No NFL sample; the case is structural. Jones is aging and Mason profiles as an early-down grinder, leaving passing-down and change-of-pace work genuinely available for a rookie with receiving chops. Low volume today, unknown efficiency — the quadrant where opportunity, not talent, decides the outcome. Floor is a zero-snap redshirt; ceiling is a 1B role in a competent offense. Week 15 at Detroit hurts the playoff slate.

kimani vidal.verdict: Already proved he can carry 155 times and score 8.4 PPG; Hampton's health is all that blocks him.
kimani vidal.report: 2025 was the proof of concept: 54% snap share over 13 games, 155 carries, 118 points at 8.4 PPG. That's the high-volume/mediocre-efficiency quadrant (4.1 YPC, -1.08 rush EPA/g), which means the volume is only his when Hampton is out — but he demonstrably survives it. Floor is a 15-touch-a-month backup; ceiling is a top-25 RB stretch. Sleeper: best proven bulk-carry insurance available after pick 150 — take him round 13-14.

jaylen wright.verdict: Direct handcuff to an undersized workhorse, but two years of poor efficiency say the job may not stick.
jaylen wright.report: Two seasons, 138 carries, 4.1 and 3.7 YPC with -0.63 rush EPA/g and a 22% snap share — low volume paired with poor efficiency, the fade quadrant. What saves him is the depth chart: Achane's frame and touch load make a Wright spike week plausible, and Ollie Gordon isn't a real threat. Floor is 2-3 PPG mop-up; ceiling assumes 15 touches a week he hasn't earned. Miami's @GB/LAC/BUF playoff run is unfriendly.

ollie gordon ii.verdict: 2.8 YPC on 70 carries with a 1.8% target share — volume he had, efficiency he didn't.
ollie gordon ii.report: His rookie line is a warning: 70 carries at 2.8 YPC, -0.56 rush EPA/g, 1.8% target share and 54 total points across 17 games. That is the low-volume/poor-efficiency quadrant and the reason he sits behind Achane and Wright rather than pushing them. Floor is inactive; ceiling is short-yardage vulture work if injuries strike, which is TD-dependent noise. Tough Miami playoff draw. Not a roster spot in 12-team leagues.

adam randall.verdict: Rookie parked behind an aging Henry and a passing-down specialist; the path exists but runs through 2027.
adam randall.report: No pro data to weigh, so the depth chart carries it: Derrick Henry's age makes Baltimore's early-down role a live succession question, but Justice Hill owns the receiving snaps and would soak up PPR value first. Unknown efficiency plus RB3 volume is a dart throw. Floor is inactive; ceiling is inheriting goal-line work in a high-scoring offense, which is a TD-dependent ceiling. Late Week 13 bye is a minor plus.

samaje perine.verdict: Highest ESPN projection in this group (101) on a stable passing-down role behind Chase Brown.
samaje perine.report: Two straight seasons of 78-81 points on modest touches, with a 35% snap share, 4.1% target share and 4.5 YPC in 2025 — low-volume/solid-efficiency work in a pass-heavy Cincinnati offense. That combination is the safest floor here: he plays every week and catches passes, which PPR rewards. Ceiling is capped by age 30+ and Chase Brown's grip on the job. Playoff slate (@CAR, @IND, BAL) is workable.

lequint allen jr..verdict: Receiving-back profile with 10 catches and 25 points as a rookie — role, not production, is the bet.
lequint allen jr..report: His rookie line is thin: 11 targets, 23 carries, 25 points, -0.24 rec EPA/g and a 2.1% target share across 16 games. Low volume, mediocre efficiency, no evidence of a coming role. The Jacksonville depth chart isn't listed here, so I'm inferring from usage alone, and usage says third-down specialist at best. Floor is a healthy scratch; ceiling needs an injury to the starter to reach flex relevance. Pass at cost.

marshawn lloyd.verdict: Never played, but Brooks is on PUP and Lloyd is the only explosive back behind Jacobs' huge workload.
marshawn lloyd.report: No usable data — two lost seasons — so this is an opportunity and draft-capital bet. Brooks starting on PUP effectively moves Lloyd to RB2 behind a Josh Jacobs workload that has been punishing for years, and ESPN's 65-point projection is the second-highest here despite zero production. Floor is another injury-wrecked redshirt. Sleeper: the clearest handcuff-to-a-bellcow opening in the group; start taking him round 14.

jaydon blue.verdict: 3.4 YPC, -1.50 rush EPA/g and RB3 behind Javonte — the numbers argue against the athletic hype.
jaydon blue.report: Five games of real snaps produced 38 carries at 3.4 YPC with -1.50 rush EPA/g and only 1.2 yards after contact — low volume, genuinely poor efficiency, the fade quadrant. He also caught one pass all year, which kills the PPR angle. He's third behind Javonte Williams and Malik Davis, so the touches aren't coming without two breaks. Floor is inactive; ceiling is a couple of spike weeks. Not worth a bench spot.

george holani.verdict: 6% snap share, 3.3 YPC, RB4 on a muddled chart — no volume, no efficiency, no path.
george holani.report: Fifteen points across 17 games on a 6% snap share, 3.3 YPC and -0.93 rush EPA/g: the low-volume, poor-efficiency fade quadrant with nothing to project forward. The listed Seattle depth ordering looks unsettled, but he's fourth in any version of it, which is the operative fact. Floor is zero; even the ceiling requires multiple injuries just to reach committee work. Undraftable in 12-team formats.

ty johnson.verdict: Two straight 90+ point seasons with positive rec AND rush EPA — the safest floor at this ADP.
ty johnson.report: 100 points in 2025 and 92 in 2024 with a 6.8% target share, 30% snap share, +0.67 rec EPA/g and +0.16 rush EPA/g. That is textbook low-volume/high-efficiency: he does real damage on 4-5 touches, and Buffalo trusts him on passing downs behind Cook. Floor is the highest in this group because the role is stable and he played all 17. Ceiling needs a Cook absence. Sleeper at pick 170 — take him round 13 in PPR.

emari demercado.verdict: 7.1 YPC and 4.4 yards before contact on tiny volume; now insurance for an injury-prone Walker.
emari demercado.report: Back-to-back 55-58 point seasons on a 23% snap share with 7.1 YPC and 4.4 yards before contact per rush — a small sample, but squarely the low-volume/strong-efficiency breakout quadrant. New team matters: he steps in behind Kenneth Walker, whose availability has never been reliable, with only rookies behind him. Floor is 3 PPG change-of-pace work; ceiling is a lead role in a scoring offense. Week 5 bye is early and easy to absorb.

isaiah davis.verdict: 5.5 YPC, +0.29 rec EPA/g and a 6.3% target share — efficient, but buried behind Hall and Allen.
isaiah davis.report: 71 points on a 28% snap share with 5.5 YPC, 3.0 yards before contact and a positive receiving EPA is a genuine low-volume/high-efficiency profile, and he's improved his target share two years running. The problem is pure blockage: Breece Hall and Braelon Allen both sit ahead. Floor is spot duty; ceiling is a three-down role if Hall misses time, which the Jets' usage history makes plausible. Fine last-pick stash.

emmett johnson.verdict: Rookie third in line in KC with Demercado — and Walker — in front; projection outpaces the path.
emmett johnson.report: No NFL data, so the depth chart decides it: Kenneth Walker takes the early-down work and Demercado has already shown efficiency in the complementary role. Unknown efficiency plus RB3 volume is the dart-throw quadrant. Floor is a redshirt year; ceiling requires the two men ahead to both fail or get hurt, at which point the offense is good enough to produce. ESPN's 46-point projection is generous relative to the opportunity.

chris brooks.verdict: On PUP with declining efficiency; Lloyd has already passed him for the Jacobs handcuff role.
chris brooks.report: 2025 was worse than 2024 across the board — 1.9 PPG, 3.9 YPC, -0.29 rush EPA/g, 1 broken tackle on 27 carries — low volume with fading efficiency. Now he opens camp on PUP, which is a verifiable fact that outweighs any depth-chart listing and effectively hands the backup job to MarShawn Lloyd. Floor is a roster cut; ceiling is short-yardage work if he's healthy by October. No draft-day interest.

sean tucker.verdict: 86 carries and 91 points, but 3.7 YPC on a 16% snap share and now third behind Irving and Gainwell.
sean tucker.report: He got real volume in 2025 — 86 carries, 91 points — yet produced only 3.7 YPC with -0.22 rush EPA/g and 1.0 yards after contact, and his 8.0 weekly stdev says the points came in injury-driven bursts. That's the volume-at-risk quadrant, and Tampa added Gainwell ahead of him. Floor is 15-20 touches all season; ceiling is another two-week fill-in run. Only worth it in deep leagues as an Irving contingency.

dj giddens.verdict: Clear RB2 behind the league's heaviest workload back — the single best leverage bet at this ADP.
dj giddens.report: Only 5 games of real snaps and a 12% share, so efficiency is unproven (1.8 yards before/after contact, neutral rush EPA) — I'm buying structure, not production. He is unambiguously second behind Jonathan Taylor with only Seth McGowan behind him, meaning a Taylor absence hands him a bellcow role in a run-first offense. Floor is 25 points of mop-up. Sleeper: take him round 14 as the highest-equity handcuff on the board.

devin singletary.verdict: Two straight 17-game, ~100-point seasons on real carries; safest bench body here even as Giants RB3.
devin singletary.report: Back-to-back 17-game seasons of 97-109 PPR points on 113-119 carries is genuine volume, but 3.7 ypc, -0.16 rush EPA and 1.8 yards before contact place him in the high-volume/poor-efficiency warning quadrant. Now RB3 behind Skattebo and Tracy, so that 28% snap share should shrink, not grow. Ceiling needs an injury ahead of him; floor is inactive. Bye-week cover, not a stash.

malik davis.verdict: Direct backup to an injury-prone Javonte Williams; the depth chart, not the tape, is the entire case.
malik davis.report: Held a 21% snap share as Dallas' RB2 on 52 carries, but the profile is low volume with unremarkable efficiency: 4.8 ypc built on 3.0 yards before contact, only 1.8 after, zero broken tackles. That's blocking, not creation. Value is purely positional — he's next in line behind Javonte Williams with only Blue and Mafah pushing. Floor is 20 touches and irrelevance; ceiling is a lead role for six weeks.

jawhar jordan.verdict: 8 broken tackles in 4 games at 30% snaps — the most explosive per-touch profile in this entire group.
jawhar jordan.report: Tiny sample, loud signal: 4 games, 30% snap share, 43 carries, 8 broken tackles and 2.1 yards after contact — low volume with elite tackle-breaking, the classic breakout quadrant (rush EPA -2.25 is noise over 43 rushes). Montgomery is aging and only Woody Marks stands between him and change-of-pace work. Sleeper: take him with a final-round flier (round 15+); the opening is Montgomery's early-down decline.

emanuel wilson.verdict: Proven 31%-snap volume, but the efficiency never justified it and Seattle buried him at RB3.
emanuel wilson.report: Two straight seasons near 95 points on 103-125 carries with a 31% snap share is real work, yet 4.0 ypc, -0.45 rush EPA and 1.8 yards before contact define the high-volume/poor-efficiency warning quadrant — exactly the volume that gets reassigned. In Seattle he's RB3 behind Jadarian Price and Charbonnet, so the touches are already gone. Seven broken tackles hint at competence, not takeover.

bam knight.verdict: 93 points and 31 targets says usable dual-role back; no confirmed roster spot says lottery ticket.
bam knight.report: Produced 93 PPR points across 12 active games with a 6.3% target share, 31 targets, WOPR 0.10 and 31 first downs — that's a functional passing-down profile. The rushing side undercuts it badly: 3.3 ypc and -1.37 rush EPA per game, so the low volume/mixed efficiency read is receiver-first. With no confirmed Arizona depth slot listed, his job security is the real unknown. Last-pick flier.

kendre miller.verdict: 7 broken tackles on 47 carries is real creation; Etienne and Kamara are the only thing in the way.
kendre miller.report: Miller sits in the low-volume/strong-creation quadrant: 47 carries but 7 broken tackles and 2.6 yards after contact, meaning he generates yards the blocking doesn't (1.5 before contact). The blockers are Travis Etienne and an aging Kamara, plus his own availability — 24% snaps over just 7 games. Sleeper at the very end of drafts (round 16) if Kamara's workload finally collapses; injury risk keeps the floor near zero.

isaac guerendo.verdict: 2024 efficiency was excellent, but PUP plus RB5 behind CMC is a verifiable fact that overrides it.
isaac guerendo.report: The 2024 line is the breakout quadrant: 5.0 ypc, 0.95 points per touch and 9.5 yards per target on 84 carries — high efficiency waiting on volume. Then 2025 vanished (0% snaps over 14 games) and he opens on PUP behind McCaffrey, Jordan James and Kaelon Black. The PUP tag is confirmed and beats the old tape. Tough playoff slate (@LAC, @KC, PHI) if he ever mattered. Monitor in August, don't spend a pick.

brashard smith.verdict: 6.6% target share as a rookie gives him a PPR pulse; the rushing numbers say he'll never see early downs.
brashard smith.report: The receiving usage is legitimate for a rookie — 35 targets, 25 catches, 6.6% target share, WOPR 0.08 on just 17% snaps — and it produced 63 points. The rushing side is the fade half: 3.4 ypc, -0.57 rush EPA, 1.3 yards after contact, zero broken tackles. Low volume with receiving-only efficiency means he can't take work from Kenneth Walker. PPR-only depth with a defined but small role.

tyler badie.verdict: Pure third-down specialist with 31 targets and 8 carries; useful role, no path to a real workload.
tyler badie.report: Badie's entire value is receiving: 31 targets, 19 catches, a 5.3% target share and 1.31 points per touch, against just 8 carries. That's low volume with acceptable efficiency, but the role caps him near 2 ppg. Denver stacks Dobbins, RJ Harvey and Jonah Coleman ahead, so even the pass-down job can be reassigned. He only matters in deep PPR if two backs ahead miss time.

trevor etienne.verdict: Quietly fine per-carry marks on 20 rushes, but zero receiving role and three backs ahead in Carolina.
trevor etienne.report: Small sample, decent signs: 4.7 ypc with 2.4 before and 2.3 after contact on 20 carries at a 6% snap share — low volume with tolerable efficiency. The problem is a 0.6% target share, which caps PPR upside even if the run work comes. Hubbard is entrenched, Jonathon Brooks is returning and Dillon adds short-yardage competition. A Brooks setback is the realistic path to change-of-pace touches.

kaleb johnson.verdict: A 2025 pick who never got off the ground, then watched Pittsburgh add Dowdle above Warren.
kaleb johnson.report: Year one was the fade quadrant outright: 9% snaps over 10 games, 1.3 yards before contact, 1.2 after, rush EPA -0.77 and two first downs. Nothing in the usage suggests the staff trusts him. Pittsburgh's addition of Rico Dowdle on top of Jaylen Warren pushes him to RB4, so even the injury path runs through two players. Draft capital is the last argument, and it expires with a second lost season.

will shipley.verdict: 34 points over two seasons at 12% snaps behind four backs — no volume, no efficiency, no path.
will shipley.report: Two full seasons produced 34 combined PPR points on 44 carries and 13 catches, with negative rushing and receiving EPA and zero broken tackles — the low-volume/poor-efficiency fade quadrant. Philadelphia then stacked the room with Barkley, Bigsby, Mitchell and Pierce, leaving him RB5. Even a Barkley absence funnels work to Bigsby first. The SEA/HOU/@SF playoff slate is academic; he isn't rosterable.

tahj brooks.verdict: 5% snaps and one first down as a rookie behind a workhorse; needs two injuries to matter.
tahj brooks.report: His rookie year gave nothing to project forward: 5% snap share, a 0.5% target share, one first down, -0.34 rush EPA and 1.6 yards before contact. That's low volume and poor efficiency together. Chase Brown handles the early-down workload and Perine still owns passing downs, so Brooks is the third body in a room that rarely needs one. Deep-dynasty watchlist rather than a redraft pick.

seth mcgowan.verdict: Rookie with no data stuck behind a genuine workhorse in Jonathan Taylor plus Giddens.
seth mcgowan.report: There is no NFL usage or efficiency data at all, so the inference has to come from the depth chart, and it's unforgiving: Jonathan Taylor is a true bell-cow and DJ Giddens already owns the change-of-pace role. McGowan would need a Taylor injury and to beat Giddens, two independent long shots. Any ceiling case is pure speculation on athletic profile, not opportunity. Undraftable in 12-team redraft.

rasheen ali.verdict: 0.4 yards after contact and 18 total touches — the profile of a backup who isn't creating anything.
rasheen ali.report: Ali logged 11 targets and 7 carries across 15 games at a 13% snap share, and the split is damning: 3.0 yards before contact but only 0.4 after, with zero broken tackles. Low volume paired with no creation is the fade quadrant. He's fourth in Baltimore behind Derrick Henry, Justice Hill and Adam Randall, with Hill locked into passing downs. No realistic route to standalone value.

kene nwangwu.verdict: Special-teams returner at 4% offensive snaps; fifth in line in a Jets room that already has three backs.
kene nwangwu.report: The offensive profile barely exists: 4% snap share, a 0.5% target share, a -6.0 aDOT and two first downs on the year. That's no volume and no efficiency signal to evaluate. Breece Hall, Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis all sit ahead, so even a top-of-chart injury leaves him third for touches. Kick-return scoring in return-scoring formats is the only realistic use case.

dylan laube.verdict: 3% snaps and 0.4 yards before contact per rush behind a true workhorse in Ashton Jeanty.
dylan laube.report: Laube's sample is negligible and what exists is bad: 3% snap share over 17 games, one first down, a 0.8% target share, 0.4 yards before contact and 0.9 after. Fade quadrant on both axes. Ashton Jeanty is an every-down back in Las Vegas, and Mike Washington sits above Laube for the leftovers. There's no volume to inherit even in an injury scenario worth planning for.

jacob saylors.verdict: 1% snap share and one first down across 16 games in a backfield led by Gibbs with Pacheco added.
jacob saylors.report: Effectively zero offensive role: 1% snaps over 16 games, one first down, rush EPA -0.10 on a handful of carries. The 2.5 before and 3.0 after contact are noise at that sample size, not evidence. Detroit runs Jahmyr Gibbs with Isiah Pacheco added and Sione Vaki ahead of him on the chart, so he's fourth for scraps. No volume, no measurable efficiency, no draftable path.

deejay dallas.verdict: Six-year special-teamer sixth on Jacksonville's chart; his best season was 12 total touches.
deejay dallas.report: Dallas played six games at a 6% snap share with one first down, and his 2024 line — 3 targets, 9 carries, 21 points — was already a coverage-unit profile rather than an offensive one. No volume and no usable efficiency read. He sits sixth in Jacksonville behind Bhayshul Tuten, Chris Rodriguez, J'Mari Taylor and LeQuint Allen. There is no injury sequence that reaches him.

josh williams.verdict: Two games, 4% snaps, zero first downs — the zero projection is an honest one.
josh williams.report: There is no usable sample: two appearances, a 4% snap share over three games, zero first downs and rush EPA -0.93. Fade quadrant by default, since neither volume nor efficiency exists to argue with. Tampa Bay runs Bucky Irving with Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker layered above him, so even a lead-back injury leaves him third. Nothing here changes without multiple roster moves.

kyle juszczyk.verdict: Best of a group of fullbacks: 46% snaps and a real 5.5% target share, but 3.4 PPG is bench filler.
kyle juszczyk.report: Low-volume, decent-efficiency quadrant: 28 targets, 5.5% target share, 0.10 WOPR and 2.04 pts/tgt — real receiving role, no rushing value (-1.5 yds before contact/rush). Two straight 3.4 PPG seasons with tiny stdev means the floor and ceiling are nearly the same number. Ceiling needs a spike TD run in a strong SF offense; floor is weekly zeroes. Age/13 years experience and a brutal wk15-17 slate (@LAC, @KC, PHI) cap any late upside. Not draftable in 12-team PPR.

hunter luepke.verdict: Dual-role FB with the best efficiency of the group, but 21% snaps and RB6 depth cap it at zero.
hunter luepke.report: Low volume, respectable efficiency: 15 targets and 16 carries, 4.4 YPC with 2.8 yards after contact and 2.47 pts/tgt — he does something with touches. Trend is upward (1.6 to 2.2 PPG), but a 3.3% target share and 0.05 WOPR is not a fantasy role. Ceiling is a short-yardage TD package if the Dallas backfield thins ahead of him; floor is inactive weeks. Wk16 JAX and wk17 NYG are soft, which matters only in the deepest of leagues.

alec ingold.verdict: Snap share fell and production halved in 2025; a blocking fullback with no target trend to bet on.
alec ingold.report: Low volume, poor efficiency — the fade quadrant: 11 targets, 1.28 pts/tgt, 4.7 yds/tgt and -0.04 receiving EPA/game, down from 2024's 2.19 pts/tgt. Only 9 games of advanced tracking and 37% snaps signals a shrinking role. Ceiling is a return to the 26-point 2024 line if LAC leans on play-action checkdowns; floor is single digits. Playoff slate (SF, @MIA, KC) is no help. Undraftable outside 20-team best-ball.

adam prentice.verdict: 19% snaps, 8 targets, 10 carries — a blocker with a projection of 10 points for a reason.
adam prentice.report: Bottom quadrant: negligible volume (1.7% target share, 0.03 WOPR) and neutral-to-negative efficiency (-0.05 rush EPA/game, 0.98 pts/touch). The 3.0 yards before contact/rush is scheme, not talent — only 1.4 after contact. Ceiling is a couple of goal-line vulture scores in a Denver offense that scripts well; floor is literal zero fantasy relevance. RB6 on the depth chart with no injury path to volume. Do not draft.

connor heyward.verdict: 27 points on 9% snaps is TD noise, not a signal; 0.9% target share is the actual role.
connor heyward.report: Low volume, misleadingly hot efficiency: 6.85 pts/tgt on four targets is pure touchdown variance, and 2.9 YPC on 15 carries with 0.7 yards after contact undercuts the 0.61 rush EPA/game. He is listed behind a TE room fronted by Brock Bowers, so receiving work is spoken for. Ceiling is 30 points on gadget/goal-line usage; floor is a healthy scratch. New team, tiny snap share, no path — pass entirely.

michael burton.verdict: No 2025 data, 11 years of experience, RB4 in Cleveland — a projection floor, not a player to roster.
michael burton.report: With 2025 missing entirely I'm inferring from 2024: 10 targets, 7 carries, 1.1 YPC, 29 points — low volume with poor rushing efficiency, the fade quadrant. The 2.93 pts/tgt is TD-driven on a ten-target sample, not repeatable. Ceiling is a Cleveland short-yardage role worth 25-30 points; floor is not making the roster given the missed season and RB4 depth. Playoff weeks (@NYG, @BAL, IND) are irrelevant here. Undraftable.

puka nacua.verdict: 22.1 PPG on a 30% target share with elite YAC — high volume plus high efficiency, the safest WR1 profile.
puka nacua.report: Nacua nearly doubled his 2024 output (12.2 to 22.1 PPG) while holding a 30.1% target share, 0.69 WOPR and 7.1 yards after contact per rush — high-volume, high-efficiency quadrant. Ceiling is the overall WR1 if the 68% snap share (injury-suppressed weeks) climbs back toward 85%. Floor is the 11.1 weekly stdev and the games he has missed each year. Adams still commands 25% of targets, but Nacua is unquestionably the alpha.

ja'marr chase.verdict: League-best 32% target share and 0.74 WOPR; 2025 dip was QB-driven efficiency, not lost opportunity.
ja'marr chase.report: Volume is untouchable: 185 targets, 32.1% share, 36.6% air yards, 94% snaps. The drop from 23.7 to 18.4 PPG came entirely from efficiency (2.30 to 1.70 pts/target, rec EPA 2.59 vs prior elite), which reads as quarterback play rather than decline. Ceiling is the 2024 400-point season if Burrow is whole; floor is another 18 PPG year, still a top-8 WR. Higgins caps nothing at this share.

jaxon smith-njigba.verdict: 0.90 WOPR and 50% air-yards share with a 7.3 weekly stdev — the most bankable target monopoly in football.
jaxon smith-njigba.report: JSN posted a 36.8% target share and a 50.4% air-yards share, a 0.90 WOPR that no other WR here approaches, and did it in all 17 games with the lowest weekly variance in the group. High volume plus rising efficiency (1.85 to 2.21 pts/target, aDOT up to 11.2) is the expensive, safe quadrant. Kupp and Shaheed have not dented the share. Ceiling is overall WR1; floor is ~17 PPG, which still returns the pick.

amon-ra st. brown.verdict: Five straight healthy seasons, 31.7% share, 85% snaps — the floor play of the first round.
amon-ra st. brown.report: St. Brown has now played 17 games in back-to-back years with a 31.7% target share, 0.75 WOPR and 172 targets; the efficiency dip (2.24 to 1.88 pts/target) came alongside 31 more looks, the normal volume-for-efficiency trade. High volume, solid efficiency. Ceiling is a 20+ PPG slot-alpha season if red-zone scoring normalizes; floor is ~18 PPG. Jameson Williams takes air yards but not slot targets. Week 15 at MIN is the only rough playoff draw.

ceedee lamb.verdict: Missed time and lost real share to Pickens — 25.1% target share is the lowest of his prime years.
ceedee lamb.report: The 2025 line is a genuine warning: 13 games, 11.8 PPG, target share down to 25.1% and WOPR 0.61 while Pickens out-produced him at 17.2 PPG. Efficiency held (9.2 yds/target, aDOT 12.0), so this is a volume story, not a talent one. Ceiling is a reclaimed 30% share and 18+ PPG in a pass-heavy Dallas offense; floor is another split-target 12 PPG season. Late Week 14 bye, and Week 15 at LAR is tough.

justin jefferson.verdict: 30.7% share and 0.74 WOPR with -0.81 rec EPA/game: opportunity intact, quarterback play destroyed the output.
justin jefferson.report: Jefferson played all 17 games and kept a 30.7% target share, 40.1% air-yards share and 94% snaps, yet fell to 11.9 PPG on 1.43 points per target with negative receiving EPA — the textbook high-volume/poor-efficiency quadrant, and the cause was under center, not on the field. That makes him a buy at ADP 11.9 rather than a fade. Ceiling is the 2024 18.7 PPG line; floor is a repeat if Minnesota's passing game stays broken.

drake london.verdict: 29.7% share and 91% snaps in 12 games; per-game rate is WR1, availability is the whole question.
drake london.report: London's rate stats held up (29.7% target share, 40.2% air-yards share, 0.73 WOPR, 91% snaps) but he only got on the field for 12 games and the 12.0 weekly stdev is the highest here — a boom-bust, TD-leveraged profile. Ceiling is the 2024 16.5 PPG season across 17 games. Floor is another missed month. Branch and Dotson are non-threats to his target monopoly; the offense's overall passing volume is the real cap.

rashee rice.verdict: 29% target share in his eight games; a full season at that rate is a top-12 WR at a discount to that price.
rashee rice.report: Rice was only available eight games but commanded a 29.0% target share and 75% snaps when active. The profile is short-area (aDOT 4.3, just 13.7% of air yards), which caps yardage upside but is very PPR-friendly and reception-stable. Moderate volume, good efficiency (1.92 pts/target). Ceiling is 130+ targets in a Mahomes offense; floor is another interrupted year — the 10.7 stdev on 8.8 PPG says the weekly range is wide. Worthy is the one real competitor.

nico collins.verdict: Best yards-per-target efficiency in the tier on a modest 24% share; needs volume, not talent.
nico collins.report: Collins is the low-volume/high-efficiency quadrant: 24.2% target share and 0.61 WOPR, but 9.3 yards per target, aDOT 12.7 and 3.10 points per touch. He has missed two-plus games in each of the last two seasons. Ceiling is 140 targets and 17 PPG if Higgins and Noel do not siphon looks; floor is 13 PPG and another absence. Houston's crowded young WR room is the honest risk. Week 16 at PHI and Week 17 at GB are unfriendly playoff spots.

garrett wilson.verdict: 0.92 WOPR and 56% of air yards in seven games — monopoly volume trapped in a broken offense.
garrett wilson.report: When healthy Wilson owned everything: 35.4% target share, 56.3% air-yards share, 87% snaps. But 6.7 yards per target and -0.30 receiving EPA per game put him squarely in high-volume/poor-efficiency, which is a quarterback indictment. At ADP 35 you are paying for the volume and getting the efficiency free if the passing game improves. Ceiling is the 154-target 2024 baseline with better play; floor is 100 points again if he misses ten games. No competing target-earner on the roster.

a.j. brown.verdict: New England move resets everything; the 28.7% share and 91% snaps travel, the target volume is unknown.
a.j. brown.report: Brown held a 28.7% target share, 0.68 WOPR and 91% snaps in 15 games while efficiency slid from 2.24 to 1.82 points per target — good volume, softening efficiency at age-30. In New England the depth chart (Doubs, Boutte, Douglas) hands him an unchallenged WR1 role and likely more targets than a run-first Philly gave him. Ceiling is 130 targets and 16 PPG; floor is a slow chemistry build plus his usual two missed games. Week 15 at KC is a hard playoff open.

chris olave.verdict: Fully healthy 2025 produced 156 targets and 15.8 PPG; ADP 35.7 lags his actual finish.
chris olave.report: Olave answered the durability question with 16 games, a 29.2% target share, 41.0% air-yards share and 0.72 WOPR, turning it into 268 points. Efficiency is only fair (1.72 pts/target, 7.5 yds/target) — high volume, average efficiency, the profile that lives on continued opportunity. Rookie-year Jordyn Tyson is the one meaningful threat to the target share. Ceiling is 17 PPG; floor is a return to concussion-shortened seasons. The camp headline offers nothing specific.

george pickens.verdict: 17.2 PPG on only a 22.5% share — elite 5.22 rec EPA/game means he does not need more targets.
george pickens.report: Pickens is the low-volume/high-efficiency breakout already partly realized: 22.5% target share and 0.56 WOPR turned into 292 points on 2.13 points per target and a 5.22 receiving EPA per game, best in this tier. He played all 17 games. Ceiling is a genuine WR1 season if a healthy Lamb forces defenses off him; floor is target share squeezed back under 20% with Lamb whole — that split is the real risk. Week 14 bye is inconvenient but the playoff slate is fine.

malik nabers.verdict: 170-target rookie year and a 15.9 aDOT in his four 2025 games; listed Questionable, so this is a health bet.
malik nabers.report: The 2024 season (170 targets, 16.1 PPG, 109 catches) is the real baseline; the four-game 2025 sample still showed a 27.1% target share, 43.9% air-yards share and 0.71 WOPR before the injury. Volume is elite when he plays, efficiency is only average (1.61-1.63 pts/target) — he wins on sheer looks. Ceiling at ADP 44.7 is a top-10 WR return; floor is a Questionable tag that becomes another lost season. Mooney and Slayton do not threaten the role.

tetairoa mcmillan.verdict: 122 targets, 45.9% air-yards share and 87% snaps as a rookie — the classic year-two volume breakout.
tetairoa mcmillan.report: McMillan drew a 25.7% target share and a striking 45.9% of Carolina's air yards on 87% snaps across all 17 games, with a low 6.9 weekly stdev for a rookie. Efficiency was only okay (1.73 pts/target, 1.49 rec EPA/g), which is normal for a first-year alpha absorbing deep targets. Metchie, Coker and Legette pose no threat to the role, so 140 targets is realistic. Ceiling 17 PPG; floor is stagnation if the quarterback play does not improve. Playoff slate (CIN, at PIT, SEA) is unhelpful.

zay flowers.verdict: 29.9% share, 10 carries and 2.06 pts/target across 17 games — quietly the steadiest WR2 on the board.
zay flowers.report: Flowers improved in every column: 14.3 PPG, 29.9% target share, 0.70 WOPR, 2.06 points per target, plus 10 designed carries, on 86% snaps in all 17 games. That is good volume with above-average efficiency, and the 7.3 stdev makes him a plug-and-play WR2. Ceiling is 16 PPG if Baltimore throws more; floor is his 12.3 PPG 2024 line. Bateman and Lane are secondary. Playoff draw is all division games, a mild negative.

devonta smith.verdict: A.J. Brown's departure vacates a 28.7% target share in Philadelphia — Smith is the direct beneficiary.
devonta smith.report: Smith has been a consistent 11.7-11.9 PPG on a 24.6% share and 0.59 WOPR with strong per-target work (3.20 rec EPA/game, aDOT 12.0) — low-volume, good-efficiency, exactly the profile that only needs opportunity. Brown leaving for New England frees roughly 120 targets, and Philadelphia's remaining WR room is empty. Ceiling is a 140-target, 16 PPG season; floor is a run-heavy Eagles offense keeping him near 11 PPG. Durable: 17 games each of the last two years.

emeka egbuka.verdict: 127 rookie targets but 1.54 pts/target and a 50% catch rate — the volume outran the efficiency.
emeka egbuka.report: Egbuka played all 17 games with a 23.6% target share and 78% snaps, but converted just 63 of 127 targets and posted 0.42 receiving EPA per game — high volume, poor efficiency, the quadrant where the targets are at risk of moving. Godwin's health and McMillan's presence make that share contestable. Ceiling is a year-two efficiency jump to 15 PPG on the same looks; floor is a target-share squeeze back toward 18%. Playoff schedule (NO, at ATL, LAR) is manageable.

davante adams.verdict: 3.72 points per touch on just 60 catches is touchdown math, and he is the clear WR2 behind Nacua.
davante adams.report: Adams turned a 25.1% share into 223 points largely through scoring: 3.72 points per touch on only 6.9 yards per target and a 71% snap share across 14 games at age 33. That is TD-dependent production on shrinking volume behind an ascendant Nacua who commands 30% of targets. Ceiling is another red-zone-fueled 14 PPG; floor is snap-share erosion to the mid-60s and single-digit weeks. Weekly stdev of 8.5 confirms the boom-bust.

ladd mcconkey.verdict: Target share fell to 21.1% with a 0.50 WOPR — the crowded Chargers room genuinely took work away.
ladd mcconkey.report: McConkey regressed across the board: 14.2 to 10.6 PPG, 2.15 to 1.71 points per target, target share 21.1% and WOPR just 0.50, the lowest in this group, with 0.45 receiving EPA per game. That is a shrinking role, not bad luck. Harris and Johnston are both real target competition. Ceiling is a rebound to the 2024 112-target, 14 PPG line if the room thins; floor is another 10 PPG WR3 season. ADP 54 is fair rather than a bargain.

tee higgins.verdict: Best blend of role security and per-target scoring in this range; 81% snaps opposite Chase with Burrow throwing.
tee higgins.report: Two straight full seasons at 12-13 ppg with 98-109 targets and rising efficiency (2.16 pts/tgt, 41 first downs). Quadrant: solid volume (18.3% share, 33% air yards, WOPR 0.50) with above-average efficiency — the safe profile at a WR2 price. Ceiling is a 90-catch, double-digit-TD year if Burrow plays 17; floor is the same 200-point baseline he posted even in a messy 2025. Chase caps target share, so TD variance drives the range.

jameson williams.verdict: 90% snap share, 11.0 yds/tgt and back-to-back ~215-point seasons — the most stable profile at ADP 67.
jameson williams.report: Remarkably repeatable: 212 then 220 points, 12.5/12.9 ppg, identical 11.0 yds/tgt. Quadrant: moderate volume (18.6% target share, WOPR 0.50) with excellent efficiency (3.30 rec EPA/g) — the deep role is earned, not lucky, and 90% snaps means he's on the field for everything. Ceiling is 275+ if the target share ticks up behind St. Brown; floor is the 200 he's twice guaranteed. Nobody in the room (TeSlaa, Dortch) threatens snaps.

jaylen waddle.verdict: Elite 2025 usage (WOPR 0.65, 42.7% air yards) but he carries it into Denver as the #2 behind Sutton.
jaylen waddle.report: 2025 was his real breakout by usage: 23.3% target share, 42.7% air-yards share, 100 targets, 11.4 ppg. Quadrant: high volume, average efficiency (1.94 pts/tgt) — meaning the production was opportunity-driven, and opportunity is exactly what changes in Denver. Sutton commanded 124 targets and 21.1% share last year; Franklin and Mims eat more. Ceiling is a genuine 1A role and 250+; floor is a 110-point split-role season while the offense sorts out.

terry mclaurin.verdict: Lost 2025 masks elite per-game usage — WOPR 0.61 when healthy — but age 31 and injury make ADP 60 steep.
terry mclaurin.report: The 6.7 ppg headline is a 10-game, injury-wrecked sample; inside it he ran a 23.2% target share, 37.1% air-yards share, WOPR 0.61 with a 14.0 aDOT. Quadrant: high volume, average efficiency (1.90 pts/tgt) — the role is unquestioned with only Antonio Williams and Dyami Brown behind him. Ceiling is the 2024 line, 268 points at 15.8 ppg. Floor is another shortened year at 31; that risk, not the role, is why I won't pay ADP 60.

courtland sutton.verdict: 220 and 240 points in back-to-back 17-game seasons at ADP 86 — the cleanest value in the group.
courtland sutton.report: Two identical seasons: 124-135 targets, 21.1% share, 34.4% air-yards share, WOPR 0.56, 52 first downs, 85% snaps, and zero games missed. Quadrant: high volume, fair efficiency (1.77 pts/tgt) — the volume is the asset, and it is the piece Waddle's arrival puts at risk. Ceiling is another 240 if he stays the red-zone alpha; floor is ~145 if Denver truly splits it two ways. At ADP 86 you're paid for that risk.

dk metcalf.verdict: 22.4% target share and WOPR 0.60 make him the alpha, but Pittman's arrival trims the ceiling.
dk metcalf.report: Metronomic: 187 and 191 points, 11.0-11.2 ppg with the lowest weekly stdev (6.8) in this tier. Quadrant: high volume (22.4% share, 37.2% air yards), fair efficiency (1.89 pts/tgt) at a shrunken 10.5 aDOT — production hinges on target count, and Pittman just walked in with a 111-target profile. Ceiling ~235 if he keeps the deep and red-zone work; floor ~130 in a true 1A/1B. Playoff slate (BAL, CAR, @TEN) is workable.

michael pittman jr..verdict: 86% snaps and 111 targets two years running; a proven target earner priced as a WR4 in Pittsburgh.
michael pittman jr..report: Rebounded to 202 points on 111 targets and 80 catches with 86% snap share — the volume has never wavered across two seasons. Quadrant: high volume, modest efficiency (1.82 pts/tgt, 7.1 yds/tgt) — a possession/PPR profile that survives a QB downgrade better than a deep threat's would. Ceiling ~225 if he out-targets Metcalf underneath; floor ~120 as the clear No. 2 in a run-leaning offense. New scheme is the real unknown, not the role.

carnell tate.verdict: Listed WR1 in Tennessee as a rookie with real pedigree, but ADP 68 pays for the projection, not evidence.
carnell tate.report: No NFL data, so I'm inferring from role: LWR1 ahead of Wan'Dale Robinson, an aging Ridley and Ayomanor, which is the largest rookie opportunity in this group. ESPN's "most pro-ready" call supports the profile. Ceiling is a 130-target true alpha at 240; floor is the standard rookie 55-catch, 95-point season in a low-volume passing game. The TikTok chatter is vague hype with no camp specifics — it moves price, not my evaluation, and price is already up.

luther burden iii.verdict: Best low-volume/high-efficiency profile here: 2.13 pts/tgt on a 13.1% share with ~150 targets vacated ahead.
luther burden iii.report: Rookie year was efficient on scraps: 47 catches on 60 targets, 10.9 yds/tgt, 2.00 rec EPA/g at a 7.7 aDOT. Quadrant: low volume, strong efficiency — the classic breakout setup, and ESPN flags roughly 150 vacated targets. Ceiling is a 110-target, 250-point year if Chicago funnels the slot to him; floor is a second straight ~130 if Odunze keeps commanding 23%+. ADP 76 is already inside top-100, so this is a price you pay, not a steal.

brian thomas jr..verdict: A 284-point 2024 available at ADP 101 after an efficiency crash the market has fully priced in.
brian thomas jr..report: 2025 fell to 139 points on 1.53 pts/tgt and 7.8 yds/tgt, but the role held: 19.3% target share, 31.6% air-yards share, WOPR 0.51, 14.5 aDOT. Quadrant: real volume with broken efficiency — the kind that mean-reverts when QB play does, not the kind that gets the volume taken away. Meyers, Washington and Hunter crowd the room, which is the floor risk. Sleeper: start taking him in round 8-9; the 2024 ceiling (16.7 ppg) is still in the building.

rome odunze.verdict: 23.6% target share with 1.62 pts/tgt is the warning quadrant — big volume he isn't converting, and Burden is coming.
rome odunze.report: Two seasons at 8.5-8.6 ppg despite 90-101 targets and an 88% snap share; 7.3 yds/tgt both years is not a sample-size fluke. Quadrant: high volume, poor efficiency — precisely the profile where the targets migrate elsewhere, and Burden's 10.9 yds/tgt is the reason. The McCourty note ("doesn't have to be WR1") reads as the team telegraphing a split. Ceiling ~225 on touchdown positive regression; floor is a third straight 145. ADP 71 is too rich.

dj moore.verdict: Usage fell off a cliff in 2025 (WOPR 0.38, 0.80 EPA/g); Buffalo's crowded room isn't an obvious fix.
dj moore.report: From 140 targets and 14.0 ppg to 85 targets and 10.0 — target share dropped to 16.1% and air-yards share to 19.9%, a short-area role with only 0.80 rec EPA/g. Quadrant: fading volume, mediocre efficiency. Allen raises the touchdown math, but Shakir, Palmer and Coleman all have standing, and Moore is 29 with eight years of mileage. Ceiling ~230 if he wins the perimeter job outright; floor ~115 as the third option.

marvin harrison jr..verdict: Two disappointing seasons and Michael Wilson out-targeted him; talent case only, at a non-discount price.
marvin harrison jr..report: 7.5 ppg on a 18.1% target share over 12 games, with snap share down to 71% — the volume itself regressed, and Wilson's 126 targets took the difference. Quadrant: moderate volume, below-average efficiency (1.75 pts/tgt, 8.3 yds/tgt) two years running. The 2.59 rec EPA/g says the deep work is still productive when it comes. Ceiling is the pedigree year at 240; floor is another 128-point split. At ADP 86 I'd rather have Sutton or Thomas.

alec pierce.verdict: Absurd 19.0 aDOT and 3.72 EPA/g, but he's on PUP and the profile is boom-bust by construction.
alec pierce.report: Two years of elite per-target work: 2.18 pts/tgt, 11.9 yds/tgt, 40.6% air-yards share on only a 17.6% target share. Quadrant: low volume, elite efficiency — the breakout shape, except the aDOT means weekly stdev of 8.5 and heavy TD dependence. The PUP designation (ankle) is the verifiable fact here and it caps early-season floor while Downs absorbs slot work. Ceiling 220 with a healthy 90-target year; floor 90 if the ankle lingers.

michael wilson.verdict: Scored 221 points on 126 targets and 17 games, and the market has him at ADP 110 — take the volume.
michael wilson.report: Doubled his 2024 output on a 19.2% target share, 81% snaps and 51 first downs in a full 17-game season.
