Quadrant: high volume, ordinary efficiency (1.75 pts/tgt) — the risk is a Harrison bounce-back reclaiming the targets, not a talent question. Ceiling ~220 if the split holds; floor ~110 in a genuine MHJ resurgence. Sleeper: he outproduced his own WR1 and costs four rounds less — start taking him in round 9, and he's a fine WR4 with WR2 weeks.

christian watson.verdict: 2.41 pts/tgt and 17.8 aDOT on 55 targets — the purest low-volume/high-efficiency lottery ticket here.
christian watson.report: Only 10 games and a 68% snap share, but inside them: 20.3% target share, 34.8% air-yards share, WOPR 0.55, 3.23 rec EPA/g. Quadrant: low volume, elite efficiency — he needs snaps, not skill. Reed and Golden crowd the room and Green Bay spreads it thinner than any offense, which is the floor case (85 points). Sleeper: start taking him round 9; if he clears 75 targets healthy the 11.1 yds/tgt makes 215 realistic. Injury history is the tax.

jordyn tyson.verdict: Rookie WR2 behind Olave with real draft capital; a cheap piece of a passing game the market is warming to.
jordyn tyson.report: No NFL data, so I'm inferring from role: RWR2 with only Means and Vele behind him, in an offense the crowd expects to throw more under Shough. ESPN's "rookie complementing a veteran star" framing fits — Olave takes the alpha share, Tyson takes the leftovers, which is a 90-target ceiling. Note the chatter's checkable facts (Pittman gone, Pierce's ankle) are about other players, not him. Sleeper: round 9-10; floor is the typical 80-point rookie year.

parker washington.verdict: Real 2025 leap, but a 61% snap share in a room adding a healthy Hunter and Meyers is fragile volume.
parker washington.report: Jumped from 97 to 185 points on 95 targets and an 18% target share with 38 first downs. Quadrant: moderate volume, ordinary efficiency (1.94 pts/tgt, 24.2% air-yards share) — a slot role, and the 61% snap share says the offense was never fully committed. Ceiling ~195 if Jacksonville keeps him at 95 targets; floor ~95 as Hunter and Thomas soak up the perimeter and Meyers takes underneath work. ADP 101 is fair, not a bargain.

matthew golden.verdict: ESPN's sleeper call, but 12.4% share, 53% snaps and 1.59 pts/tgt as a rookie don't support the badge.
matthew golden.report: Rookie line was weak on both axes: 44 targets, 12.4% target share, 19.4% air-yards share, WOPR 0.32, and 1.59 pts/tgt — low volume AND poor efficiency, the fade quadrant. He's listed third behind Watson and Reed, so the "handed early opportunity" premise isn't visible in the snap data; I'm skipping the sleeper badge for that reason. A year-two leap is plausible (12.5 aDOT, 2.2 yds after contact on jet work) but it's a bet on nothing measured.

mike evans.verdict: 33 years old, 5.0 ppg and 0.66 EPA/g in eight games, now WR2 in San Francisco — ADP 88 is the worst price here.
mike evans.report: The 2025 collapse wasn't only injury: in the 8 games played, a 24.3% target share produced just 1.39 pts/tgt and 6.0 yds/tgt with 0.66 rec EPA/g — high volume, broken efficiency, the quadrant where the volume disappears next. Now he's behind Deebo with Pearsall and Kirk also in the room and a 66% snap share to defend. Ceiling is a 190-point touchdown-fueled bounce; floor is 70 points and a waiver drop. Fade at cost.

jakobi meyers.verdict: Safest volume in this range: 22.9% target share and 85% snaps, but efficiency caps the spike weeks.
jakobi meyers.report: High-volume/average-efficiency quadrant: 22.9% target share, 0.54 WOPR, 85% snaps, yet only 1.60 pts/tgt and 7.6 yds/tgt. Two straight 17-game seasons and 44 first downs make him the steadiest PPR floor here. Ceiling needs Brian Thomas to pull coverage and more red-zone work; floor is 8-9 PPG if Travis Hunter's year-two leap eats slot and route share. Playoff slate (@HOU, @DAL, WSH) is neutral.

wan'dale robinson.verdict: Elite 30.3% target share and 91% snaps; new Tennessee funnel is the only real question.
wan'dale robinson.report: Top-of-league volume — 30.3% target share, 0.65 WOPR, 91% snaps, 140 targets — with low-efficiency underpinnings (8.5 aDOT, 7.2 yds/tgt), the profile PPR still pays (218 pts). New team matters: Carnell Tate and Ridley reshape the target tree, so 140 looks like the outlier, not the baseline. ESPN's sleeper tag is already priced at ADP 113, so no badge. Floor is reception-driven; ceiling needs touchdowns he has never had.

travis hunter.verdict: Year-two athletic upside, but 17.5% target share and negative rec EPA on 66% snaps is a bet, not a base.
travis hunter.report: Low volume, poor efficiency so far: 17.5% target share, 0.39 WOPR, -0.33 rec EPA/g in only seven games at 66% snaps. Camp news (10 pounds heavier, faster than ever) is a genuine positive signal and the two-way workload should shrink toward offense. Ceiling is a 120-target alpha share if he passes Washington and pushes Meyers; floor is another injury-shortened, part-time year behind Brian Thomas. Price at ADP 118 assumes the leap.

makai lemon.verdict: Rookie slot WR2 in Philadelphia with real route access, but ADP 107 already pays for the projection.
makai lemon.report: No NFL data, so the inference is role: SWR2 behind DeVonta Smith with only Marquise Brown and Wicks contesting snaps — a genuine 90-110 target path if he wins camp. Crowd chatter is vague and negative (2 likes, no snap counts) and tells us about price, not the player; ignore it. Ceiling is a 12-PPG rookie in a real offense; floor is a run-heavy scheme that leaves him at 55 targets. Playoffs SEA/HOU/@SF are tough.

josh downs.verdict: Snap share fell to 59% and target share to 17.5%; the trend is the wrong direction at a fair price.
josh downs.report: 2025 was a step back on both axes — 17.5% target share (from a bigger 2024 role), 0.38 WOPR, 59% snaps, 1.55 pts/tgt — so he sits mid-volume with only average efficiency. Alec Pierce owns the deep share and the Colts split three ways, capping the funnel. Ceiling is a return to 2024's 107 targets and 10.8 PPG if Indy throws more; floor is 6-7 PPG part-time slot work. ADP 134 is fair value, not a bargain.

jordan addison.verdict: Low-volume, high-efficiency downfield role next to Jefferson; 2024's 213 points is the live ceiling.
jordan addison.report: Efficiency quadrant: 33.0% air-yards share, 13.7 aDOT, 1.00 rec EPA/g and 1.71 pts/tgt on just 18.2% of targets across 14 games. That is a breakout profile waiting on volume, but Jefferson commands the coverage and targets, and Jauan Jennings adds a body. Ceiling is 2024 again (99 targets, 12.5 PPG, 213 pts); floor is another 79-target season with a 6.2 weekly stdev of boom-bust. Playoffs DET/WSH/@NYJ are workable.

khalil shakir.verdict: Reception floor with a 3.7 aDOT ceiling cap, and only 60% snaps with DJ Moore now in Buffalo.
khalil shakir.report: Volume without yardage: 21.1% target share but an 8.6% air-yards share and 3.7 aDOT, so 72 catches produced just 166 points. Efficiency per target (1.75) is fine; the route depth simply forbids spike weeks. Snap share of 60% with DJ Moore arriving as the clear WR1 is the real risk to the volume itself. Ceiling is 85 catches and 11 PPG in a high-scoring Buffalo offense; floor is a 7-PPG rotational slot. Boring, safe, capped.

jayden reed.verdict: 2.63 pts/tgt on 75 targets in 2024 — the cleanest low-volume/elite-efficiency breakout bet on this board.
jayden reed.report: 2024 was the profile: 11.6 PPG on only 75 targets plus 20 carries, 11.4 yds/tgt, 2.63 pts/tgt. 2025 was five games and a lost season, not a talent change — his 2.31 rec EPA/g in that sample is loud. Green Bay's room is unsettled (Watson, second-year Golden), so a 100-target role is available. Floor is another injury year; ceiling is 200-plus points. Sleeper: start taking him in round 11 at ADP 137.

xavier worthy.verdict: 26.8% air-yards share and 1.06 rec EPA/g on limited volume in Mahomes' offense at a round-11 price.
xavier worthy.report: Low volume, strong efficiency: 16.1% target share but 26.8% air-yards share, 12.9 aDOT, 1.06 rec EPA/g across 14 games after an early injury wrecked the start. 2024's 98 targets, 20 carries and 187 points is the realistic ceiling if Rice misses any time; Rice healthy makes him the clear No. 2 and caps him near 75 targets. Gadget carries add floor. Sleeper at ADP 137 — I would start taking him in round 11.

quentin johnston.verdict: Two straight 10-PPG seasons with 2.01 pts/tgt and 1.84 rec EPA/g, and the market has him at pick 144.
quentin johnston.report: Good efficiency on real volume: 20.0% target share, 0.50 WOPR, 11.8 aDOT, 1.84 rec EPA/g, 2.01 pts/tgt — 171 points despite missing time. The catch is touchdown reliance and an 8.4 weekly stdev, plus Tre' Harris pushing for the second outside job behind McConkey. Ceiling is 90 targets and 12 PPG; floor is a 6-PPG stretch when the scores dry up. Sleeper from round 12 given the two-year production baseline.

kc concepcion.verdict: Rookie slot with a real path past Jeudy's collapse, but a bottom-tier passing game caps the payoff.
kc concepcion.report: No NFL data; the case is role and vacancy — Jeudy posted -1.90 rec EPA/g and 1.14 pts/tgt on 106 targets, so those looks are genuinely available. Chatter is thin (a 21-like TikTok; the Sanderson video never confirms him), which moves price, not projection, so no sleeper badge from me. Ceiling is 90 targets and WR3 numbers; floor is 40 targets in a low-volume, low-efficiency Cleveland offense. @BAL in week 16 hurts.

deebo samuel.verdict: Signed back in SF on a 1-year deal after an 11.1-PPG, 99-target, 17-carry season — free at ADP 167.
deebo samuel.report: The confirmed one-year 49ers deal is the freshest fact and it puts a dual-usage veteran back in a scheme built for him: 2025 gave 188 points on 99 targets plus 17 carries at 72% snaps, with 2.6 yards after contact per rush. The room is crowded (Evans, Pearsall, Kirk), so target squeeze is the floor case at 7 PPG. Ceiling is 90 touches and 190-plus points. Sleeper: worth a round-13 pick, earlier than his rank.

chris godwin jr..verdict: Nine games, 4.9 PPG, and Egbuka now owns the offense — the age and injury curve is bending down.
chris godwin jr..report: Volume has evaporated: 17.9% target share, 0.38 WOPR, 51 targets in nine games, and 1.63 pts/tgt versus 2.22 the year before. The 1.63 rec EPA/g says he can still play when healthy, but two straight injury-shortened years and Egbuka's emergence make the target path narrow. Ceiling is a 100-target bounce if Tampa's room thins; floor is another five-week absence at 5 PPG. Bench-flex dart only at this price.

romeo doubs.verdict: 2.17 rec EPA/g and 28% air-yards share travel well, but A.J. Brown owns New England's target tree.
romeo doubs.report: Efficient mid-volume profile: 18.9% target share, 0.48 WOPR, 12.8 aDOT, 2.17 rec EPA/g, 1.95 pts/tgt and 41 first downs on 78% snaps — real WR2 work, not empty targets. New team is the swing: Drake Maye is a QB upgrade, but A.J. Brown absorbs the alpha share and Boutte/Douglas split the rest. Ceiling is 90 targets and 11 PPG; floor is 60 targets as the third read. Week 15 @KC is a tough playoff open.

jayden higgins.verdict: 1.90 pts/tgt and 12.3 aDOT on a 12.4% target share — the classic low-volume, good-efficiency breakout bet.
jayden higgins.report: Rookie year was efficient but rationed: 12.4% target share, 0.31 WOPR, 57% snaps, yet 1.90 pts/tgt, 0.99 rec EPA/g and 130 points. ESPN's breakout call (matched the WR1's touchdowns) is supported by the per-target data, and a snap-share jump alone gets him to 100 targets. Nico Collins caps the ceiling and Dell/Noel contest the rest, which is the floor case at 6 PPG. Sleeper — start taking him in round 13.

jalen coker.verdict: Two seasons above 2.0 pts/tgt and 9-plus yds/tgt, but he is buried at WR3 behind McMillan and Metchie.
jalen coker.report: Efficiency is legitimate — 2.10 pts/tgt, 9.2 yds/tgt, 1.99 rec EPA/g on a 15.4% target share and 69% snaps across 11 games. That is the breakout quadrant, but the opportunity is not opening: McMillan is the alpha and Metchie sits ahead of him, so he needs an injury to clear 70 targets. No sleeper badge for that reason. Ceiling is 10 PPG in an expanded role; floor is 40 targets and waiver-wire relevance.

jerry jeudy.verdict: Big volume, terrible per-target output: 0.56 WOPR but -1.90 rec EPA/g — the volume itself is at risk.
jerry jeudy.report: The warning quadrant in full: 20.5% target share, 35.4% air-yards share, 0.56 WOPR and 85% snaps produced just 121 points at 1.14 pts/tgt and 5.7 yds/tgt. That is quarterback-driven, and Cleveland has not fixed it; Concepcion and Boston are the reason the 106 targets may not repeat. Ceiling is a QB upgrade restoring 2024's 241-point season; floor is 7 PPG with a shrinking route share. Draft the volume, not the player.

rashid shaheed.verdict: Third option behind JSN and Kupp with -0.24 rec EPA/g; big-play spikes, no weekly floor.
rashid shaheed.report: Volume is thin and efficiency did not justify it: 16.2% target share, 0.40 WOPR, 61% snaps and -0.24 rec EPA/g on an 11.4 aDOT, adding to only 8.7 PPG across 18 games. He is the field-stretcher behind Smith-Njigba with Kupp still taking slot work, so the target ceiling is roughly 95. Ceiling is a touchdown-fueled 11 PPG; floor is three catches for 35 most weeks. Week 15 @PHI is a bad playoff open.

jalen mcmillan.verdict: Four-game 2025 hides a real 2024 (2.33 pts/tgt); Godwin's decline is the opening at a round-14 cost.
jalen mcmillan.report: 2024 gave 135 points on 58 targets at 2.33 pts/tgt — low volume, strong efficiency. 2025 was four games and 15 targets, but 11.9 yds/tgt and 3.12 rec EPA/g in that sliver back the FantasyPros/ESPN call. Egbuka is the alpha and Godwin still nominally sits ahead, yet Godwin's 4.9 PPG and injury history is exactly the opening. Floor is another lost year; ceiling is 90 targets. Sleeper — round 14 dart.

calvin ridley.verdict: 2.8 PPG over seven games at age 31, now the third option behind Tate and Robinson in Tennessee.
calvin ridley.report: The collapse was real: 47 points, 1.31 pts/tgt, 36 targets in seven games at 57% snaps. The 24.4% air-yards share and 1.75 rec EPA/g say he can still win deep, so this is low volume with mixed efficiency, not zero talent. But Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson's 30% target share leave him third in line, and 2024's 120-target season is not coming back without an injury ahead of him. Dart throw only.

tre tucker.verdict: Only true every-down WR1 here: 95% snaps, 19% target share, rising efficiency — at a 14th-round price.
tre tucker.report: High volume + improving efficiency, the safest quadrant in this group: 95% snap share over 17 games, 19.0% target share, .47 WOPR, 26% air-yards share, and PPG up 7.6 to 9.5 with pts/target climbing 1.60 to 1.76 and +1.28 rec EPA/g. Nailor and Bech are complementary, not threats to the alpha role. Floor is the 130-150 he has already banked twice; ceiling is 100+ targets and WR3 numbers. Wk15 DEN is the one rough playoff draw.

jauan jennings.verdict: Proven 90-113 target earner, but a move to Minnesota buries him behind Jefferson and Addison.
jauan jennings.report: Two straight seasons of real volume (113 then 90 targets, 19.9% share, .48 WOPR, 82% snaps) with league-average efficiency — high volume, so-so efficiency, and now the volume itself is the question. In Minnesota he is the clear No. 3 behind Jefferson and Addison; the slot role and red-zone hands keep a WR4 floor, and an injury ahead of him unlocks 10+ PPG again. Wk15 DET, wk16 WSH is a workable playoff run.

rashod bateman.verdict: 2024 gave 175 points; 2025 gave 55 on collapsed efficiency — cheap bet on the middle outcome.
rashod bateman.report: Bateman fell from 72 targets/2.43 pts per target to 38 targets/1.46 with -0.13 rec EPA/g, and 11.9% target share on 69% snaps is a low-volume, poor-efficiency line — the fade quadrant unless the touchdown regression that inflated 2024 and gutted 2025 mean-reverts. He is still the clear No. 2 opposite Zay Flowers with only unproven bodies behind him, which is the whole case. Playoffs are all division games (@PIT, CLE, @CIN) and tough.

adonai mitchell.verdict: 30% air-yards share on 51% of snaps is real opportunity; the 1.19 pts/target that came with it is not.
adonai mitchell.report: Volume signal is genuine — 74 targets, 15.3% target share, 30.3% air-yards share, .44 WOPR, 14.9 aDOT — but the efficiency is the worst in this group: 1.19 pts/target, 6.1 yds/target, -1.01 rec EPA/g. That is the high-air-yards, poor-conversion quadrant where the targets get reallocated if he does not improve. ESPN's sleeper call is on talent and snap growth, not production, so I am not badging it. Garrett Wilson caps the ceiling; a deep-ball spike week is the payoff.

antonio williams.verdict: Rookie slot with the emptiest depth chart in the group behind McLaurin; multiple analysts already on him.
antonio williams.report: No NFL usage data, so the case is depth chart: behind Terry McLaurin sit Dyami Brown, Van Jefferson and Jaylin Lane — replaceable bodies, and the slot job is genuinely open. Smyth, Boone and FantasyPros all flagged the immediate role plus contested-catch ability, and I agree the opening is concrete rather than hype. Floor is 35-40 targets if Washington rotates; ceiling is 90 targets and WR3 value. Start taking him in round 13.

denzel boston.verdict: Highest rookie projection here (132) with only Jeudy and a fellow rookie ahead of him in a thin Cleveland room.
denzel boston.report: No usage data yet, so I lean on the depth chart and the 132-point projection, which is the top mark among the rookies listed. Cleveland's room is Jerry Jeudy, rookie KC Concepcion and Cedric Tillman — no entrenched second option, so a boundary rookie can win 70-80 targets by midseason. Floor is a rotational 30 targets on a low-volume passing game; ceiling is WR3 flex weeks. Playoff slate (@NYG, @BAL, IND) is mixed. Round 14 dart.

darnell mooney.verdict: Still commands 16% of targets and 28% of air yards, but 1.14 pts/target is the fade half of that profile.
darnell mooney.report: The 2024 line (106 targets, 193 points) is now two years stale; 2025 was 72 targets for 82 points at 1.14 pts/target and 6.2 yds/target despite an 82% snap share and 14.2 aDOT — real volume, bad conversion, the warning quadrant. Nabers owns the offense and Slayton, Austin and Beckham split what is left. Floor is the WR5 he was last year; ceiling requires the deep balls to connect again. Wk16 @DET, wk17 @DAL is a poor playoff draw.

jalen nailor.verdict: Best points-per-touch in the group (3.25) on only 11.7% of targets — the classic needs-opportunity profile.
jalen nailor.report: Low volume, strong efficiency: 53 targets but 1.90 pts/target, 8.4 yds/target, 12.4 aDOT, +0.68 rec EPA/g and 6.0 yards after contact on his rare touches, all on a 65% snap share. Two straight 100-point seasons on sub-55 targets means any bump in role scales fast. Tucker's 19% share is the ceiling cap, and Bech/Thornton eat some snaps. If Tucker misses time this is an instant flex. Take him in the last two rounds.

germie bernard.verdict: Rookie slot in Pittsburgh with Metcalf and Pittman outside — real target funnel underneath if he wins the job.
germie bernard.report: No pro data; the read is situational. Metcalf and Pittman command the perimeter, which leaves the slot and the underneath work genuinely available with only Roman Wilson and Skowronek behind him. A 127-point projection implies the staff expects a role by midseason. Floor is a fourth-option rookie who never clears 40 targets; ceiling is 75 catchable slot targets. Wk16 CAR and wk17 @TEN is a friendly playoff finish.

tank dell.verdict: 8.2 PPG the last time he was healthy, but he lost a full year and Houston drafted past him.
tank dell.report: 2024 was a legitimate WR3 line — 81 targets, 51 catches, 1.73 pts/target, 8.2 yds/target — but a missed 2025 and a Questionable tag mean the burst is unproven. Houston's room hardened around Nico Collins and Jayden Higgins, with Noel also in the slot mix, so he is the third or fourth option even when right. Floor is a wasted roster spot; ceiling is the 2024 form if he reclaims the slot. Wk16 @PHI, wk17 @GB is a hard finish.

ryan flournoy.verdict: 2.04 pts/target and +1.91 EPA/g on a 45% snap share — efficiency is there, the snaps are not yet.
ryan flournoy.report: Went from 14 targets to 56 and 114 points while playing under half the snaps: 1.11% target share aside, 2.04 pts/target, 8.5 yds/target and +1.91 rec EPA/g is the low-volume, high-efficiency breakout quadrant. The problem is Lamb, Pickens and Turpin ahead of him — his path is an injury or a Pickens departure, not organic growth. Floor is the same 45% rotational role; ceiling is 85 targets in a high-volume passing game. Last-round flier.

zachariah branch.verdict: Rookie slot behind Drake London with only Dotson and Zaccheaus to beat — cheap, but Atlanta throws little.
zachariah branch.report: No usage data; the inference is role plus environment. The slot job is winnable immediately against Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus, but London absorbs the target share and Atlanta has been a run-first, low-volume passing team, which caps the ceiling more than the depth chart does. Floor is 30 targets and return work; ceiling is a 70-target PPR slot role. Playoff slate (@WSH, TB, NO) is neutral to good.

stefon diggs.verdict: Best 2025 line in this group (210 pts, 21.9% target share) but unsigned in late July — a pure lottery ticket.
stefon diggs.report: On the field he was excellent: 102 targets on just 54% of snaps, 21.9% target share, 85 catches, 2.06 pts/target, +4.14 rec EPA/g and 51 first downs at 8.5 aDOT — elite efficiency on part-time snaps. The problem is category one: no team, a zero projection, and no playoff schedule. If he signs somewhere with targets he immediately outproduces everyone below Tucker here; if he does not sign, he scores nothing. Only draft in the final round or off waivers after signing.

ricky pearsall.verdict: ADP 128 for a 59-point projection — great per-route efficiency, but Deebo and Evans crowded him out.
ricky pearsall.report: The nine-game advanced sample is excellent — 18.0% target share, 31.8% air-yards share, .49 WOPR, 14.1 aDOT, +2.97 rec EPA/g — genuine low-volume, high-efficiency talent. But the July news confirms Deebo Samuel is back and Mike Evans sits ahead of him too, dropping him to third or fourth in a crowded room while carrying a Questionable tag and a 9-of-17 game history. The ADP is 40 picks earlier than the value board says; let someone else pay.

tre' harris.verdict: Low volume, modest efficiency as a rookie WR3 — needs McConkey or Johnston gone to matter.
tre' harris.report: 43 targets, 69 points, 1.61 pts/target and a tiny 2.9 weekly stdev say rotational and unspectacular — the low-volume, average-efficiency corner where you are betting on year-two development rather than opportunity. Ladd McConkey owns the target share and Quentin Johnston still holds the other boundary spot. Floor is another sub-50-target season; ceiling is 80 targets in a good passing offense if the depth chart shifts. Wk17 KC is a rough finish.

xavier legette.verdict: Two years of poor efficiency (1.40 pts/tgt, -0.27 EPA/g) and now fourth on the Carolina depth chart.
xavier legette.report: Volume declined from 84 to 64 targets while efficiency stayed bad — 5.7 yds/target, 1.40 pts/target, -0.27 rec EPA/g on a 68% snap share. That is the poor-efficiency half of a moderate-volume role, exactly the profile teams take snaps away from, and they did: McMillan, Metchie and Coker are all listed ahead of him now. Floor is a special-teams-adjacent WR5; ceiling requires two injuries plus a leap he has not shown.

omar cooper jr..verdict: Rookie with no measurable role yet on a Jets offense that funnels through Garrett Wilson.
omar cooper jr..report: No usage data and no clean depth-chart match, so the inference is a 105-point projection and a listed No. 3 spot behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell. Wilson's target share plus Mitchell's air-yards role leaves little for a rookie unless he wins the slot outright in camp. Floor is inactive weeks; ceiling is 60 targets if Mitchell's efficiency problems cost him snaps, which is a real if. Watch camp before spending a pick.

de'zhaun stribling.verdict: Fourth or fifth on the most crowded WR depth chart in this group — talent has nowhere to go.
de'zhaun stribling.report: No pro data to work from, and the situation is the worst here: Deebo Samuel, Mike Evans, Ricky Pearsall and Christian Kirk are all ahead of or level with him in San Francisco, with the tight end also eating targets. A 101-point projection looks generous against that room. Floor is zero fantasy relevance; ceiling requires two injuries ahead of him. Wk15 @LAC and wk16 @KC compound the problem. Deep dynasty stash, not a redraft pick.

jack bech.verdict: 8% target share, 0.20 WOPR and negative EPA behind Tucker and Nailor — low volume, low efficiency.
jack bech.report: The fade quadrant: 29 targets, 42 points, 1.46 pts/target, -0.15 rec EPA/g and a 40% snap share, with 8.3 aDOT that gives him no big-play equity either. Tucker takes 19% of targets and Nailor is the more efficient complement, so the third-option snaps are not obviously his. Floor is single-digit fantasy weeks all year; ceiling is a modest slot bump if Nailor misses time. Year-two leap is possible but nothing in the usage predicts it.

jaylin noel.verdict: 6% target share, 26% snaps, and now on PUP — no volume, no health, no path.
jaylin noel.report: The thinnest usage profile in the group: 35 targets, 6.0% target share, .13 WOPR, 26% snap share, listed primarily as a kick returner. Efficiency was fine on those scraps (1.95 pts/target, +0.83 EPA/g), but that is a tiny sample and does not create opportunity behind Nico Collins, Jayden Higgins and Tank Dell. The PUP designation is a verifiable fact that pushes the start of any role back further. Wk16 @PHI and wk17 @GB seal it — undraftable in 12-team redraft.

isaac teslaa.verdict: Low-volume/high-efficiency rookie in a great offense with only two bodies ahead — the cleanest breakout dart here
isaac teslaa.report: Textbook low-volume, high-efficiency breakout profile: just a 5.7% target share and 40% snaps, but 2.81 pts/tgt, 8.9 yds/tgt, a 13.0 aDOT and 1.27 rec EPA/g as a rookie. Year 2 in Detroit with only St. Brown and Jameson Williams ahead is the opening. Floor is another 4-5 PPG if snaps don't move; ceiling is 130+ if Williams misses time. Sleeper — start taking him round 14.

chris bell.verdict: PUP rookie sitting fifth in Miami's room; the injury costs him the camp reps he needed to climb
chris bell.report: Rookie on PUP and fifth on the depth chart — the injury designation is the verifiable fact and it costs him exactly the camp reps needed to climb. Miami's room is thin enough that health alone could produce a role by midseason, which is the entire ceiling case. No usage data exists to argue efficiency either way, so I infer from role only. Undraftable in 12-team formats; watchlist stash.

malik washington.verdict: High volume, poor efficiency — but the PPR catch floor is real in a gutted Miami receiver room
malik washington.report: High-volume, poor-efficiency quadrant, and that is the warning: 14.4% target share and 46 catches, but a 5.2 aDOT, 4.9 yds/tgt and -0.58 rec EPA/g. Still, the PPR reception floor plus 17 carries is real in a Miami room where only Wease is established ahead of him. Ceiling is 80+ targets and WR4 value; floor is rookie Douglas passing him on the outside. Round 14 sleeper for volume, not talent.

jalen tolbert.verdict: 152 points in 2024 to 46 in 2025 as target share halved; new team, but fourth on the chart again
jalen tolbert.report: Collapse from 152 points to 46 as the target share halved to 7.6% and efficiency fell to 1.36 pts/tgt — decent air-yards share, no conversion, the poor-efficiency side of a shrinking role. The new team resets the depth chart but he still projects fourth in Miami behind two players with more current juice. Ceiling is 2024's 8.9 PPG if he wins the X job; floor is a healthy scratch.

cooper kupp.verdict: Still a 76%-snap, 0.34-WOPR slot at 33 — safest volume in this range even with a capped ceiling
cooper kupp.report: High-volume, ordinary-efficiency quadrant: a 16.0% target share, 0.34 WOPR and 76% snaps is genuine WR3 usage, but 1.66 pts/tgt and a 7.5 aDOT cap the upside and the PPG has fallen 10.3 to 6.8. Ceiling is a JSN or Shaheed absence pushing him back toward 100 targets; floor is Tory Horton eating the snaps mid-season. Wk15 @PHI is a rough playoff opener. Boring, cheap, startable in deep leagues.

caleb douglas.verdict: Rookie with no data, but Miami's post-Hill/Waddle room is the thinnest opportunity pool in the league
caleb douglas.report: No NFL usage data, so this is a pure situation bet: Miami's room behind Wease and Washington is close to empty, and a rookie who wins routes early can hold them all year. The ESPN camp headline is a generic roundup with no player-specific intel, so I discount it entirely. Ceiling is 70+ targets and low-end WR4 numbers; floor is losing the outside job and never clearing 50% snaps.

kayshon boutte.verdict: Elite per-target efficiency (2.63 EPA/g, 17.0 aDOT) on small volume — A.J. Brown is the only thing capping him
kayshon boutte.report: Low-volume, elite-efficiency quadrant: a 12.0% target share but 21.5% air-yards share, 17.0 aDOT, 2.70 pts/tgt and a huge 2.63 rec EPA/g over 14 games at 68% snaps. A.J. Brown's arrival plus Doubs squeezes the target pool, so the floor is spiky WR5 weeks. Ceiling is 8-9 PPG if he keeps the vertical role on 70 targets. The @KC/@NYJ playoff draw is unfriendly. Round 14 sleeper.

brandon aiyuk.verdict: Zero-point projection, DNR tag, sixth on the chart — the facts say do not draft
brandon aiyuk.report: A 0-point ESPN projection plus a DNR designation and WR6 on the depth chart is a verifiable fact set that overrides any memory of the 2022-23 peak. Even the last healthy sample was 3.7 PPG on 47 targets at 1.33 pts/tgt — low volume and poor efficiency, the fade quadrant. San Francisco now runs Deebo, Mike Evans and Pearsall ahead of him. Do not draft in any 12-team format.

ja'kobi lane.verdict: Rookie third in a run-first Baltimore offense; the 82-point projection outruns the available targets
ja'kobi lane.report: No NFL data, so the call rests on situation, and Baltimore's is unhelpful: Flowers and Bateman are entrenched in one of the league's lower-volume passing attacks, leaving a rookie WR3 with a thin target pool. The generic camp-roundup headline contains no player-specific intel and I ignore it. Ceiling arrives only if Bateman misses time; floor is inactive weeks. The 82-point projection is generous for the role.

ted hurst iii.verdict: No data, no confirmed depth-chart spot — a projection number attached to an unknown role
ted hurst iii.report: No NFL usage data and no depth-chart match at all, meaning we cannot even confirm he has a defined role in Tampa's room. With no snap, target or efficiency data to work from, I infer from roster ambiguity that he is a camp body fighting for WR5 reps. The 65-point projection is a placeholder, not evidence of opportunity. No basis to draft; monitor only if a Buccaneers starter goes down.

keon coleman.verdict: 0.41 WOPR usage but fourth on Buffalo's chart and 6.8 yds/tgt — volume at real risk of being taken away
keon coleman.report: Classic high-air-yards, poor-conversion warning: a 16.7% target share, 22.8% air-yards share and 0.41 WOPR in 12 games, yet efficiency fell from 9.8 to 6.8 yds/tgt and he now sits fourth behind DJ Moore, Shakir and Palmer. That is exactly the profile where volume gets reallocated. Ceiling is re-winning the X job for 130+; floor is 30 targets. ESPN's 60-point projection reflects the squeeze.

dontayvion wicks.verdict: New team, same fringe profile: 45% snaps, 1.65 pts/tgt, and fourth in a run-heavy Philadelphia offense
dontayvion wicks.report: Middling on both axes: a 12.8% target share and 16.9% air-yards share sound fine, but 1.65 pts/tgt, 7.2 yds/tgt and only 45% snaps say the volume wasn't productive. Philadelphia lists him fourth behind DeVonta Smith, Lemon and Marquise Brown in a run-first attack, so growth is unlikely. That is the low-volume, fringe-efficiency fade quadrant. Floor is roster-cut irrelevance; ceiling needs two injuries.

savion williams.verdict: 2.6% target share, 0.04 WOPR, negative rush EPA — no volume and no efficiency at either job
savion williams.report: There is almost nothing to like in the data: a 2.6% target share, 0.04 WOPR, 12% snaps, a 1.7 aDOT and -0.58 rush EPA/g on gadget carries. That is low volume and poor efficiency simultaneously — the fade quadrant. Fourth in a Green Bay room with Watson, Reed and Golden, he needs two injuries to matter. Ceiling is an expanded designed-touch role worth ~90 points; floor is total irrelevance.

pat bryant.verdict: Fine rookie process (1.09 EPA/g, 22 first downs) buried to slot #4 by Denver's Waddle addition
pat bryant.report: The rookie process was respectable — 11.0% target share, 0.28 WOPR, 1.09 rec EPA/g, 48% snaps, 22 first downs — but the efficiency was ordinary at 1.53 pts/tgt, so this is middling volume with middling conversion. Denver adding Waddle behind Sutton and Franklin drops him to slot #4, which is the real problem. Ceiling near 110 requires two absences ahead; floor is a bench stash you cut in September.

tory horton.verdict: 2.96 pts/tgt on a 15.3 aDOT in eight games — the snaps ahead of him in Seattle are the least secure here
tory horton.report: Low volume, strong efficiency: 2.96 pts/tgt, 15.3 aDOT, 1.28 rec EPA/g and a 0.28 WOPR across only eight games before the injury. He is fourth in Seattle's room, but Kupp is 33 and Shaheed is a short-term piece, so the blockers ahead are the softest in this tier. Floor is another injury-shortened 60-point year; ceiling is 130 as the vertical complement to JSN. Round 15 sleeper.

elijah sarratt.verdict: Rookie fourth on the chart in the league's lowest-volume passing game; the 59 projection is honest
elijah sarratt.report: No NFL usage data, and the situation is the worst available: fourth in Baltimore behind Flowers, Bateman and Lane in a run-first offense that does not support four fantasy receivers. With no snap or target baseline, I lean entirely on role, and the role is empty. ESPN's 59-point projection is the honest read. Ceiling requires two injuries ahead of him; floor is inactive. Not draftable in 12 teams.

dyami brown.verdict: Negative rec EPA on 37% snaps across two declining years — the 85-point projection is name recognition
dyami brown.report: Low volume and poor efficiency, the fade quadrant: a 9.9% target share, 37% snaps, 1.34 pts/tgt and -0.19 rec EPA/g despite a 14.0 aDOT that should generate big plays. Production has fallen two straight seasons, and McLaurin plus Antonio Williams sit ahead in Washington. The 85-point projection looks like name recognition rather than opportunity. Only a McLaurin injury unlocks any usable ceiling.

darius slayton.verdict: 0.41 WOPR, 25% air-yards share, 81% snaps — by far the best real usage available at pick 240
darius slayton.report: Quietly the best volume profile in this range: a 15.5% target share, 25.0% air-yards share, 0.41 WOPR and 81% snaps, with acceptable 8.5 yds/tgt and 1.29 rec EPA/g efficiency. Nabers owns the target middle, but Slayton is the field-stretcher and has cleared 99 points in each of the last two years. Floor is the same 5-6 PPG; ceiling is 140+ if Nabers misses time. Sleeper — start taking him round 14.

treylon burks.verdict: -1.10 rec EPA/g, 1.32 pts/tgt, Questionable tag, seventh on the chart — a clean fade
treylon burks.report: The fade quadrant without ambiguity: a 12.5% target share over eight games produced 1.32 pts/tgt, 5.9 yds/tgt and a dismal -1.10 rec EPA/g, so the air yards never converted. Add a Questionable tag and seventh on Washington's depth chart and the path to snaps is gone. Injuries have defined the career. Floor is zero playing time; ceiling is spot starts if both McLaurin and Brown miss extended time.

tyquan thornton.verdict: 26.9 aDOT and 27.5% air-yards share on 39% snaps — Mahomes' field-stretcher, wildly boom-or-bust
tyquan thornton.report: Extreme low-volume, high-efficiency profile: a 9.0% target share and 39% snaps, but a 26.9 aDOT, 27.5% air-yards share, 2.18 pts/tgt and 2.19 rec EPA/g. Tied to Mahomes that is a real weekly ceiling, but it is almost purely TD- and big-play dependent behind Rice and Worthy. Floor is three catches a month and a 5.5-point stdev of noise; ceiling is 140 if Rice misses time again.

troy franklin.verdict: 18.2% target share, 0.47 WOPR and 104 targets at rank 313 — the clearest mispricing in this range.
troy franklin.report: High volume, average efficiency quadrant: 104 targets, 28% air-yards share, 0.47 WOPR and 10.4 PPG in 2025 — WR3-caliber usage. The catch is Denver adding Jaylen Waddle above him, which is why the 51-point projection ignores last year entirely. Even as the third option his aDOT 12.7 role keeps big weeks live; floor is a 60% snap rotation piece. Sleeper: start taking him round 12, two-plus rounds before ADP.

hollywood brown.verdict: 138 points and 74 targets last year in a real role; new Philly situation is the only unknown.
hollywood brown.report: Moderate volume, fair efficiency (1.86 pts/tgt, 7.9 yds/tgt) on 74 targets and 8.1 PPG — a genuine WR3 season after a lost 2024. No advanced usage or Eagles depth chart is available, so I'm inferring role from the 2025 snap-heavy target count; a crowded Philly passing tree caps him. Ceiling is a 100-target field-stretcher, floor is a 35-snap rotation body if the target tree stays top-heavy.

andrei iosivas.verdict: 76% snaps behind Chase and Higgins — the best contingent-target profile at this ADP.
andrei iosivas.report: Modest volume, modest efficiency: 10.2% target share, 0.24 WOPR, 1.55 pts/tgt in 2025 after a 120-point 2024 — that dip was TD regression, not lost snaps (76%). He is locked in as the WR3, so any Higgins absence hands him a 20%+ share overnight. Floor is the 5 PPG he just posted; ceiling is 130-140 if Cincinnati's targets ever open. Sleeper worth a round-13 pick as a bye-week/contingency stash.

devaughn vele.verdict: 13.3% share, 0.33 WOPR and 1.87 rec EPA/g when healthy — efficiency waiting on volume.
devaughn vele.report: Low volume, strong efficiency quadrant: in nine games he ran a 13.3% target share, 18% air-yards share and 1.87 receiving EPA per game, the best per-snap marks in this tier. The problem is the depth chart — Olave plus rookie Jordyn Tyson pushes him to the fourth slot at a 50% snap rate. Ceiling is 100+ targets if injuries hit ahead; floor is the 3.9 PPG scatter of 2025. Round-14 sleeper on efficiency alone.

kendrick bourne.verdict: 10.8% share with 1.47 rec EPA/g and 27 first downs — quietly productive third option in Arizona.
kendrick bourne.report: Moderate volume, good efficiency: 53 targets, 10.4 yds/tgt, 1.47 receiving EPA per game and 57% snaps on a team where Harrison and Wilson soak up the primary looks. A ninth-year slot man has little breakout equity, so the ceiling is roughly the 92 points he just scored plus TD variance. Floor is a rotational 40-target season if Arizona leans younger. Bench depth, not a target.

marvin mims jr..verdict: Big-play/return specialist whose 9.9% target share caps him unless Denver's tree thins out.
marvin mims jr..report: Low volume, boom efficiency: 51 targets and 12 carries with a 0.22 WOPR — a designed-touch player, not a route-runner, and 2024's 130 points came on the same volume via explosives. Denver's room now has Sutton, Waddle and Franklin ahead, so the depth chart argues against target growth. Ceiling is 120 on gadget usage and returns; floor is the 5.5 PPG scatter with an 8.6 stdev in 2024 showing how spiky it is.

kavontae turpin.verdict: 6.9% target share but 10.4 yds/tgt and 17 carries — pure gadget spike, no weekly floor.
kavontae turpin.report: Low volume, strong efficiency: 35% snaps, 0.16 WOPR, yet 2.22 pts/tgt and 1.11 receiving EPA per game on 38 targets plus 17 rushes. Behind Lamb and Pickens the target path is closed, so his value is manufactured touches and return equity. Ceiling is the 104 points of 2024 with a couple of long scores; floor is 3 PPG weeks. Week 14 bye then a soft wk17 Giants matchup is a minor plus.

demario douglas.verdict: 1.76 rec EPA/g on 26% snaps — efficient but buried behind A.J. Brown in New England.
demario douglas.report: Low volume, excellent efficiency: 9.7 yds/tgt, 2.08 pts/tgt and 1.76 receiving EPA per game, but only a 26% snap share after an 87-target 2024. The role collapse is the story — the arrival of A.J. Brown plus Doubs and Boutte leaves him fourth. Ceiling is a return to 80 targets if slot work reopens; floor is the 46-target rotation he just had. Tough wk15 at KC playoff draw.

joshua palmer.verdict: Halved from 107 to 52 points and now the WR3 in Buffalo — volume is trending the wrong way.
joshua palmer.report: Low volume, poor efficiency: 37 targets, 1.41 pts/tgt and 3.1 PPG, down from 65 targets in 2024, with no advanced usage given — I'm inferring a reduced role from the raw target drop. DJ Moore, Shakir and Coleman all sit ahead. Ceiling is 60-70 targets in a high-scoring Buffalo offense if injuries hit; floor is single-digit weekly relevance. Deep bench only.

jaylin lane.verdict: 13.3 aDOT rookie with 36% snaps behind McLaurin — cheap dart, but the EPA says not yet.
jaylin lane.report: Low volume, poor efficiency: 8.3% target share, 0.21 WOPR and -0.38 receiving EPA per game across a 36% snap rookie year with just 10 first downs. The vertical role (13.3 aDOT) means his weeks are TD-or-bust. Washington's room behind McLaurin is soft enough that a year-two jump in snaps is realistic, which is the whole ceiling case. Floor is the 2.9 PPG he posted; leave him on waivers in most 12-team formats.

jahan dotson.verdict: 15.4 aDOT and -1.00 EPA/g on 8.3% share — the deep-shot decoy role has no fantasy floor.
jahan dotson.report: Low volume, poor efficiency quadrant: 36 targets, 1.39 pts/tgt, -1.00 receiving EPA per game and only 10 first downs at a 57% snap share. Two straight seasons under 3.1 PPG make the trend clear. Atlanta's tree runs through London with Branch developing behind him, so a target bump needs an injury. Ceiling is 90 if he inherits the WR2 job; floor is roster-cut territory.

kevin coleman jr..verdict: Rookie into the league's thinnest WR room — Theo Wease as WR1 is an opening worth a dart.
kevin coleman jr..report: No usage data at all, so this is an opportunity bet, not a production bet. Miami's depth chart — Wease, Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas, Reagor — is the weakest listed here, meaning a rookie who wins camp reps could see real target share by midseason. Ceiling is a 70-target WR3 line; floor is inactive. Sleeper only in deep or best-ball formats: round 15 or later, and only after the preseason snap reports confirm a role.

kalif raymond.verdict: 2.23 pts/tgt on a 5.6 aDOT dink role — efficient, but 30 targets is the whole business.
kalif raymond.report: Low volume, strong efficiency: 6.0% target share, 0.12 WOPR, yet 9.6 yds/tgt, 6.5 yards after contact per rush and 1.01 receiving EPA per game — a real yards-after-catch weapon on tiny usage. At 10 years in and fourth behind Odunze and Burden, volume will not come. Ceiling is 85 points; floor near zero on any week Chicago plays from ahead. Wk15 at Buffalo is a bad playoff draw.

nick westbrook-ikhine.verdict: 2024's 136 points were nine TDs of noise; 5.2% share and 4.5 yds/tgt in 2025 is the truth.
nick westbrook-ikhine.report: Low volume, poor efficiency: 20 targets, 0.99 pts/tgt, 5.5 aDOT, 0.11 WOPR — a total collapse from the touchdown-fueled 2024 line. That 2024 season is exactly the kind of TD-dependent spike that does not repeat, and Indianapolis has Pierce and Downs plus Burks ahead of or level with him. Ceiling requires red-zone luck to strike twice; floor is irrelevance. Fade.

luke mccaffrey.verdict: 3.42 pts/tgt on 15 targets is noise, not a signal — sixth on the Commanders' depth chart.
luke mccaffrey.report: Low volume, apparently strong efficiency (13.5 yds/tgt, 1.05 EPA/g), but a 15-target sample over nine games is too small to trust and the 6.8% target share and 32% snaps are the real story. He sits behind McLaurin, Williams, Brown, Jefferson and Lane. Ceiling is a slot promotion to 55 targets; floor is a healthy scratch. Watch camp, don't draft.

tutu atwell.verdict: 20.1 aDOT on 15 targets and sixth on the Miami chart — a lottery ticket, nothing more.
tutu atwell.report: Low volume, boom-or-bust efficiency: 4.9% target share, 0.14 WOPR, 12.8 yds/tgt at a 20.1 aDOT across eight games — pure deep-shot usage. His 2024 (62 targets, 99 points) shows the ceiling if volume returns, but he's listed sixth in a room he has to climb. Floor is the 1.8 PPG he just posted. Only worth a look if Miami's camp shakes out in his favor.

skyler bell.verdict: Rookie fifth on a Bills chart with Moore, Shakir, Palmer and Coleman ahead — no path yet.
skyler bell.report: No professional usage data, so this is a pure situation read: Buffalo's offense scores enough to support a third receiver, but Bell is listed fifth and would need two players ahead of him to fall. Ceiling is a late-season role in a high-total offense; floor is zero snaps. No sleeper badge — the opportunity ahead of him is not open, only theoretically openable.

cyrus allen.verdict: KC rookie behind Rice and Worthy — great offense, no snaps, and no data to argue otherwise.
cyrus allen.report: No 2025 data; the case is entirely environmental. Kansas City's passing volume makes any promoted receiver useful, but Rice and Worthy own the target tree and Allen is the fifth slot listed. Ceiling is 60-70 points as an injury replacement in a good offense; floor is inactive weeks. Bye week 5 and a fine wk15 draw versus New England are irrelevant until he plays.

ashton dulin.verdict: 2.7% target share and 21% snaps across seven seasons — special-teamer priced as a WR.
ashton dulin.report: Very low volume, misleadingly good efficiency: 10 targets, 15.8 aDOT and 10.6 yds/tgt produce shiny rates on a sample that means nothing, with a 0.07 WOPR the honest number. Fourth on Indy's depth chart behind Pierce, Downs and Westbrook-Ikhine at age-30-plus experience. Ceiling is 55 points on a couple of deep scores; floor is zero. Undraftable in 12-team leagues.

bryce lance.verdict: Fifth on the Saints chart behind Olave, Tyson, Means and Vele — name value, no path.
bryce lance.report: No usage data and the worst depth-chart position in this group: four receivers listed ahead of him including a rookie the team invested in and Vele's efficiency profile. New Orleans is also unlikely to support four fantasy-relevant wideouts. Ceiling requires multiple injuries; floor is a practice-squad-adjacent role. Deep dynasty only, not a 2026 redraft asset.

jordan whittington.verdict: 41% snaps but 5.1% target share and 6.8 aDOT — a blocker-first WR3 in a room with Nacua and Adams.
jordan whittington.report: Low volume, poor efficiency — the fade quadrant. Two straight years of shrinking output (3.1 to 2.1 PPG) despite decent snap share tells you the Rams use him for blocking, not routes: 5.1% target share, 0.10 WOPR, 3.8% air-yards share. Nacua and Adams eat the target pie and Mumpfield is behind him. Floor is zero fantasy relevance; ceiling only opens on a Nacua or Adams injury.

zavion thomas.verdict: Rookie WR5 in Chicago behind Odunze and Burden with no route path — projection is a placeholder.
zavion thomas.report: No NFL usage data at all, so I'm inferring from depth chart alone: fifth in a room with Rome Odunze and Luther Burden already locking the primary target shares. Ceiling requires two injuries ahead of him plus a special-teams-to-offense promotion. Floor is inactive weeks. Tough playoff draw (@BUF, GB, DET) even if he did emerge. Waiver-wire name, not a draft pick.

odell beckham jr..verdict: 1.1 PPG on 18 targets in his last measured season and no depth-chart slot — a name, not an asset.
odell beckham jr..report: Last real usage was 0.81 points per target and 3.1 yards per target across 13 games, then a blank season: that is low volume AND poor efficiency, the clearest fade quadrant here. No Sleeper depth match means no defined role behind Nabers, Mooney and Slayton in New York. Floor is not making the roster; ceiling is a handful of TD-dependent spike weeks. Do not draft.

devontez walker.verdict: 24.5 aDOT, 4.7 pts/target, 2.24 rec EPA/g on eight targets — tiny sample, huge per-snap edge.
devontez walker.report: Textbook low-volume, elite-efficiency breakout profile: 8.8% air-yards share on a 4.3% target share means Baltimore only uses him as the deep shot, and it worked (17.0 yards per target, 2.24 rec EPA/g). Floor is the 25% snap share repeating and 2.2 PPG. Ceiling needs a Bateman or Flowers absence, then he's an every-week boom threat in a top offense. Sleeper: take him in the last two rounds as a bench dart.

malachi fields.verdict: Rookie sixth on the Giants depth chart; the Nabers-Mooney-Slayton-Austin wall leaves nothing.
malachi fields.report: No usage data exists, so the depth chart is all I have: LWR #6 behind Nabers, Mooney, Slayton and Austin, four players who already command targets. Even a strong camp only moves him to the fourth WR in a run-lean offense. Floor is healthy scratch; ceiling is a late-season injury-driven role with double-digit weeks. Playoff slate (@DET, @DAL) is no help. Watch list only.

xavier hutchinson.verdict: Quadrupled his output to 98 points on 11.2% target share and 57% snaps — real role, real trajectory.
xavier hutchinson.report: Best usage trend in this group: 26 targets to 57, 1.4 to 5.8 PPG, with a legitimate 0.26 WOPR, 10.2 aDOT and 0.81 rec EPA/g — moderate volume with acceptable efficiency and 21 first downs. The catch is a stacked Houston room (Collins, Higgins, Dell, Noel), which caps the ceiling unless injuries hit, and @PHI/@GB is a brutal playoff close. Floor is the WR5 snaps he already holds.

dont'e thornton jr..verdict: 24.9% air-yards share is real, but -1.09 rec EPA/g and 10 catches on 30 targets is the wrong kind of volume.
dont'e thornton jr..report: Low volume with genuinely poor efficiency: a 33% catch rate, 4.5 yards per target and -1.09 rec EPA per game despite a 16.6 aDOT. The deep role is his (0.32 WOPR is respectable), but that role is exactly what gets taken away when the throws don't land. Floor is 20-something points again; ceiling is TD-variance regression to two or three 20-point spikes. No Sleeper depth match adds role uncertainty.

olamide zaccheaus.verdict: 14.7% target share is the volume, but 4.8 yds/target and -0.27 EPA/g is volume at risk of vanishing.
olamide zaccheaus.report: High-ish volume, poor efficiency — the warning quadrant. He led this group in target share (14.7%, 0.30 WOPR) yet fell from 112 to 85 points because the throws are shallow (7.1 aDOT) and unproductive. Atlanta added Branch and Dotson behind London, so his 54% snap share is the thing most likely to erode. Floor is a PPR-only 4-5 PPG grinder; ceiling needs a London absence.

chimere dike.verdict: 126 points, 74 targets, 17 games as a rookie — the most proven role in this group, even in a crowded room.
chimere dike.report: Moderate volume with mediocre efficiency (13.9% target share, 0.31 WOPR, but 5.7 yards per target and 0.09 rec EPA/g), which means the opportunity is real and the production must come from more of it. Tennessee then imported Tate and Ridley alongside Wan'Dale, so the 59% snap share is genuinely contested. Floor is a rotational 3 PPG; ceiling is 2025 volume plus TD normalization. Sleeper worth a final-round pick.

isaiah bond.verdict: 21.4% air-yards share on a 9.3% target share — the field-stretcher role exists, the production hasn't.
isaiah bond.report: Low volume, mediocre efficiency: 18 catches on 44 targets with a 17.1 aDOT and -0.05 rec EPA/g means he's the vertical option on a bad passing offense. The 48% snap share is a foothold, and Cleveland's room (Jeudy, Concepcion, Boston, Tillman) is beatable but he's listed sixth. Floor is another 55-point season; ceiling is a QB upgrade turning those deep looks into 700 yards. Bench flier only.

konata mumpfield.verdict: 32% snaps, 6.2% target share and -0.88 rec EPA/g behind Nacua and Adams — no path, no efficiency.
konata mumpfield.report: Low volume and poor efficiency, the fade quadrant: 10 catches on 23 targets, 4.0 yards per target, negative receiving EPA despite a 12.9 aDOT that should produce chunk plays. He's fourth in the Rams room with Whittington also competing for the leftovers. Floor is single-digit season points; ceiling requires Adams missing significant time. Nothing in the data recommends a pick.

mack hollins.verdict: 0.39 WOPR and 1.94 rec EPA/g were the group's best — but that was elsewhere; NE lists him fifth behind A.J. Brown.
mack hollins.report: Genuinely good volume plus efficiency last year: 16.2% target share, 20.6% air-yards share, 13.1 aDOT, 28 first downs, 68% snaps. The problem is entirely situational — New England's room now runs A.J. Brown, Doubs, Boutte, Douglas ahead of him, and he's a ninth-year player. Camp headline is a generic roundup with nothing on him, so I weight the depth chart. Floor is 3 PPG; ceiling is the same efficiency on half the routes.

brenen thompson.verdict: Rookie fourth in a Chargers room where McConkey, Johnston and Harris already split the targets.
brenen thompson.report: No professional usage to evaluate, so this is pure depth-chart math: McConkey owns the high-value slot work, Johnston and Harris hold the outside jobs, and Lambert-Smith is fighting for the same scraps. Floor is inactive; ceiling is a late-season deep-threat role if injuries clear two men. Week 7 bye and a Week 15 SF matchup add nothing. Leave him on the wire.

keandre lambert-smith.verdict: 19% snaps, 12 targets, 3 first downs — a 17.6 aDOT with nothing to show for it.
keandre lambert-smith.report: Low volume, poor efficiency: five catches on 12 targets, 4.3 yards per target, -0.49 rec EPA/g. The deep aDOT is the only interesting number and it produced no explosive output. He's fifth in a Chargers room and now has rookie Brenen Thompson pushing from behind. Floor is a zero; ceiling is a 25-catch complementary season if McConkey or Harris misses time. Not draftable in 12-team leagues.

kyle williams.verdict: 4.10 pts/touch and 10.0 yds/target on 21 looks — the best efficiency-per-opportunity dart in this tier.
kyle williams.report: Classic low-volume, strong-efficiency profile: 5.0% target share and 31% snaps, yet 2.34 points per target, 19.0 aDOT and 0.70 rec EPA/g. That is a player who only needs routes. The blocker is New England's room — A.J. Brown, Doubs, Boutte, Douglas all ahead — so the opening has to come from injury or Hollins fading. Floor is 40-50 points; sleeper worth a final-round stash if the camp reports move him up.

tez johnson.verdict: 92 points on 44 targets: 2.10 pts/target and 1.09 rec EPA/g is the efficiency profile that scales with volume.
tez johnson.report: Low-to-moderate volume with clearly strong efficiency — 9.2% target share and 47% snaps produced 5.4 PPG, 16 first downs and positive receiving EPA, plus seven carries for gadget usage. Tampa's room is deep (Egbuka, Godwin, McMillan) and he's listed seventh, which is the real cap; the camp headline is generic and tells me nothing. Floor is his 2025 line; ceiling is a Godwin absence turning him into a 90-target slot. Sleeper, last round.

jimmy horn jr..verdict: Gadget usage only: 15 targets, 2.7% air-yards share, 6.0 aDOT — a returner with touches, not a receiver role.
jimmy horn jr..report: Low volume with fine but meaningless efficiency (7.2 yards per target, 8.6 yards per carry on eight carries, positive rush EPA). A 2.7% air-yards share says Carolina never throws him the ball downfield, which caps any PPR ceiling regardless of snaps. No Sleeper depth match makes the role even murkier. Floor is a handful of points; ceiling is a return-TD-inflated 60-point season.

mitchell tinsley.verdict: 25% snaps and 8 catches on 24 targets — a 33% catch rate is not a foundation to build on.
mitchell tinsley.report: Low volume, poor efficiency: 4.8 yards per target and six first downs across eight games of usage, though the 13.8% air-yards share and 14.8 aDOT show Cincinnati at least aimed him downfield. No Sleeper depth match means no confirmed role in a room that funnels everything to its top two. Floor is inactive weeks; ceiling is a 40-catch WR3 season only if the depth chart collapses.

calvin austin iii.verdict: 25.5% air-yards share and 0.37 WOPR is real target equity, but the efficiency fell off and NYG is crowded.
calvin austin iii.report: Moderate volume with declining efficiency — 7.0 to 5.1 PPG, 2.05 to 1.57 points per target, and -0.30 rec EPA/g despite the biggest air-yards share in this group. That is the warning quadrant: he was fed and didn't convert. Now he's behind Nabers, Mooney and Slayton in New York, so the 54% snap share likely shrinks. Floor is a bench WR; ceiling is 70 targets of deep work if Slayton or Mooney sits.

jalen royals.verdict: Two games of usage in a Mahomes offense — pure lottery ticket behind Rice and Worthy, but the lottery is KC.
jalen royals.report: Almost no sample: 19% snaps over seven games, 5.0% target share, -0.81 rec EPA/g on a 7.3 aDOT — nothing to interpret except that he wasn't trusted. The bull case is entirely environmental: fourth in a Kansas City room where the top two have injury histories and the offense supports three fantasy-relevant pass catchers. Floor is irrelevance; ceiling needs a Rice or Worthy absence. Cheap stash, no more.

elic ayomanor.verdict: Rookie-year WOPR 0.50 and 32.5% air-yards share at WR170 price; room got crowded, but the alpha reps were real.
elic ayomanor.report: High volume, poor efficiency quadrant: 89 targets, 18.5% target share, 32.5% air-yards share and 81% snaps as a rookie, but 1.31 pts/target and -0.60 rec EPA/g explain why Tennessee imported Tate, Ridley and Robinson. Floor is a 55-target WR4 squeezed out of the rotation. Ceiling is the deep-ball share sticking with better QB play for a 120-target, WR3 season. Sleeper worth a last-round flier — I'd take him by round 13 ahead of every other name here.

tyrell shavers.verdict: Best per-snap efficiency in the group (1.12 EPA/g, 13.0 aDOT) but PUP and fifth in line in Buffalo.
tyrell shavers.report: Low volume, strong efficiency: 7.7% target share and 12.3% air-yards share on 40% snaps produced 10.7 yds/target and +1.12 rec EPA/g — the profile of a player who only needs opportunity. The problem is the depth chart (Moore, Shakir, Palmer, Coleman) and a PUP designation that could cost camp and early weeks. Floor is a healthy scratch; ceiling is Buffalo's field-stretcher on a top offense. Watch the injury report before spending anything.

xavier smith.verdict: 1.37 rec EPA/g and 12.6 yds/target on 21% snaps — the cleanest low-volume, high-efficiency case here.
xavier smith.report: Classic breakout-candidate quadrant: only 24 targets and a 4.6% share, but 16.9 aDOT, 12.6 yds/target and an elite +1.37 rec EPA/g mean the Rams got real value every time they used him. Blocked by Nacua and an aging Adams, so the floor is 25 targets again. The ceiling arrives only if Adams misses time, at which point he's the vertical complement in a high-volume passing offense. Genuine sleeper — last-round dart, round 15 or later.

isaiah williams.verdict: 36% snaps and an 8.8% target share in a thin Jets room, but a 3.4 aDOT caps everything.
isaiah williams.report: Middling volume, middling efficiency: 36 targets on 36% snaps with 1.63 pts/target and just 5.4 yds/target off a 3.4 aDOT — screen and check-down work with no air-yards equity (5.0% share). The Jets room behind Garrett Wilson is genuinely soft (Mitchell, Cooper), so a Wilson absence could push him to 6-7 targets a week in PPR. Floor is the same 4 PPG role. Not a ceiling play, just a contingency body.

greg dortch.verdict: Reliable 34%-snap slot body in a great offense, but ASB and Williams leave nothing to inherit.
greg dortch.report: Low volume, adequate efficiency: 6.8% target share, 1.8 aDOT, 1.2% air-yards share — pure underneath filler at 2.09 pts/touch, and his PPG fell from 5.3 to 4.4 as Detroit's rotation firmed up. Seven-year vet WR4 behind St. Brown, Jameson Williams and TeSlaa; the target tree above him is immovable. Floor and ceiling are close together, which is the whole problem for a bench spot. Draftable only in deep best-ball.

colbie young.verdict: Rookie with no data, but the Bengals offense is the best environment any WR5 in this group has.
colbie young.report: No NFL usage to interpret, so I'm inferring from situation: Cincinnati throws at a top-of-league rate, and Chase plus Higgins draw enough coverage that the third and fourth options see soft looks. He is behind both plus Iosivas, so the realistic floor is inactive most weeks. Ceiling requires a Higgins injury, which is not a plan. No sleeper badge — there is no efficiency or opportunity evidence yet, only a good address.

malik benson.verdict: Undrafted-profile rookie fifth in a Raiders room that already has four ahead of him.
malik benson.report: Zero usage data, so this is a projection off depth chart alone: Tucker, Nailor, Bech and Thornton are all ahead, and Las Vegas's passing volume does not support five fantasy-relevant receivers. The ceiling case is a camp riser who wins the vertical role Thornton held; nothing in the reports given supports that yet. Floor is inactive. Waiver-wire name, not a draft pick.

barion brown.verdict: Explosive rookie return type buried as the eighth Saints WR — opportunity math is prohibitive.
barion brown.report: No NFL volume or efficiency data exists, and the depth chart says SWR #8 behind Olave, Tyson, Means and Vele. Even an injury or two only moves him to the fringe of the rotation in a low-volume offense. Ceiling is a kick-return-driven big week or two; floor is no snaps on offense. Nothing in the data supports a sleeper tag despite the athletic profile.

bo melton.verdict: 17.1 aDOT decoy on 10% snaps behind four better Packers receivers — fade.
bo melton.report: Low volume, poor efficiency: 4.0% target share, 13 targets, -0.20 rec EPA/g and just 24 points across a full season, essentially unchanged from 2024's 23. The deep aDOT is the only interesting number and it produced six first downs. Watson, Reed, Golden and Savion Williams are all ahead of him. Floor and ceiling both round to roster clutter in a 12-team league.

derius davis.verdict: Return specialist with 0 first downs and a 0.02 WOPR on 11% snaps; McConkey owns the slot.
derius davis.report: Low volume, poor efficiency: 0.9% target share, 0.02 WOPR, negative rec and rush EPA, and zero first downs generated in 11 games. His 2024 line (17 targets, 12 carries, 40 points) is the realistic ceiling of the gadget role. Sixth on the depth chart behind McConkey, Johnston and Harris in a room that just does not need him on offense. Not a fantasy asset.

anthony gould.verdict: 0.5% target share, -1.0 aDOT, zero first downs — no offensive role to project forward.
anthony gould.report: Lowest-volume, lowest-efficiency profile in the group: a 0.01 WOPR, negative air-yards share and no first downs across 11 games at 9% snaps. He is sixth in an Indianapolis room led by Pierce and Downs, so even two injuries barely move him. Floor is inactive; ceiling is a return-game role with occasional jet sweeps. No draft consideration in any format.

ben skowronek.verdict: Six targets in a full season; the pretty per-target rates are noise on a blocking specialist.
ben skowronek.report: A 1.4% target share and 0.04 WOPR make the 2.82 pts/target and +0.34 EPA/g meaningless small-sample artifacts — he plays 15% of snaps as a blocker. Pittsburgh added Metcalf and Pittman with Bernard and Wilson also ahead, so no target growth is coming. Floor is one point a week; ceiling is a red-zone fluke score. This is the clearest fade of the twelve.

trey mcbride.verdict: Elite volume plus elite efficiency: 27.9% target share, 91% snaps, 18.6 PPG — the safest TE1 on the board.
trey mcbride.report: High volume + strong efficiency, the expensive safe quadrant: 169 targets, 27.9% target share, 0.59 WOPR and 91% snaps produced 18.6 PPG and 4.28 rec EPA/game. He improved on 2024's 14.7 PPG with the same role, so the trend points forward, not to regression. Floor is protected by short-aDOT reception volume; ceiling needs only a normal TD rate. Zero real TE competition and a soft NYJ/@NO/LV playoff run.

brock bowers.verdict: 2024's 263-point form on 153 targets is the true baseline; 2025's dip came with only 12 healthy games of usage.
brock bowers.report: Advanced data covers 12 games versus 17 logged, so 2025's 10.4 PPG reflects a compromised season, not lost talent — he still held a 23.4% target share, 25% air-yards share and 86% snaps. High volume with 2.05 pts/target keeps him in the safe quadrant when healthy, and 2024's 263 points is the realistic ceiling. Floor risk is another banged-up year plus Mayer siphoning inline snaps.

colston loveland.verdict: Low-volume, high-efficiency rookie year: 2.80 pts/touch and 9.1 aDOT on only 65% snaps — the classic breakout profile.
colston loveland.report: 165 points on a 16.6% target share and 65% snap rate is the breakout quadrant: efficiency (2.01 pts/target, 8.7 yds/target, 2.97 rec EPA/g) well ahead of opportunity. Any move toward an 85% snap share and 110 targets makes him a top-four TE. The floor is that Kmet keeps eating blocking-down snaps and the target share stalls near 17%. Playoff slate is rough: @BUF, GB, DET.

tyler warren.verdict: 112 targets and 84% snaps as a rookie with a tiny 4.7 weekly stdev — the most stable young TE floor here.
tyler warren.report: High volume, modest efficiency: 21.5% target share and 84% snaps, but a 5.4 aDOT, 14.7% air-yards share and 0.93 rec EPA/g mean he lives on short throws. That produces a remarkably steady 11.1 PPG with league-low variance, ideal as a set-and-forget TE1. The ceiling requires more downfield or red-zone work, which the air-yards share does not yet promise. No competition behind him at all.

kyle pitts sr..verdict: 118 targets and 211 points finally matched the talent, but the 9.6 weekly stdev says boom-bust, not stable.
kyle pitts sr..report: The 2025 leap was volume-driven: targets jumped 74 to 118 and points 131 to 211, with efficiency flat (1.79 vs 1.77 pts/target) — so the gain is repeatable only if the target share holds. Advanced usage is missing, so I'm leaning on raw targets and 88 catches as the opportunity read. Ceiling is a 120-target TE1; floor is the 2024 version if Atlanta's passing volume dips. Weekly variance is the real cost.

harold fannin jr..verdict: Volume is real (21.8% share) but 0.09 rec EPA/g is the warning sign that the targets aren't productive ones.
harold fannin jr..report: High volume, poor efficiency — the quadrant where the touches themselves are at risk. 107 targets and a 21.8% target share at a 6.0 aDOT yielded just 6.8 yds/target and essentially zero receiving EPA per game. He'll keep catching passes, so the PPR floor is fine, but the ceiling needs Cleveland's offense and his yards-per-target to both improve. Playoff draw of @NYG/@BAL/IND is mixed.

sam laporta.verdict: 9 games, 91% snaps and 4.05 rec EPA/g — elite per-snap play; the only question is whether he stays on the field.
sam laporta.report: Low volume, strong efficiency: just 49 targets in nine healthy games, yet 2.18 pts/target, 10.0 yds/target and 91% snap share. Full health at 2024's 83-target pace with 2025 efficiency is a 190-210 point season, and Detroit's offense supports more. Floor is another missed month — he's now missed significant time and the 7.4 weekly stdev shows TD reliance. No TE behind him threatens the role.

george kittle.verdict: Best efficiency at the position (2.34 pts/tgt) but on PUP at 33 with a brutal @LAC/@KC/PHI playoff run.
george kittle.report: Low volume, elite efficiency: 69 targets in 11 games, 2.34 pts/target, 9.1 yds/target, 4.21 rec EPA/g and 81% snaps. When he plays he's a top-five TE, as 2024's 237 points showed. The PUP designation is the verifiable fact that caps the floor — games missed, not per-game decline, is the risk, plus age-33 attrition. Discounted ADP near 90 is fair rather than a bargain.

tucker kraft.verdict: Activated off PUP under nine months post-ACL; 3.55 pts/touch and 4.89 rec EPA/g is the best per-target profile here.
tucker kraft.report: The July 31 activation is the freshest verifiable fact and removes most of the availability discount at an ADP of 109. Low volume, elite efficiency: 44 targets in 8 games but 2.66 pts/target, 11.1 yds/target and 4.89 rec EPA/g on 86% snaps. Sleeper — the opening is a full 70-90 target season in Green Bay's only established TE role; start taking him in round 8. Floor is a slow ramp and re-injury.

dallas goedert.verdict: 185 points on 82 targets was TD-fueled (3.09 pts/touch on 7.2 yds/target) — real role, thin margin for error.
dallas goedert.report: Solid volume for a Philadelphia TE — 20.8% target share, 85% snaps, 0.42 WOPR — with efficiency inflated by scoring: 2.26 pts/target against only 7.2 yards per target. Regress the TDs and the 2024 line (104 points) is closer than the ceiling. Ceiling is a repeat if red-zone looks hold in a run-heavy offense. Age 8 plus Stowers behind him adds mild snap risk; playoff slate is neutral.

travis kelce.verdict: Two straight 11-plus PPG seasons on 20% target share; boring, stable, and finally priced at round 9.
travis kelce.report: High volume, average efficiency: 108 targets, 20% target share, 82% snaps and 46 first downs with 2.38 rec EPA/g — the role is fully intact and the 6.2 weekly stdev makes him a plug-and-play TE1. Efficiency actually improved from 2024 (1.47 to 1.79 pts/target). Age 37 is the obvious cliff risk and the floor assumes a mid-season fade or a missed stretch. Gray is a nuisance, not a threat.

jake ferguson.verdict: 82 catches gives a real PPR floor, but a 4.7 aDOT and 8.9% air-yards share cap the upside hard.
jake ferguson.report: High volume, poor per-target value: 102 targets and 82 receptions at only 5.9 yds/target with a 0.31 WOPR and 67% snaps. That's a reception-driven floor and a TD-dependent ceiling — 1.84 pts/target came mostly from scoring, since 2024's identical target count yielded just 104 points. Consistency is good (6.9 stdev). Little TE competition, but Dallas's WRs own the downfield share.

mark andrews.verdict: Snap share fell to 62% and EPA to zero, but the TD-rebound bet is cheap at ADP 120.
mark andrews.report: 2025 was a genuine efficiency collapse — 1.87 pts/target and 0.09 rec EPA/g on a 17.1% share and only 62% snaps, versus 2.74 pts/target in 2024. RotoWire's healthy-QB rebound thesis is the right read on ambiguous data: his volume never cratered, his touchdowns did. Sleeper from round 10 on, with the opening being red-zone looks returning. Floor is a 62%-snap committee TE; @PIT/CLE/@CIN playoffs are tough.

hunter henry.verdict: 179 points, 17.4% share and 79% snaps for an ADP of 141 — the cheapest starting-caliber TE here.
hunter henry.report: Middle quadrant done well: 87 targets, 17.4% target share, 8.2 aDOT, 2.22 rec EPA/g and 42 first downs across a full 17 games. He has improved his per-target scoring two years running and has no TE behind him. Sleeper — the value is purely price, a top-12 TE finish available in round 12. Floor is age-related snap erosion or New England adding a pass-catcher; @KC/@NYJ/DEN playoffs are unfriendly.

juwan johnson.verdict: 180 points, 17.7% share, 4.7 weekly stdev — a steady starting TE going 160th overall.
juwan johnson.report: Balanced quadrant: 102 targets, 17.7% target share, 75% snaps, 8.7 yds/target and 2.07 rec EPA/g, with the second-lowest weekly variance in this group. FantasyPros' staff call matches the data — the target share is real and repeatable. Sleeper worth taking in round 12-13 as a TE1 at TE2 cost. The floor risk is Noah Fant cutting into two-TE snaps and New Orleans' offense capping passing volume.

t.j. hockenson.verdict: Volume without value: 15.9% share, 5.0 aDOT, 10.2% air-yards share — the QB-upgrade case isn't in the usage data.
t.j. hockenson.report: He is in the high-volume, poor-efficiency quadrant that warns the role can shrink: 66 targets for 6.6 PPG, 1.71 pts/target and a 0.31 WOPR despite 78% snaps. RotoWire's QB-upgrade thesis is plausible but the aDOT and air-yards share say he's being used as a checkdown, which better quarterbacking doesn't automatically fix — so I withhold the sleeper badge. Josh Oliver limits the snap ceiling.

dalton kincaid.verdict: 37% snaps yet 2.57 pts/target and a 20.7% air-yards share — pure opportunity play at a round-12 price.
dalton kincaid.report: Textbook low-volume, high-efficiency breakout candidate: only 49 targets on a 37% snap share, but 11.7 yds/target, 9.5 aDOT, 20.7% air-yards share and 3.28 rec EPA/g. If Buffalo restores him to a 70% snap role he's a top-eight TE. Sleeper from round 11 — the opening is Knox and Hawes holding blocking snaps that could shift. Floor is the same part-time role, which is barely startable.

isaiah likely.verdict: New team, clear TE1 depth slot, but 2025 was a 12% target share and 3.6 PPG — buy the role, not the production.
isaiah likely.report: Low volume and mediocre efficiency in Baltimore: 37 targets, 12% target share, 0.26 WOPR and 56% snaps for 62 points. The 2024 line (124 points, 2.13 pts/target) shows what he does with even moderate opportunity, and the Giants list him ahead of Theo Johnson. Sleeper only at his round-11 price and only on the depth-chart change; if Johnson wins snaps back this is a wasted pick.

kenyon sadiq.verdict: Rookie hybrid with no NFL usage data and Mason Taylor already in the building — ESPN's projection is faith, not evidence.
kenyon sadiq.report: There is no volume or efficiency data at all, so the 162-point projection rests entirely on the listed TE1 slot and the hybrid WR/TE role ESPN describes. The crowd chatter contains no camp snap counts or beat-writer depth-chart news — the only mention is a stale pre-draft mock, so it moves price, not evaluation. Ceiling is a 70-target rookie season; floor is a 30% snap situational role behind Taylor.

terrance ferguson.verdict: 18.6 aDOT and 4.34 pts/touch on 37% snaps — a fun deep-league dart, but the target share was only 6.5%.
terrance ferguson.report: Extreme low volume, intriguing efficiency: 25 targets, 6.5% target share, 0.18 WOPR, yet 2.08 pts/target and an 18.6 aDOT that makes him a big-play red-zone piece. ESPN's opportunity call is reasonable with Higbee aging, but Parkinson and Higbee still split the room, so the path isn't clear. Sleeper only in round 14 or later in TE-premium or deep formats; the floor is functionally zero.

dalton schultz.verdict: Highest-volume TE in the range: 106 targets, 19.1% share, 0.39 WOPR — the safest floor at a TE17 price.
dalton schultz.report: 106 targets, 19.1% target share and a 0.39 WOPR made him a genuine volume TE1; 178 points at 10.5 PPG with a modest 5.5 stdev is the steadiest weekly profile in this group. Quadrant: high volume, modest efficiency (1.68 pts/tgt, 6.2 aDOT), so volume IS the case and the ceiling is capped. Klein/Stover threaten nothing behind him. Playoff draw @PHI, @GB is unfriendly. Value at ADP 168.

brenton strange.verdict: Two-year usage climb with real efficiency: 15.6% share, 0.32 WOPR, 75% snaps, 2.61 rec EPA/g, no competition.
brenton strange.report: Growth in both seasons — 5.4 to 6.9 PPG — behind a 15.6% target share, 0.32 WOPR, 75% snap share and a group-best 2.61 rec EPA/g on 9.0 yds/target. That is the rare good quadrant here: real volume plus above-group efficiency, with Boerkircher and Long offering no threat to the job. Floor is the 6-7 PPG already banked; ceiling is 90-plus targets if Jacksonville concentrates. Start taking him round 13-14.

oronde gadsden.verdict: Best per-target producer in the group as a rookie; Njoku's arrival is the only thing holding the price down.
oronde gadsden.report: 131 points as a rookie on 69 targets — 9.6 yds/target and 1.90 pts/target lead this tier, and the 7.4 weekly stdev says the spike weeks were real, not dink volume. No advanced usage given, so I'm inferring opportunity from raw target count and yards, which point to a low-volume/high-efficiency breakout profile. Njoku's presence caps snaps some, but Njoku's -0.33 EPA/g in 2025 is no rebuttal. SF/KC playoff draw is harsh.

chig okonkwo.verdict: Move to a bare Washington TE room is the opportunity; per-target value is the thing that has to improve.
chig okonkwo.report: Consistent 70-79 targets and 15.0% share two years running, but a 4.6 aDOT, 8.7% air-yards share and 0.75 rec EPA/g mark him mid-volume/low-efficiency — a checkdown asset, not a field-stretcher. The new-team case is legitimate: Bates and Sinnott are non-factors, so 90 targets is on the table with a bigger role. Floor is the same 6-7 PPG dead zone he's lived in. Round 14 dart with a starting job.

pat freiermuth.verdict: 2024's 168-point season is the lure, but 50% snaps and an 11.3% share in 2025 say the role already shrank.
pat freiermuth.report: The trend is the wrong way: 9.9 PPG and 78 targets in 2024 collapsed to 6.7 PPG, 54 targets, an 11.3% share and a 50% snap rate in 2025 as Washington ate into the role. Efficiency held (2.10 pts/tgt), so this is low-volume/decent-efficiency — he needs snaps back, not talent. FantasyPros' sleeper call is priced on the 2024 line; the 2025 usage contradicts it, so no sleeper badge from me. BAL/CAR/TEN playoff slate is workable.

aj barner.verdict: 147 points on a 4.4 aDOT and 7.7% air-yards share is touchdown math, not usage math — regression candidate.
aj barner.report: 77% snaps and 68 targets are real, but 8.7 PPG came from a 2.17 pts/target rate built on a 4.4 aDOT and a tiny 7.7% air-yards share — classic TD-dependent scoring that rarely repeats. Quadrant: moderate volume, inflated efficiency. Arroyo was poor in 2025 (-1.25 EPA/g) so the job is safe, which supports the floor. Ceiling requires the red-zone rate to hold; floor is 6 PPG if it doesn't.

greg dulcich.verdict: THE efficiency-on-low-volume bet: 10.2 yds/tgt, 1.95 EPA/g on 42% snaps in a thin Miami target room.
greg dulcich.report: Only 33 targets over 10 games, but 10.2 yds/target, a 15.4% share and 1.95 rec EPA/g on a 42% snap share is exactly the low-volume/high-efficiency breakout quadrant. The opening is concrete: Kacmarek, Sims and Turner behind him, and Miami's perimeter target competition is thin. Floor is ugly — he has missed time repeatedly and a 42% snap rate is not a job yet. Worth a round 14-15 swing at the ADP.

cade otton.verdict: 94% snaps and a 17.4% share, but 0.21 EPA/g and 1.51 pts/target — the volume itself is at risk.
cade otton.report: Nobody in this group plays more: 94% snap share, 17.4% target share, 81 targets. But 1.51 pts/target, 7.1 yds/target and 0.21 rec EPA/g put him squarely in high-volume/poor-efficiency, the quadrant where the targets get reallocated. PPG has slid 8.3 to 7.2 across two years. Floor is decent because the snaps are guaranteed today; ceiling is limited by a 5.2 aDOT and no red-zone edge. Sharp is the only nibbler.

gunnar helm.verdict: Uncontested TE1 job in year two, but rookie-year 10.7% share and 0.24 EPA/g show nothing yet.
