gunnar helm.report: A full rookie season produced 5.4 PPG on a 10.7% target share, 8.0% air-yards share and 0.24 rec EPA/g — low volume and low efficiency, the fade quadrant on the numbers alone. What keeps him here is the depth chart: Bellinger and Granson are replacement level, so a year-two target bump is cheap to bet on. Playoff slate (IND, @LV, PIT) is fine. Floor is a bench TE; ceiling is a 75-target streamer.

evan engram.verdict: 76 targets produced only 103 points — worst pts/target in the group at 1.35, on 42% of snaps.
evan engram.report: The volume looks fine (76 targets, 13.7% share, 0.31 WOPR) but 1.35 pts/target, 6.1 yds/target and 0.22 rec EPA/g are the weakest conversion here — high-ish volume, poor efficiency, the warning quadrant. A 42% snap share in year nine with Trautman and Adkins around says the workload is already being managed. Floor is a low-end streamer; ceiling needs a target-share jump the age curve argues against.

mike gesicki.verdict: Halved his output as snaps fell to 39%; the 10.0 aDOT is the only reason to care.
mike gesicki.report: 8.3 PPG on 83 targets in 2024 became 4.2 PPG on 42 targets in 2025 as the snap share cratered to 39% with Erick All back — that is a role loss, not variance. The 10.0 aDOT and 13.1% air-yards share mean the few targets are downfield, so spike weeks exist, but 0.37 rec EPA/g says they were rare. Low volume, mediocre efficiency. Only draftable as a bye-week dart in the final rounds.

dawson knox.verdict: Efficient TD scorer (2.12 pts/tgt) but capped behind Kincaid on 11% of targets.
dawson knox.report: 104 points on just 49 targets means 2.12 pts/target and 2.88 pts/touch — good conversion, and 1.09 rec EPA/g on a 6.7 aDOT backs it up. But an 11.0% target share behind Kincaid is a hard ceiling, and the scoring rate is touchdown-leveraged, not volume-leveraged: low volume, good efficiency, no clear path to more. He is a contingency play on a Kincaid absence, nothing more at this price.

colby parkinson.verdict: 130 points on 56 targets was pure red-zone luck; now the TE2 behind Ferguson.
colby parkinson.report: 2.32 pts/target and 3.02 pts/touch on a 4.5% air-yards share and 4.4 aDOT is the loudest touchdown-luck signal in the group — 2024's 3.8 PPG on similar targets is the honest baseline. Low volume, unsustainable efficiency. Ferguson now sits ahead of him with Higbee also in the room, so the 60% snap share should fall. Floor is waiver-wire; ceiling requires an injury ahead of him.

jake tonges.verdict: Real per-snap efficiency (2.03 pts/tgt, 21 first downs on 33% snaps) locked behind Kittle.
jake tonges.report: On a 33% snap share he still produced 93 points, 2.74 pts/touch and 21 first downs with 1.42 rec EPA/g — low volume, strong efficiency, the profile that only needs opportunity. The problem is the opportunity is George Kittle's, and ESPN's 33-point projection reflects that. He is the single best TE handcuff here: if Kittle misses time, Tonges is an instant streamer. Draft only as a final-round contingency.

david njoku.verdict: New team, but arrives as the TE2 behind Gadsden after a -0.33 EPA/g season.
david njoku.report: The two-year slide is steep: 97 targets and 8.7 PPG in 2024 down to 48 targets, 5.1 PPG, a 12.5% share and -0.33 rec EPA/g in 2025 across 11 games. Low volume, negative efficiency — the fade quadrant. Landing in Los Angeles behind a more efficient Gadsden makes the target path worse, not better, and ESPN's 75-point projection agrees. Only a Gadsden injury makes him relevant.

darnell washington.verdict: Blocking-first TE2 with a decent 1.13 EPA/g, but 43 targets is the whole story.
darnell washington.report: Improved to 73 points on 43 targets with a 11.2% share, 11.9% air-yards share and 1.13 rec EPA/g — efficient enough for the volume, and the 57% snap share is mostly blocking work. Low volume, fine efficiency, but Freiermuth still owns the passing-down role even in a down year. The trend is upward two straight seasons, which is the only bull case. Not startable in 12-team PPR without an injury ahead.

michael mayer.verdict: Improved to 74 points but -0.76 rec EPA/g behind Brock Bowers is unplayable volume.
michael mayer.report: 13.7% target share and 62% snaps sound usable until you see -0.76 rec EPA/g, 1.48 pts/target and 4.8 aDOT — moderate volume, clearly negative efficiency, which is the quadrant where the targets go away. Bowers is the entire passing-game funnel in Las Vegas. The 2.2 to 4.3 PPG jump is progress from nothing to little. Pure Bowers handcuff in deep leagues; leave him undrafted otherwise.

elijah arroyo.verdict: 7.9% target share and -1.25 EPA/g as a rookie; the athletic upside has no usage behind it yet.
elijah arroyo.report: 26 targets, a 7.9% share, 0.18 WOPR and -1.25 rec EPA/g over 13 games — low volume and the worst efficiency in this group, the clear fade quadrant. The 8.5 aDOT is the only encouraging number, suggesting a downfield role that could scale. Barner has 77% of the snaps and is not moving without an injury. Year-two leaps happen at TE, but this is a dynasty hold, not a 2026 redraft asset.

ja'tavion sanders.verdict: Went backward in year two: 9.2% share, 8 first downs, 3.2 PPG with Tremble taking work.
ja'tavion sanders.report: Both usage and production declined — 43 to 34 targets, 4.3 to 3.2 PPG, a 9.2% target share, 5.3% air-yards share and just 8 first downs on a 48% snap share. Low volume, poor efficiency, the fade quadrant with no ambiguity. Tremble and Evans are splitting the room and Carolina's passing volume does not support three TEs. There is no realistic 2026 path to weekly startability.

eli stowers.verdict: Rookie with zero NFL data buried behind Dallas Goedert; ESPN's 38-point projection tells the story.
eli stowers.report: No 2025 or 2024 data at all, so there is nothing to interpret on volume or efficiency — I'm working entirely off depth chart and projection. Goedert is the established starter with Calcaterra also ahead in the pass-game pecking order, so snaps in year one project to be situational at best. Rookie TEs almost never produce, and this one has the worst opportunity in the group. Dynasty stash only, undrafted in redraft.

theo johnson.verdict: Best real volume in this range: 74 targets, 17.2% share, 87% snaps — Likely's arrival is the only thing capping him.
theo johnson.report: Johnson nearly doubled his 2024 output (68 to 128 pts) on 74 targets with a 17.2% target share, 16.6% air-yards share, WOPR 0.37 and an 8.3 aDOT — solid volume with acceptable efficiency (1.73 pts/tgt), the safest quadrant in this tier. Ceiling is back-end TE1 if he holds the every-down role at 87% snaps. Floor is a true timeshare with Isaiah Likely now listed ahead of him. Wk17 @DAL is a plus playoff draw.

mason taylor.verdict: Rookie-year 17.2% target share and 81% snaps at TE; efficiency must follow, and Sadiq is a real threat.
mason taylor.report: Taylor posted a rare rookie TE workload: 65 targets, 17.2% target share, WOPR 0.35, 81% snaps, 23 first downs. That is the high-volume/low-efficiency quadrant — 5.8 aDOT and 5.7 yds/tgt mean the points lag the opportunity, and volume like that is only safe if the efficiency climbs. Ceiling is a 90-target year-two leap; floor is Kenyon Sadiq, listed TE1, siphoning the passing snaps. Take him rounds 13-14.

cole kmet.verdict: Still 71% of snaps with 8.8 aDOT and strong 0.84 rec EPA/g, but Loveland owns the target growth.
cole kmet.report: Kmet fell from 120 pts to 79 as Loveland took over, with target share down to 9.6% — low volume, but the efficiency held (7.2 yds/tgt, 0.84 rec EPA/g, 17 first downs on 48 looks). He's the injury-away TE1 in a real offense, which is the ceiling case. Floor is 45-50 points as a blocker with a red-zone target or two. Playoff slate @BUF/GB/DET is not friendly.

noah gray.verdict: The Kelce handcuff with a 113-point season already on file if the room opens up.
noah gray.report: Gray's 2024 (113 pts, 6.7 ppg, 2.31 pts/tgt) shows the ceiling when he plays a real role; 2025 collapsed to 2.3 ppg on an 8.2% target share with -0.49 rec EPA/g — low volume and now poor efficiency, a fade at current usage. He is only draftable as the contingency behind an aging Kelce, and ESPN's 61-point projection prices in some of that. Floor is complete irrelevance in a crowded KC target tree.

austin hooper.verdict: Tiny volume, elite per-target work (10.1 yds/tgt, 1.29 rec EPA/g) — one Pitts absence from matter.
austin hooper.report: Hooper is the classic low-volume/high-efficiency profile: only 26 targets and a 7.1% share, but 2.28 pts/tgt, 9.0 aDOT and a group-best 1.29 rec EPA/g, with 13 first downs on those 26 looks. He also flashed 109 points in 2024 on 59 targets, so the role scales if Pitts misses time. Floor is 30 points at a 50% snap share behind Pitts. Age-31 profile caps the upside.

erick all jr..verdict: Missed 2025 entirely; a healthy return into Cincinnati's passing volume is the only case, and it's a live one.
erick all jr..report: No 2025 data after the lost season, and 2024 was modest (36 pts, 22 targets, 1.63 pts/tgt), so there is no usage baseline to lean on — I'm inferring from the offense rather than the player. Cincinnati throws enough to support a TE, and Gesicki ahead of him is beatable if All is fully recovered. Ceiling is 60-70 targets in a high-volume attack; floor is a rotational blocker or another injury absence.

tommy tremble.verdict: Steady 60% snaps and TD equity, but 9.1% target share and 4.4 aDOT cap the weekly outcome.
tommy tremble.report: Tremble has been remarkably static: 3.3 then 3.8 ppg on 32 and 37 targets, with a 9.1% target share, 5.8% air-yards share and WOPR 0.18 — low volume, mediocre efficiency (6.7 yds/tgt, 10 first downs). That's the fade quadrant unless scores carry him. ESPN's 62-point projection assumes he holds snaps over Ja'Tavion Sanders, which the depth chart disputes. Floor is a blocking role; ceiling needs a Sanders injury.

noah fant.verdict: Snap share collapsed to 38% with -0.91 rec EPA/g behind Juwan Johnson — trend is straight down.
noah fant.report: Fant slid from 64 targets and 104 points in 2024 to 41 targets, 75 points and a 38% snap share, with a 3.3 aDOT and -0.91 rec EPA/g: low volume and genuinely poor efficiency, the fade quadrant. Juwan Johnson is the clear TE1 and the target share (9.2%) is not trending toward change. Ceiling is a short-area PPR floor if Johnson misses games; realistic floor is single-digit weekly relevance.

josh oliver.verdict: Best pts/touch in the group (3.67) on 19 targets — pure TD variance behind Hockenson, and dinged up.
josh oliver.report: Oliver converts what he gets: 2.89 pts/tgt, 3.67 pts/touch, 0.88 rec EPA/g on a 6.5% target share and 46% snaps — low volume, excellent efficiency, but that efficiency is TD-driven on 19 targets and not repeatable at scale. Hockenson is entrenched, so the volume never arrives absent injury, and Oliver himself is listed Questionable. Floor is 20-25 points; ceiling requires a Hockenson absence.

tyler higbee.verdict: 0.9% air-yards share at age 33 behind two younger TEs — the role is already gone.
tyler higbee.report: Higbee's 71 points came on 36 targets with an 11.0% share but a 0.9% air-yards share and 3.3 aDOT — he is a checkdown/red-zone body, not a receiving asset, and the 55% snap share over 10 games shows the workload eroding. Low volume with efficiency that is entirely leverage-dependent (1.97 pts/tgt). Terrance Ferguson and Parkinson are ahead of him now. ESPN's 38-point projection is the honest read.

elijah higgins.verdict: 17 games of availability but a 6.7% target share behind McBride — nothing to unlock.
elijah higgins.report: Higgins played all 17 games at a 43% snap share with 37 targets, 6.7% target share and WOPR 0.12: low volume, roughly neutral efficiency (8.1 yds/tgt, 0.08 rec EPA/g). Trey McBride absorbs essentially every meaningful TE target in Arizona, so the path to relevance is injury-only. Ceiling is a 45-target season if McBride misses time; floor is the 2.9 ppg he posted in 2024. Late wk14 bye is a minor plus.

will kacmarek.verdict: Zero data, but Miami's TE room is the emptiest in the league — Dulcich is beatable.
will kacmarek.report: No NFL usage to grade, so this is an opportunity bet: the only body ahead of him is Greg Dulcich, who has never held a full-time role, and the rest of the room (Sims, Turner, Traore) is replacement level. That is a genuine opening rather than hype. Ceiling is 55-60 targets if he wins the job out of camp; floor is inactive. Final-round or waiver-stash price only — I'd take him after pick 170.

eli raridon.verdict: Rookie behind an aging Hunter Henry; a real long-term role, probably not a 2026 one.
eli raridon.report: No college-to-pro usage data here, so I'm inferring from the depth chart: Hunter Henry is the incumbent but the room behind him (Hill, Westover, Dippre) offers no receiving competition, so Raridon is next in line rather than buried. Ceiling is a mid-season role takeover in an improving offense; floor is 15-20 snaps a game as a blocker. Playoff slate @KC/@NYJ/DEN is unhelpful. Not worth a pick before the final round.

charlie kolar.verdict: Fine per-target work (9.5 yds/tgt) but TE3 behind Gadsden and Njoku — the targets aren't there.
charlie kolar.report: Kolar's 15 targets produced 2.41 pts/tgt and 3.62 pts/touch with 9 first downs — low volume, strong efficiency, the profile that only matters with opportunity, and there is none: Oronde Gadsden and David Njoku are both ahead of him and both healthier bets for the passing snaps. His 40% snap share is blocking-driven. Floor is near zero fantasy relevance; ceiling needs two injuries.

mitchell evans.verdict: Year-two Panther with a 37% snap share, listed third and Questionable — too many bodies ahead.
mitchell evans.report: Evans handled 25 targets as a rookie (6.4% share, WOPR 0.12, 2.41 pts/touch) at a 37% snap share, which is respectable groundwork but not a role. Low volume with middling efficiency (3.6 aDOT, 0.23 rec EPA/g) leaves him dependent on both Ja'Tavion Sanders and Tremble losing snaps. The Questionable tag adds risk to an already thin projection. Ceiling is 45 targets; floor is a healthy scratch week.

cade stover.verdict: 1.24 pts/touch on 16 targets with a 1.9 aDOT — worst efficiency in the group behind Schultz.
cade stover.report: Stover regressed from 34 points to 20, playing just 6 games of meaningful usage at a 44% snap share; the 9.3% target share is misleading on that sample given a 1.9 aDOT and 1.24 pts/touch. Low volume plus poor efficiency is the fade quadrant, and Dalton Schultz plus Marlin Klein sit ahead of him. Even the four carries produced -0.71 rush EPA/g. There is no realistic path to weekly usability.

drew sample.verdict: A -0.3 aDOT and 0.1% air-yards share: he is a lineman who catches screens.
drew sample.report: Sample's profile is about as inert as a TE's can be — 4.9% target share, WOPR 0.07, 0.1% air-yards share, negative aDOT, 5 first downs on 20 targets. Low volume, low efficiency, and he is now TE3 behind Gesicki and a returning Erick All. Two straight seasons at roughly 2.0 ppg establish the trend clearly. Only a multi-injury scenario in Cincinnati makes him startable, and even then the aDOT caps it.

john bates.verdict: 51% snaps are all blocking — 16 targets and a 3.0 aDOT behind Okonkwo.
john bates.report: Bates improved from 14 to 27 points, which tells you the baseline. A 6.8% target share on 10 games, 2.9% air-yards share and 3.0 aDOT is low volume with efficiency (0.78 rec EPA/g) earned on nothing; Chig Okonkwo is the clear receiving TE with Sinnott also in the room. Floor is functionally zero fantasy value. Ceiling is a two-TD flukey stretch. Do not draft in a 12-team league.

tanner hudson.verdict: 15% snap share as the fifth Bengals TE — decent per-target rate on a role that no longer exists.
tanner hudson.report: Hudson's 24 targets at 1.99 pts/tgt and 7.0 yds/tgt are fine per opportunity, but a 15% snap share over 15 games is the tell: he is TE5 behind Gesicki, All, Sample and Endries. Low volume with average efficiency and no snap base is the clearest fade shape in the group. Ceiling is a 40-target season only if Cincinnati's room is decimated; floor is being cut in camp.

max klare.verdict: Rookie listed fifth in a five-deep Rams room with a 10-point projection — undraftable in redraft.
max klare.report: No NFL data, and the depth chart is the whole story: Ferguson, Parkinson, Higbee and Allen all sit ahead of him, and ESPN's 10-point projection reflects an expected inactive or special-teams role. Any inference has to come from opportunity, and there is none in 2026. Ceiling requires multiple injuries plus a Ferguson stumble; floor is zero. Dynasty consideration only, not a redraft pick.

daniel bellinger.verdict: Best backup-TE profile here: real 9.4 aDOT role, 1.74 rec EPA/g, one Helm absence from streamer status.
daniel bellinger.report: Bellinger more than doubled his 2024 output (1.6 to 3.5 PPG) on a genuine downfield role: 6.3% target share, 6.6% air-yards share, WOPR 0.14, aDOT 9.4 and a group-best 1.74 receiving EPA/g with 14 first downs. That's the low-volume/strong-efficiency quadrant — the breakout quadrant if opportunity arrives. Gunnar Helm caps the floor at ~40 points; a Helm miss with 50% baseline snaps makes him a bye-week TE1. Wk17 PIT is a tough finish.

luke musgrave.verdict: Highest target share and WOPR in the group, but PUP and Tucker Kraft stand between him and any of it.
luke musgrave.report: Musgrave's 8.5% target share, 7.0% air-yards share and 0.18 WOPR at an 8.6 aDOT lead this tier, and 0.7 to 2.9 PPG is the right trend line. Low volume with respectable efficiency — a breakout profile waiting on snaps, since 40% snap share is the ceiling behind Tucker Kraft. The PUP designation is the real problem: floor includes missing a month or losing the TE2 job to Whyle. Only worth a final-round dart in TE-premium or as a Kraft handcuff.

jackson hawes.verdict: Elite per-target efficiency (2.77 pts/tgt, 1.14 EPA/g) on tiny volume, buried behind Kincaid and Knox.
jackson hawes.report: Hawes posted the best efficiency line in the group as a rookie: 2.77 points and 9.8 yards per target, 1.14 receiving EPA/g and 13 first downs on only 19 looks, with a 44% snap share as a blocker-first TE3. Classic low-volume/high-efficiency quadrant, but Buffalo's room has Kincaid and Knox ahead and the target share (5.7%) never scaled. Floor is 40 points of blocking snaps; ceiling requires two injuries. Wk16 @DEN and wk17 @MIA are neutral.

adam trautman.verdict: 57% snap share is real, but a 4.6 aDOT and 4.8% target share behind Engram cap him as a blocker.
adam trautman.report: Two straight seasons at ~2.7 PPG with nearly identical 1.98/1.99 points per target says the role is fixed: heavy in-line snaps (57%), tiny receiving share (4.8% targets, 3.4% air yards, WOPR 0.10) at a 4.6 aDOT. High snaps with poor receiving efficiency-per-opportunity is a warning that the volume isn't fantasy volume. Evan Engram owns the routes; an Engram injury plus Denver's red-zone usage is the only path to relevance. Streamer only in deep TE-premium.

davis allen.verdict: Group-leading 3.7 PPG, but the Rams added Ferguson and Klare — he's TE4 now and the volume is gone.
davis allen.report: Allen led this group in raw scoring (63 points, 3.7 PPG) on 33 targets and a 50% snap share, but the shape is grim: 3.9 aDOT, 2.7% air-yards share, WOPR 0.11 — checkdown and goal-line volume, not a route role. High-ish volume with weak efficiency is exactly the profile that loses snaps, and Terrance Ferguson, Parkinson and Higbee all sit ahead of him now. The 2025 line is stale evidence; treat him as a TD-dependent dart.

brock wright.verdict: 8.8% target share is deceiving at a 1.0 aDOT; pure LaPorta insurance in a good Detroit offense.
brock wright.report: Wright's 8.8% target share over eight games looks strong until you see the 1.0 aDOT, 1.3% air-yards share and -0.24 receiving EPA/g — dump-offs and blocking, the high-snap/poor-efficiency warning quadrant. The 58% snap share is the asset: if Sam LaPorta misses time, Wright inherits a top-five scoring offense and could stream. Two years pinned at ~2.1-2.2 PPG is the honest baseline. Early wk6 bye helps roster flexibility.

jeremy ruckert.verdict: Career-best 47 points, but a 3.5 aDOT and a Sadiq/Taylor room ahead of him leave no path.
jeremy ruckert.report: Ruckert improved to 2.8 PPG with a 7.3% target share, yet the 2.9% air-yards share and 3.5 aDOT show pure safety-valve work — low volume, mediocre efficiency (1.62 pts/tgt), which is the fade quadrant. He was efficient enough to hold a 47% snap share, so the floor isn't zero. The problem is depth chart: Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor both project ahead, and the Jets should be more spread out. Last-pick flier at best.

ben sinnott.verdict: Nice 6.8% target share and 8.2 aDOT in nine games, but third in a room with Okonkwo and Bates.
ben sinnott.report: Sinnott doubled his rookie output and flashed a usable route profile — 6.8% target share, 6.3% air-yards share, 0.15 WOPR, 8.2 aDOT on limited snaps (36%). Low volume with acceptable efficiency (2.18 pts/tgt) makes him a name to watch, but Chig Okonkwo is the pass-catcher and Bates the blocker, leaving him a rotational third. Floor is under 30 points; ceiling needs an Okonkwo absence. Not draftable in 12-team formats.

luke schoonmaker.verdict: Went backwards in 2025 (1.6 PPG, 1.18 pts/tgt) and Dallas added Trigg — clear fade.
luke schoonmaker.report: Schoonmaker's arrow points down: 3.4 PPG on 36 targets in 2024 fell to 1.6 PPG on 23 targets, with a 33% snap share, 4.6% target share and a poor 1.18 points/5.7 yards per target. Low volume plus poor efficiency is the fade quadrant, and Jake Ferguson plus Michael Trigg push him to TE3. The one positive is a 7.2 aDOT suggesting he still runs real routes. Nothing here at any price in redraft.

mo alie-cox.verdict: Nine-year blocker with -0.08 EPA/g and four first downs, stuck behind Tyler Warren. Pass.
mo alie-cox.report: Two nearly identical seasons around 1.8 PPG with 5.8 yards per target and negative receiving EPA define the ceiling. A 5.6% target share at a 4.7 aDOT with only four first downs is the low-volume/poor-efficiency quadrant, and Tyler Warren commands the Colts' TE targets while Mallory takes the rest. Age and role both point down. Red-zone size gives him occasional TD equity — that's it.

nate adkins.verdict: Third Denver TE behind Engram and Trautman; efficiency collapsed to -0.10 EPA/g on 11 targets.
nate adkins.report: Adkins fell from 2.6 PPG to 1.0 PPG as his snap share dropped to 33% over nine games, with a 4.9% target share, 3.2 aDOT and negative receiving EPA. That's low volume plus deteriorating efficiency — the fade quadrant. He sits behind both Engram and Trautman, so even an injury ahead of him only makes him the second option. His 2024 2.90 points-per-target flash was TD noise on 15 targets.

ben sims.verdict: Miami's TE room is the weakest in the league; 12.2 aDOT flash on three games is a lottery ticket.
ben sims.report: Sims has almost no sample — three games, 13% snap share — but the shape is intriguing: 8.3% target share, 13.5% air-yards share, 0.22 WOPR and a 12.2 aDOT, the only vertical usage in this group. Low volume with real per-snap juice is the breakout quadrant, and Greg Dulcich and Will Kacmarek are not entrenched starters. Floor is a healthy scratch; this is a final-pick dart in deep TE-premium leagues only, round 16-plus.

nate boerkircher.verdict: Rookie TE2 with zero pro sample behind an established Brenton Strange — dynasty name, not redraft.
nate boerkircher.report: No NFL usage data exists, so the inference has to come from depth chart and role: Jacksonville just committed to Brenton Strange as the every-down TE, with Hunter Long and Koziol also in the room. Even a strong camp likely yields a blocking rotation and single-digit targets. The ceiling case is a Strange injury opening 60%-plus snaps in a modern passing offense; the floor is inactive. Ignore in 12-team redraft.

joe royer.verdict: Rookie behind Harold Fannin in a run-leaning Cleveland offense; no data, no path, no draft capital case.
joe royer.report: No 2024 or 2025 sample, so this is pure projection off depth chart: Harold Fannin is the entrenched pass-catching TE and Whiteheart/Stoll fill the blocking snaps. Cleveland's passing volume and QB situation cap even the injury-driven ceiling. Without any efficiency signal to lean on, the safest inference is a rotational blocker with fewer than 20 targets. Waiver-wire name at best.

payne durham.verdict: Target share cratered to 1.7% with a 0.03 WOPR; now TE4 in Tampa behind Otton and Sharp.
payne durham.report: Durham's 2024 flash (2.46 pts/tgt on 14 targets) was small-sample TD luck, and 2025 wiped it out: 1.7% target share, 1.3% air-yards share, 0.03 WOPR, one first down over eight games despite a 32% snap share. Low volume and negative EPA is the fade quadrant. Cade Otton runs the routes and Bauer Sharp has jumped him for the TE2 blocking snaps. No redraft case.

foster moreau.verdict: 2024's 103-point season is dead data: 1.0 aDOT, -0.53 EPA/g, and TE4 on a new team behind Schultz.
foster moreau.report: Moreau scored 103 points at 6.1 PPG in 2024 on 43 targets, then fell to 13 points on 10 targets with a 1.0 aDOT, 1.0% air-yards share and -0.53 receiving EPA/g in seven games. That collapse plus a move to Houston, where Dalton Schultz, Klein and Stover all sit ahead of him, is the low-volume/poor-efficiency fade quadrant. Ignore the 2024 line; the role that produced it no longer exists.

luke farrell.verdict: Pure blocker behind George Kittle: 3.2% target share, 2.9 aDOT, 10 projected points.
luke farrell.report: Farrell's job is sealing the edge — 35% snap share with a 3.2% target share, 1.4% air-yards share and 0.06 WOPR at a 2.9 aDOT. The 2.11 points per target is noise on 14 looks. George Kittle plus Jake Tonges own every meaningful route, and San Francisco's playoff slate (@LAC, @KC, PHI) is brutal anyway. Lowest projection in the group for a reason; zero redraft relevance.

durham smythe.verdict: 25% snaps, 0.05 WOPR, one first down — a veteran blocker stashed behind Mark Andrews.
durham smythe.report: Smythe's numbers are the weakest here on both axes: 2.9% target share, 0.9% air-yards share, 0.05 WOPR, -0.04 receiving EPA/g and a single first down over seven games, on top of a 0.84 points-per-target 2024. That is the low-volume, poor-efficiency fade quadrant with no ambiguity. Mark Andrews owns the receiving work and Hibner is the developmental piece. Nothing to draft, in any format or league size.

josh allen.verdict: The only QB pairing elite pass EPA with a 100-carry rushing floor; nothing else in the pool is this safe.
josh allen.report: High volume + high efficiency, the expensive safe quadrant: 4.46 pass EPA/g, +2.9 CPOE, 2.42 rush EPA/g on 112 carries and 92% snaps. 21.4 and 22.3 PPG in back-to-back full seasons with no meaningful backup (Buechele, K. Allen) behind him. Floor is a healthy top-5 finish; ceiling is overall QB1 again. Wk15 CHI, wk16 @DEN, wk17 @MIA is a workable playoff run off a Week 7 bye.

drake maye.verdict: Best efficiency profile in the league last year (+12.2 CPOE, 9.72 pass EPA/g) plus 103 carries, at a discount ADP.
drake maye.report: 2025 was a genuine leap: 20.7 PPG on a tiny 5.2 weekly stdev, 96% snaps, 9.72 pass EPA/g and +12.2 CPOE — high volume, elite efficiency. Adding 103 carries gives him a rushing floor 2024 Maye (10.4 PPG) lacked. Regression on CPOE is likely, so the floor is low-QB1; the ceiling is a top-3 season. No competition (DeVito, Morton). Playoffs @KC, @NYJ, DEN are the one real drag at ADP 48.

lamar jackson.verdict: 2024's 25.3 PPG is the ceiling case; 2025's 13 games at 1.40 pass EPA/g is the warning you're paying to ignore.
lamar jackson.report: Two very different years: 430 points and 6.0 stdev in 2024, then 13 games and 16.5 PPG in games played in 2025 with pass EPA/g falling from elite to 1.40. Volume is unquestioned (92% snaps, 67 carries in a short year, 3.8 yds before contact) and CPOE stayed +2.9, so the efficiency dip reads as health, not decline. Camp headlines are generic roundups — no signal. Wk15 @PIT, wk16 CLE, wk17 @CIN is a hard finish.

jayden daniels.verdict: Buy the 2024 rushing profile (148 carries, 20.9 PPG), not the seven broken games of 2025.
jayden daniels.report: 2025 is a small, injury-poisoned sample: seven games, -0.83 pass EPA/g, -3.0 CPOE, only 58 carries. 2024 — 356 points, 20.9 PPG, 148 carries at 6.0 YPC — is the true baseline, and designed-run volume is the whole ceiling case. High volume when upright, efficiency unproven post-injury. Mariota is insurance, not a threat. Floor is another lost half-season; ceiling is overall QB1. Playoffs ATL/@MIN/@JAX are fine.

jalen hurts.verdict: Goal-line rushing volume makes him nearly bust-proof, but 4.0 YPC says the points are TD-driven, not efficient.
jalen hurts.report: 105 and 150 carries the last two years at 98% snaps — enormous volume — but 4.0 YPC and 0.7 yards after contact mean the rushing points come from tush-push scores, not explosion. Passing efficiency is solid, not special (2.14 EPA/g, +4.2 CPOE). That's high volume, modest efficiency: the floor is excellent, the ceiling capped near 17-19 PPG unless the pass game spikes. No QB competition. Wk17 @SF is the one tough playoff draw.

joe burrow.verdict: Eight games, but 4.58 pass EPA/g and +4.6 CPOE while healthy; pure passing volume with zero rushing cushion.
joe burrow.report: When he played in 2025 he averaged nearly 17 PPG on an 8-game sample with 4.58 pass EPA/g and +4.6 CPOE, and 2024 was 21.9 PPG. Low rushing volume (14 carries, 0 broken tackles) means every point comes through the air, so an injury or a bad game has no floor underneath it. High passing volume + strong efficiency when available; availability is the entire risk. Wk15 @CAR and wk16 @IND set up a friendly playoff push.

jaxson dart.verdict: Rookie-year 14.2 PPG was almost all legs (2.72 rush EPA/g); the arm has to catch up for the ADP to work.
jaxson dart.report: 86 carries and 2.72 rush EPA/g at 84% snaps gave him a real rushing floor as a rookie, but 0.24 pass EPA/g and -0.6 CPOE are replacement-level throwing. That's decent volume with poor passing efficiency — the profile that improves with time or gets streamed over. ESPN's sleeper call is fair on the year-two/supporting-cast logic, but ADP 74 already prices it, so no sleeper badge. Winston lurks if it goes badly. Wk16 @DET, wk17 @DAL are tough.

trevor lawrence.verdict: 19.9 PPG with 82 carries and 97% snaps, and you get it three rounds after the QBs he outscored.
trevor lawrence.report: 2025 was the healthy version: 338 points, 19.9 PPG, 8.5 stdev, 2.26 pass EPA/g and 1.52 rush EPA/g on 82 carries across all 17 games. CPOE of -1.3 says the accuracy is average, so this is a volume-and-legs profile rather than an efficiency one — solid volume, middling efficiency. Floor is a low-end QB1 who never misses; ceiling is a top-6 year if the TD rate climbs. No backup threat behind him at all. ADP 94 is the value.

dak prescott.verdict: 6.66 pass EPA/g over a full 17 games; the rushing zero (-0.55 EPA/g) is what caps him at QB10-ish.
dak prescott.report: Bounced back from 2024's injury year to 314 points, 18.5 PPG, 8.0 stdev, 95% snaps and an excellent 6.66 pass EPA/g. All of it comes through the air — 53 carries, 3.3 YPC, negative rush EPA — so he's high passing volume with good efficiency but no floor-raising legs. Floor is a steady QB12; ceiling top-6 if the Dallas passing volume stays elite. His camp comments are noise. Wk14 bye then @LAR/JAX/NYG is a clean playoff path.

bo nix.verdict: Two straight 17-19 PPG seasons at 100% snaps with 80+ carries — boring, durable, cheap.
bo nix.report: 305 and 317 points in his two seasons with 83 and 92 carries and a perfect 100% snap share; the weekly stdev (8.1) is modest. But -1.1 CPOE and 3.72 pass EPA/g say the efficiency is fine-not-good, and only 0.7 yards after contact means the rushing is scheme, not tackle-breaking. High volume, average efficiency — the QB12 floor is real, the top-5 ceiling is not obvious. Wk16 BUF is a rough playoff week.

brock purdy.verdict: 7.01 pass EPA/g and +7.7 CPOE in nine games — elite per-dropback play at a QB2 price if he stays upright.
brock purdy.report: Only nine games in 2025, but the rate stats are outstanding: 7.01 pass EPA/g, +7.7 CPOE, 1.80 rush EPA/g, 98% snaps. Low volume, strong efficiency — the classic breakout-with-opportunity quadrant, where the opportunity is simply health. Floor is another half-season and a wasted pick; ceiling is a top-6 QB. Mac Jones is a real backup, which is why the market discounts him. I'd start taking him in round 9 as a QB1 with an injury hedge; playoffs @LAC/@KC/PHI are brutal.

caleb williams.verdict: 18.7 PPG and rising, but -3.4 CPOE says the passing efficiency hasn't arrived; the legs carry him.
caleb williams.report: Year-two jump to 318 points and 18.7 PPG on 99% snaps with 77 carries at 5.0 YPC and five broken tackles. The warning is -3.4 CPOE and only 2.48 pass EPA/g — high volume with below-average accuracy, the quadrant where the numbers hold up only if the rushing and Ben Johnson's scheme keep propping them. Floor is a low QB1 given the mobility; ceiling top-5 if the accuracy normalizes. Playoffs @BUF/GB/DET are unfriendly.

matthew stafford.verdict: 8.85 pass EPA/g in a full 17-game season, but a 38-year-old pocket statue with literally zero rushing points.
matthew stafford.report: 350 points and 20.6 PPG on a tiny 6.8 stdev, with 8.85 pass EPA/g at 99% snaps — elite passing efficiency on elite passing volume. The catch: 29 carries producing negative rush EPA, so there is no non-passing floor, and at his age the injury/decline tail is fatter than the numbers suggest. Floor is a mid-QB2 or a missed month; ceiling is a repeat top-5. ADP 79 is a fair price, not a bargain, given the age curve.

justin herbert.verdict: Metronomic 16.8-16.9 PPG two years running with 80+ carries; a QB2 price for a floor you can start every week.
justin herbert.report: 287 and 285 points in consecutive seasons — 97% snaps, 83 carries, 6.0 YPC, 4.9 yards before contact and 0.99 rush EPA/g. Passing efficiency is only average (1.01 pass EPA/g, +1.6 CPOE), so this is a high-volume, mid-efficiency profile whose ceiling depends on a TD spike, not on hidden usage. Floor is one of the safest in the pool; ceiling is roughly QB7. Wk15 SF, wk16 @MIA, wk17 KC is a demanding finish at ADP 107.

patrick mahomes.verdict: Still 4.87 pass EPA/g and 64 carries, but 16.8 PPG twice running and a Questionable tag entering camp.
patrick mahomes.report: Two straight seasons at 16.8/16.6 PPG is now a trend, not a blip; CPOE of 0.1 says he is no longer separating on accuracy. The rushing is quietly real (64 carries, 6.6 YPC, 2.08 rush EPA/g) and props up the floor. The live fact is the Questionable designation, with Graziano suggesting a Week 1 return — treat that as the freshest signal and a discount, not a disqualifier. Fields sits behind him if it lingers. High volume, good-not-elite efficiency at a QB2 price.

jared goff.verdict: 6.26 pass EPA/g and 17 starts of 17.5 PPG; a genuinely useful streamer with a hard ceiling and no legs.
jared goff.report: Full-season availability (99% snaps, 17 games), 297 points, +2.9 CPOE and 6.26 pass EPA/g — high passing volume with strong efficiency. But 19 carries and -0.85 rush EPA/g means the ceiling is entirely TD-rate dependent, and 2024's 324 points is about the top of the range. Floor is a matchup-based QB2; ceiling is a QB8 season. Wk15 @MIN and wk17 @CHI are division road games in the fantasy playoffs. At ADP 141 he is fine, not exciting.

tyler shough.verdict: Six straight 17+ games to close his rookie year and no competition left — a round-13 QB1 lottery ticket.
tyler shough.report: Season line (9.3 PPG) hides the arc: he was QB12 in PPG from Week 9 and closed with six straight 17+ efforts, and the job is now uncontested with Rattler and Wilson behind him. Full-year rate stats are still poor (0.19 pass EPA/g, -2.7 CPOE, 83% snaps), so this is low-volume, unproven-efficiency — the bet is on the second-half version being real. Sleeper: 45 carries give a rushing floor, and playoffs @TB/ARI/@ATL are soft. Start taking him round 13.

kyler murray.verdict: New team, 78-carry rushing history and a 17.5 PPG season two years back — free upside at ADP 149 if he holds the job.
kyler murray.report: 2025 was five games and 78 points; 2024 was 297 points on 78 carries at 7.3 YPC. In the small 2025 sample the efficiency held up (1.14 pass EPA/g, 0.82 rush EPA/g, 99% snaps), so the collapse reads as availability, not talent. The risk is stark: J.J. McCarthy is the QB2 in Minnesota, so a slow start could end the job — that's the depth-chart competition no other starter here faces. Sleeper at round 12-13 purely on the rushing ceiling; floor is a cut in October.

daniel jones.verdict: 17.4 PPG in the 13 games he played with 5.02 pass EPA/g and +2.6 CPOE — the cheapest real starter on the board.
daniel jones.report: The 13.3 season PPG is a games-played artifact; in games he actually started it was ~17.4, on 5.02 pass EPA/g, +2.6 CPOE and 1.24 rush EPA/g across 45 carries. Low volume (91% snaps, 13 games) with clearly above-average efficiency is the breakout quadrant — he only needs 17 starts. Richardson and Leonard behind him are a genuine leash risk if he slumps. Sleeper worth a round-14 stab as a QB2 with weekly startable range; wk13 bye is late but manageable.

baker mayfield.verdict: Pass EPA/g fell to 0.04 with -2.5 CPOE; the 2024 21.5 PPG version isn't coming back on this efficiency.
baker mayfield.report: Volume is unchanged (97% snaps, 17 games, 55 carries with 7 broken tackles and 2.10 rush EPA/g), but the throwing collapsed from 2024's 366-point season to 0.04 pass EPA/g and -2.5 CPOE — high volume with poor efficiency, the quadrant where the job itself eventually gets questioned. The legs keep the floor respectable near 16 PPG. Ceiling requires a full accuracy rebound. Playoffs NO/@ATL/LAR are fine. Off-field noise in the news is not a data point.

jordan love.verdict: Best combination of volume and efficiency in this pool: 94% snaps, 7.37 pass EPA/g, and a growing rush floor.
jordan love.report: High volume + good efficiency, the safe quadrant here: 94% snap share, 7.37 pass EPA/g, +5.0 CPOE and 47 carries in 2025 (up from 25) that added a real rushing floor to identical 13.8 PPG seasons. Ceiling is a mid-QB1 finish if the legs stay involved and the receiver room stays healthy. Floor is the two missed games repeating with 8.4 weekly stdev. No competition — Tyrod Taylor and Kyle McCord are not threats.

c.j. stroud.verdict: Positive EPA, 91% snaps and rising rush value; the three missed games are the only thing capping the price.
c.j. stroud.report: Volume is secure (91% snaps, QB1 with Davis Mills behind him) and efficiency is solidly positive: 3.40 pass EPA/g, 1.07 rush EPA/g on 48 carries. PPG dipped 13.0 to 12.3 but weekly stdev jumped to 8.0, meaning more boom weeks — that is the ceiling case if the Texans' pass game stabilizes. Floor is another 14-game season. Playoff slate @PHI and @GB in Weeks 16-17 is a genuine negative for a streamer.

sam darnold.verdict: Bankable 17-game volume and +6.2 CPOE, but the 2024 spike (18.1 PPG) is gone and won't return.
sam darnold.report: High volume, average-plus efficiency: 96% snaps across all 17 games, 4.39 pass EPA/g and +6.2 CPOE, but rush EPA was -0.76 on 2.7 ypc, so there is no legs cushion. The drop from 308 points to 235 is the honest baseline, not bad luck. Ceiling is a return toward 280 if Seattle's play-action volume climbs; floor is 13-ish PPG with zero rushing. Drew Lock is no threat. Week 15 @PHI hurts.

bryce young.verdict: 97% snaps, 54 carries and a year-over-year PPG climb — cheap volume with a rushing floor.
bryce young.report: High volume, still-mediocre efficiency (-1.37 pass EPA/g, +1.3 CPOE), but the trend is up: 11.5 to 12.8 PPG with 54 carries and 0.26 rush EPA/g providing weekly floor. No competition at all — Kenny Pickett is the only body behind him. Ceiling is a genuine QB1 stretch if the young receiver group takes a step; floor is 11 PPG and matchup-dependent streaming. Week 17 vs SEA and Week 15 vs CIN are startable spots.

cam ward.verdict: Full 17-game rookie volume with 39 carries, but -6.42 pass EPA/g says the efficiency has to arrive.
cam ward.report: High volume, poor efficiency — the warning quadrant, though for a rookie it reads as development runway rather than a job at risk (95% snaps, Will Levis and Trubisky behind him). 11.0 PPG with 5.2 stdev was steady but low-ceiling; 0.50 rush EPA/g and 3 broken tackles hint at a rushing floor that can grow. Ceiling is a Year 2 leap into low-end QB1 range; floor is another 11 PPG streamer year.

malik willis.verdict: Only 4 games of data, but MIA's named QB1 with 5.6 ypc rushing — the cheapest real upside in the group.
malik willis.report: Low volume, elite small-sample efficiency (25.0 CPOE, 7.02 pass EPA/g over 4 games, 5.6 ypc) — the breakout quadrant that only needs snaps, and he now has them as Miami's QB1 over Quinn Ewers. Ceiling is a 280-point dual-threat season if he holds the job through camp; floor is a benching by October, which is why the range is enormous. Camp headline is generic, no signal. Playoffs @GB/LAC/BUF are rough. Sleeper: take him round 13 as a QB2 lottery ticket.

geno smith.verdict: New team and better weapons, but -4.86 EPA/g and a 15.6-to-10.2 PPG collapse make the sleeper call a stretch.
geno smith.report: High volume (96% snaps), poor efficiency — the quadrant where the job itself is at risk, and at 13 years in that is a real concern with Cade Klubnik behind him. RotoWire's sleeper call cites the better line and pass catchers, which is fair context, but the underlying data (-4.86 pass EPA/g, 2.7 ypc, PPG halved) contradicts it, so I am not badging him. Ceiling is a bounce to 2024's 15.6 PPG; floor is a midseason benching.

aaron rodgers.verdict: Steady 96% snaps and 13.4 PPG, but zero rushing equity and age make every projection a ceiling.
aaron rodgers.report: High volume, mildly positive efficiency (1.68 pass EPA/g, -0.4 CPOE) with no legs at all — 21 carries, -0.18 rush EPA/g, 0.1 yards after contact. That caps him as a pure passing-volume streamer whose 15.1-to-13.4 PPG slide is the trend line to project forward. Ceiling is 250 if Pittsburgh's pass rate climbs; floor is a couple of missed games and a Rudolph cameo. Week 17 @TEN is a fine matchup.

jacoby brissett.verdict: Emergency-starter volume produced 13.4 PPG, but -3.6 CPOE and rookie Carson Beck cap the runway.
jacoby brissett.report: Middling volume (86% snaps, 14 games) with below-average efficiency: -0.23 pass EPA/g and -3.6 CPOE, though 0.53 rush EPA/g and 3.0 yards before contact per carry added sneaky points. The 13.4 PPG is close to his real level but was propped up by high-stdev shootout weeks (9.1). Ceiling is a repeat 200-plus season if he keeps the job wire-to-wire; floor is Carson Beck taking over by midseason. QB2 only.

fernando mendoza.verdict: Rookie named QB1 over Cousins and O'Connell — no data, but the job is the asset at this price.
fernando mendoza.report: No usage data exists, so I am inferring from the depth chart alone: he is the listed starter with a fading Kirk Cousins (-4.5 CPOE, 6.1 PPG) and O'Connell behind, meaning full-season volume is plausible from Week 1. Ceiling is a 250-plus dual-threat rookie year; floor is early-season struggles and a Cousins reinsertion. Camp headline is a generic roundup, no signal. Sleeper worth a round-14 dart in superflex or deep QB leagues.

deshaun watson.verdict: Listed QB1 in Cleveland but coming off a lost season and 4.5 PPG in his last action — pure speculation.
deshaun watson.report: Low volume and poor efficiency in every recent sample: 77 points across 2024 and no 2025 data at all, with Shedeur Sanders, Taylen Green and Dillon Gabriel all behind him and pushing. The 124-point projection already assumes a partial season. Ceiling is roughly 220 if he somehow holds the job for 15 games with the 4.8-ypc rushing intact; floor is being benched before Halloween. Not draftable outside superflex.

tua tagovailoa.verdict: Back issue in camp, a new team, and Penix behind him — 9.5 PPG doesn't survive any of that.
tua tagovailoa.report: High snap share (95%) with weak efficiency and no rushing at all: -0.53 rush EPA/g, 2.1 ypc, 20 carries, so 9.5 PPG is essentially his passing-only output. The back injury is the freshest signal — he says it is precautionary, but he is held out in late July with Michael Penix Jr. on the roster, which is a live job threat. Ceiling is 210 if he starts 16 and Atlanta throws; floor is a backup role by September.

michael penix jr..verdict: Tua's camp back issue is a checkable opening; Penix's 0.57 EPA/g and legs make him the cheaper half of the ATL job.
michael penix jr..report: Low volume, roughly neutral efficiency across 9 games — 0.57 pass EPA/g and a healthy 0.79 rush EPA/g on limited work, which is the breakout quadrant profile of a player who only needs snaps. The opening is concrete: Tua is being held out in late July with a back issue and is listed Questionable. Ceiling is a 230-plus full-season ATL job; floor is 40 points in relief. Sleeper worth a final-round stash — take him ahead of Tua at the same ADP.

shedeur sanders.verdict: Rushing efficiency flashed (8.0 ypc, 1.22 rush EPA/g) but -7.41 pass EPA/g and QB2 status kill the floor.
shedeur sanders.report: Low volume with split efficiency: excellent on the ground (8.0 ypc, 5.5 yards before contact, 1.22 rush EPA/g) and genuinely bad through the air (-7.41 pass EPA/g, -6.6 CPOE) over 8 starts. He sits behind Watson with Green and Gabriel also in the room, so the path is a Watson injury, not a camp win. Ceiling is 220 if he starts 12-plus and the legs carry him; floor is a clipboard year. Contingency stash only.

kirk cousins.verdict: Backup to a rookie, zero mobility, -4.5 CPOE — nothing here except an injury-contingent bridge role.
kirk cousins.report: Low volume, poor efficiency: 86% snaps in only 10 games, -0.09 pass EPA/g, -4.5 CPOE, and 0.5 ypc rushing with 0.2 yards before contact, which is as immobile as this list gets. PPG has fallen 10.4 to 6.1 in two years. Ceiling is roughly 150 if Mendoza struggles and he retakes the job for half the year; floor is zero relevant weeks. Not a draft pick in a 12-team single-QB league.

j.j. mccarthy.verdict: 5 broken tackles and 0.68 rush EPA/g are real, but -5.41 pass EPA/g behind an entrenched starter is unplayable.
j.j. mccarthy.report: Low volume with poor passing efficiency (-5.41 pass EPA/g, -4.8 CPOE over 10 games) and genuinely good rushing markers (37 carries, 4.9 ypc, 5 broken tackles) — the legs are the only reason to care. The depth chart lists him as QB2, so weekly volume is not coming without an injury ahead of him. Ceiling is 170 in a half-season takeover; floor is a handful of garbage weeks. Deep-superflex stash.

carson beck.verdict: Rookie QB2 behind Brissett with no data — a dynasty name, not a 2026 fantasy asset.
carson beck.report: No NFL usage data at all, so I am inferring purely from depth chart: he sits behind Jacoby Brissett with Minshew and Slovis also present, and Brissett was competent enough (13.4 PPG) to hold the job into the season. Ceiling is a second-half takeover worth roughly 130 points; floor is a full redshirt. The 29-point projection is honest. Leave him on the wire in redraft.

justin fields.verdict: Elite rushing profile (71 carries, 5.4 ypc, 0.97 rush EPA/g) trapped behind Patrick Mahomes.
justin fields.report: Low volume, split efficiency: the rushing is genuinely valuable (5.4 ypc, 4.4 yards before contact, 3 broken tackles, 0.97 rush EPA/g) while the passing is not (-2.49 EPA/g, -6.9 CPOE). None of it matters as Mahomes' backup — the 11-point projection reflects zero expected snaps. Ceiling only exists in a Mahomes-injury world where his legs make him a fringe QB1; floor is nothing. Not draftable.

joe flacco.verdict: Burrow's backup with -3.14 EPA/g and no mobility; the 11-point projection is the whole story.
joe flacco.report: Low volume, poor efficiency: 78% snaps across 13 games produced 8.6 PPG with -3.14 pass EPA/g and 1.7 ypc, and even that came in a starter-by-necessity role. Behind Joe Burrow he projects for essentially no snaps. Ceiling is a 100-point relief stint with Cincinnati's weapons inflating the passing lines; floor is zero. Ignore in all single-QB formats.

mac jones.verdict: Best backup efficiency here (4.06 EPA/g, +4.0 CPOE) but Purdy blocks every snap that matters.
mac jones.report: Low volume with surprisingly strong efficiency — 4.06 pass EPA/g and +4.0 CPOE over 11 games, the low-volume/high-efficiency quadrant — but the opportunity simply is not there behind Brock Purdy. No rushing equity either (-0.48 rush EPA/g, 1.7 ypc). Ceiling is roughly 110 in a multi-week fill-in with San Francisco's scheme; floor is zero. Waiver-wire watch if Purdy misses time, not a draft pick.

jameis winston.verdict: Best contingent starter on this board: proven 12-start volume behind a second-year QB, but only a superflex dart.
jameis winston.report: Quadrant: low volume, volatile efficiency. 2024 gave 131 points on a full slate of fill-in work; 2025 was 3 appearances (68% snap share when in) with a strong +5.13 pass EPA/g but a -12.1 CPOE that screams boom/bust. If Jaxson Dart misses four-plus weeks, Winston is an instant streamer with 20-point spike games. Floor is zero snaps behind an entrenched No. 1. Playoff draw (CLE, @DET, @DAL) is unfriendly.

marcus mariota.verdict: Most recently productive backup here — 126 points and 50 carries as a fill-in behind an injury-prone starter.
marcus mariota.report: Quadrant: high volume when playing, roughly league-average efficiency (pass EPA/g -0.39, CPOE +0.5), with real rushing value (50 carries, 5.9 ypc, +0.67 rush EPA/g). He held a 75% snap share across 11 games in 2025 and turned it into ~12 PPG, which is startable. The floor is near zero if Jayden Daniels plays 17. That's the whole bet: Daniels' durability, not Mariota's talent.

ty simpson.verdict: Rookie sitting one snap behind a 38-year-old in a loaded offense — the best pure upside stash at this price.
ty simpson.report: No usage data exists, so I'm inferring from situation: QB2 to Matthew Stafford, whose age and back history make 4-8 missed starts a live outcome, with a receiving corps that would prop up any starter. Quadrant unknown — zero volume, unmeasured efficiency — which is exactly why the price is a last-round lottery. Floor is a clipboard year. Sleeper: in superflex I'd take him in the final round or two (ADP 170); in 1QB leagues he's a waiver watchlist name.

anthony richardson sr..verdict: Elite rushing archetype with no confirmed job — 0 projection is the tell; monitor, don't draft.
anthony richardson sr..report: 2024 was high rushing volume (86 carries, 5.8 ypc, 9.6 PPG) paired with poor passing efficiency — the quadrant where the volume itself gets taken away, and it was. He missed 2025 entirely and has no depth-chart match here, so there is no verified path to snaps. The ceiling if he wins a job anywhere is 200-plus on legs alone. No sleeper badge: a sleeper needs an identified opening, and the ESPN projection of 0 says the field sees none.

jake browning.verdict: Got real snaps in 2025 and was actively bad (-7.68 pass EPA/g); now buried behind Baker Mayfield.
jake browning.report: Quadrant: high volume when in (73% snap share over 5 games) with terrible efficiency — the warning profile, and the volume was duly removed. CPOE +6.0 says he completes passes, but -7.68 pass EPA/g says none of them help. Mayfield is entrenched in Tampa, so the realistic path is emergency-only work. Floor is 17 clipboard weeks; ceiling requires an injury and better play than he showed.

tyson bagent.verdict: Sharp tiny-sample accuracy (+19.7 CPOE) but Caleb Williams isn't giving up snaps.
tyson bagent.report: Quadrant: very low volume (7% snap share over 3 games), strong efficiency on a sample too small to trust — the breakout profile only if opportunity arrives, and there's no sign it will. He has prior starting experience, which raises his floor as a fill-in over the true third-stringers here. Chicago's playoff slate (@BUF, GB, DET) is rough even in the injury scenario. Pure contingency stash.

jarrett stidham.verdict: Veteran QB2 with a 6% snap share behind a durable Bo Nix — no realistic path to fantasy relevance.
jarrett stidham.report: Quadrant: essentially zero volume, unmeasurable efficiency (0.00 pass EPA/g on one appearance), so I'm inferring from role rather than production. Nix has been an every-snap starter, which caps Stidham at emergency duty. He has started NFL games before, so the fill-in floor isn't embarrassing, but nothing in the data suggests startable upside. Draft-day irrelevant; waiver name only.

nick mullens.verdict: Gaudy 26.2 CPOE on 11% of snaps is mop-up noise; Trevor Lawrence blocks everything.
nick mullens.report: Quadrant: low volume (11% snap share over 5 games), eye-catching efficiency (CPOE 26.2, +0.72 pass EPA/g) on a garbage-time sample — I'd weight the sample size over the number. Lawrence's grip on the job is total, so this is a two-start-per-decade profile. Early bye (wk7) and a hard playoff draw (@HOU, @DAL) add nothing. No draft-day case in any format.

tommy devito.verdict: Backup to a franchise QB with 13 points of career-relevant production — bottom-of-board filler.
tommy devito.report: 2024 produced 13 points at 0.8 PPG, which is the low-volume, low-efficiency fade quadrant with nothing to project forward. He sits behind Drake Maye, one of the league's most secure starters, so the opportunity tree has no branches. Floor and ceiling are nearly the same number. The @KC/@NYJ/DEN playoff slate is moot at this usage level.

sam howell.verdict: QB3 in Dallas behind Prescott and Milton — two injuries from relevance, which is not a draft strategy.
sam howell.report: No 2025 data at all, and the depth chart lists him third, so both volume and efficiency inputs are blank; I'm ranking purely on path to snaps, and it's the worst here. Howell has started a full season before, so the talent floor isn't zero, but he'd need Prescott and Joe Milton both to miss time. Late bye (wk14) and a decent wk17 NYG matchup are irrelevant at this role. Do not draft.
